title: Delhi High Court directs Amitabh Bachchan to appear in person to continue personality rights suit
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Delhi High Court has directed veteran Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan to appear personally before it if he wishes to pursue his suit seeking protection of his personality rights and fails to reach a settlement with various entities.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan was granted interim relief in his personality rights case in 2022. High Court asks Amitabh Bachchan to appear in person A bench of Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav issued the direction on Friday after the parties informed the court that although the court in November 2022 had protected Bacchan’s personality rights by granting an ex parte injunction, the parties explored the possibility of an amicable settlement through mediation during the proceedings.

Meanwhile, The parties added that an amicable settlement had been reached with some of the defendants, but the settlement agreement could not be formally signed due to logistical issues on Bachchan’s part. Amitabh Bachchan’s counsel, Dhruv Anand, thus sought additional time to complete the necessary formalities and place the agreement on record.

Notably, Granting time until November 16, the court clarified that if the settlement remained incomplete or failed to materialise, the star must appear personally at the next hearing if he wished to pursue any of the claims or issues raised in the suit.

As per the latest buzz, “Time stands granted. List on 16.11.2026. In the event of non-settlement or incomplete settlement, if the plaintiff wishes to pursue the suit on any of the claims or issues, the plaintiff shall remain personally present on the next date of hearing, enabling the Court to exercise its powers under Order X Rule 2 read with Order V Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and Section 168 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023,” the court shared in the order.

In further updates, In 2022, Amitabh Bachchan had filed a suit seeking protection of his personality rights. The suit shared that Bachchan’s name, image and voice were being used by mobile application developers to conduct lotteries by illegally associating with Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC). He has also sought a restraining order against book publishers, T-shirt vendors and various other businesses.

On top of that, In November that year, Justice Navin Chawla passed an interim order restraining persons at large from infringing Bachchan's personality and publicity rights. Justice Chawla noted that the defendants were using the veteran star's star status to promote their own businesses without his permission.

"The plaintiff is likely to suffer irreparable loss and harm. Some of the activities may even bring his disrepute. In view of the above, an ex parte ad interim order is passed, " Justice Chawla had shared.

title: Nana Patekar was to be final guest on Shekhar Suman’s show Shekhar Tonite; finale cancelled after actor’s death: ‘No one can take his place’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The news of Nana Patekar’s death has left the movie industry in mourning, with colleagues and loved ones remembering him with grief and affection. Of late, Shekhar Suman opened up that he has decided to cancel the final episode of his talk show Shekhar Tonite following Nana’s demise on October 8. Shekhar shared that Nana was supposed to be the final guest on the show. After his death, he decided to cancel the episode rather than invite another star to take his place.

Adding to this, Shekhar Suman cancelled the finale episde of his show Shekhar Tonite after Nana Patekar's death. 'I want to come on your show' Shekhar shared a video on his YouTube channel in which he remembered Nana. He shared, “Words are less to praise the artiste, star, who was going to appear in this episode. Fearless, brave, honest, a person whose simplicity was his strongest trait. He congratulated me and shared that he watches my show regularly. He also told me that he sees himself in me. He shared, ‘I get offers from a lot of shows, I don’t go anywhere, but I want to come on your show.’ It felt like I got a Padma Vibhushan.”

Meanwhile, Shekhar Suman also spoke about his long association with Nana Patekar. He recalled working with the late star in Sohanlal Kanwar’s 1990 movie Tadap. Although the movie never saw the light of day, Shekhar shared the project gave him an opportunity to get to know Nana personally.

Notably, He shared, “During that time, I got to know him personally. I learnt a lot from him as a person, and as an star. Sadly, the movie was completed but couldn’t be rolled out. Look at the coincidence, that this episode that was supposed to be shot with him also won’t reach the audience ever. My heart will be upset about this all my life. It would have been the most beautiful conversation with him. Nana took a permanent break from us. We love you Nana and we will miss you forever. I didn’t feel like inviting anyone else today because no one can take his place. He is irreplaceable. He lived life on his own terms. I had even decided on my opening lines for the episode. I want to end our first season with his memories.”

As per the latest buzz, Nana Patekar died on Thursday morning at the age of 75 after suffering cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. He was rushed to the hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him for around 45 minutes but were unsuccessful. He was declared dead at around 5:20 am, with doctors citing a heart attack as the cause of death. The star was cremated with full state honours on Thursday at his farmhouse in Donje village, Pune.

title: CJP says 'dictator is terrified' as Delhi cops detain Dhruv Rathee ahead of Jantar Mantar protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Cockroach Janta Party on Saturday condemned the detention of YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in Gurugram, ahead of the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the special intensive revision exercise.

Adding to this, Dhruv Rathee (REUTERS) In a post on X, the CJP claimed the “dictator is terrified of young people who question its wrongdoings and refuse to stay silent.” Apart from Rathee, content creator Kavya Karnatac, who goes by the username ‘kk.create’ on Instagram, was also detained in Dhaula Kuan. CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh was also detained.

Meanwhile, Germany-based YouTuber Rathee, who of late travelled to India to join the CJP protests, was detained at his residence in Kendriya Vihar society in Gurugram's Sector-56. The Gurugram Police visited Rathee's residence on Saturday morning and urged him not to travel to the national capital to take part in the CJP protest, for which permission had been denied. Rathee was detained after he refused to comply.
Notably, In a statement after Rathee's detention, the CJP shared that it “strongly condemns” what it termed as the “Delhi Police's high-handed detention” of the YouTuber and other social activists.

As per the latest buzz, “The arrests are part of an aggressive, citywide government crackdown designed to silence democratic dissent regarding electoral roll irregularities,” the CJP shared, while demanding the “immediate and unconditional” rollout of Rathee and others.
In further updates, In its post on X, the CJP shared, “Dhruv Rathee has been detained. The Dictator is TERRIFIED of young people who question its wrongdoings and refuse to stay silent!”

On top of that, Security measures were heightened in Delhi ahead of the protest, with more than 40,000 Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) personnel deployed, and barricades and spike strips installed ahead of the proposed protest.

Apart from ramped up security measures, restrictions on mobile internet, metro access, train services and commercial establishments were also imposed. Authorities have imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), deployed additional security personnel and restricted access to several sensitive locations.

title: ‘Today he didn't message’: Amitabh Bachchan remembers Nana Patekar with emotional throwback video, says he is still speechless
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In a rare display of public emotion, Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan paid a heartfelt tribute to his co-star and friend Nana Pateka r a day after his death. The megastar shared a series of throwback videos celebrating their bond and professional association going back almost 30 years.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan with Nana Patekar on the set of their movie Kohram. Amitabh Bachchan shares video for Nana Patekar On Friday evening, the 83-year-old star posted on Instagram to share a carousel post featuring videos of him and Nana. The post features a couple of videos of Nana Patekar talking about Amitabh Bachchan in interviews.

Meanwhile, One video showed the two actors at the muhurat of their 1999 movie Kohram. The candid video showed Amitabh and Nana on stage before Jackie Shroff walked up to them. The three actors engaged in a playful exchange while Amitabh spoke on the phone. There were clips of the two actors' most recent public interaction as well, when Nana appeared on Kaun Banega Crorepati in 2024. The megastar’s social media post conveyed a deep sense of loss without an elaborate caption.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Amitabh Bachchan (@amitabhbachchan)

As per the latest buzz, Beyond the nostalgic videos, Amitabh Bachchan offered a more intimate glimpse into his grief in his blog. Revealing that the two actors had remained in regular touch through messages, the veteran star expressed his disbelief at the sudden loss.

In further updates, “Stabdh! Har doosre din unka aur hamara contact message ke zariye rehta tha. Aaj unka message nahi aaya! (Speechless! Every other day, he and I would stay in touch through messages. Today, he didn't message me),” the star wrote in his blog post.

On top of that, Earlier, in a heartfelt tribute to the veteran star, Amitabh Bachchan, while taking to the stage of Kaun Banega Crorepati, he honoured his dear friend, reflecting on his unmatched screen presence, uncompromising honesty, and lifelong dedication to humanitarian causes.

Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday at the age of 75 at his residence in Goa. According to doctors, he was found unconscious at his home and rushed to the hospital at 4 AM, where they tried to revive him but were unsuccessful. His death was mourned by the entire Indian movie industry and drew tributes from various public figures, including the Prime Minister and the President. Nana Patekar was cremated with full state honours at his Donje farmhouse in Pune on Thursday night.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Adding to this, Police shared the detentions were being made to prevent mass mobilisation and maintain law and order at Jantar Mantar. Meanwhile, According to a senior officer, more than 250 of the detainees were picked up by district police in southeast Delhi after they identified protesters around Shaheen Bagh and Jamia Nagar.

title: Aneet Padda calls working with Nana Patekar in Shakti Shalini ‘a lesson’, shares emotional tribute: ‘Still leaves me without words’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Aneet Padda stars with Nana Patekar in Shakti Shalini, his final movie. Aneet pays tribute to Nana Patekar Taking a trip down memory lane, Ane​et recalled her first meeting with Nana Patekar, admitting that she could barely speak as she took in the experience of sitting across from someone she described as honest, unfiltered and unapologetically himself.

Adding to this, “The first time I met Nana Patekar sir, I barely spoke. I think I was just taking it all in. To sit across from someone so honest, so unfiltered, so unapologetically himself was an experience in itself,” she wrote.

Meanwhile, In her heartfelt note, the star also spoke about Nana’s distinctive approach to life and cinema, highlighting how he chose simplicity over the noise of fame and stayed true to his own principles. She also recalled how simply listening to him speak and watching him work proved to be a learning experience that she would cherish for the rest of her life.

Notably, “He was someone who lived life on his own terms, chose simplicity over the noise of fame, and reminded you what it truly meant to be an star. Listening to him speak, watching him work, and simply being around him was a lesson I will always carry with me,” she added.
As per the latest buzz, Ane​et expressed gratitude for having met the veteran star so early in her journey and subsequently getting the opportunity to work with him.

In further updates, “To have met him so early in my journey, and then to work with him, is something I'll always be grateful for I learnt so much just by observing him, and looking back, I realise how precious those moments were. That one of his last films was with me still leaves me without words. It feels surreal,” she continued.

On top of that, Concluding her emotional tribute, the star wrote, “I'm grateful our paths crossed, even if only for a short while, and I'll carry it for the rest of my life.” She signed off with a heartfelt farewell to the veteran performer: “Rest in peace, Sir.”
Shakti Shalini director Aditya Sarpotdar also offered his tributes to the late star and spoke about having the opportunity to work with Nana Patekar.

title: ‘PM Modi is scared of youth’: Abhijeet Dipke on way to Delhi for Jantar Mantar protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke called Prime Minister Narendra Modi a “dictator” and shared that he is “afraid of the youth of the nation” as he left for Delhi from Mumbai to lead the protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday.

Adding to this, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke during the 'people's tribunal protest, organised by various civil society groups against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, at Freedom Park in Bengaluru. (PTI) “Narendra Modi is a dictator. He is scared, which is why he has closed the Delhi Metro, roads, everything. If he is this scared of the youth of the nation, why is he sitting in the PM's post?” he told reporters.

Meanwhile, Questioning the curbs on Delhi Metro and heavy security blanket, Dipke asked in a conversation with news agency ANI later: "Do Narendra Modi and Amit Shah want to wage war against the people of their own country? Is Gyanesh Kumar so dear to them that they would unleash their police and army forces upon their own citizens?"
Notably, Dipke shared that Modi is “afraid as he fears that the people of this country will not vote for him after this”.

As per the latest buzz, Defending the group's planned protest at Jantar Mantar, he shared, “Protesting is our fundamental right. Article 19 grants us the fundamental right to protest in a democratic and peaceful manner, and that is exactly what we intend to do.”

In further updates, With a massive gathering expected on Saturday, the Capital has been turned into a fortress, with more than 40,000 Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) personnel deployed to prevent protesters from converging on Jantar Mantar for a demonstration called by the CJP against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral roll irregularities.

On top of that, Jantar Mantar, the intended focal point of the protest, was sealed off even to media personnel. Its connecting roads were barricaded and manned by security forces, with loudspeakers at three key entry-exit points broadcasting warnings in Hindi and English against gatherings, processions, road blockades and other prohibited activities under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
Delhi Police shared more than 15,000 of its personnel had been deployed to handle Saturday’s anticipated protest, with around 26,000 central force personnel expected in the city.

title: World Mental Health Day Exclusive| Taapsee: I’m not going to romanticise trolling with fancy lines about knowing your self worth
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

On World Mental Health Day star Taapsee Pannu admits, “Like many of us in India I used to think mental health support is required when you go crazy but slowly grew up to understand it’s got dimensions more than that. I thought one approaches a therapist when touching clinical depression stage or when one cannot express what one is feeling but I realised mental health is also about being in the present and finding peace in what you have. If you aren’t at peace you constantly feel unstable and that’s what showbiz can make you feel.”

Adding to this, Taapsee Pannu She goes on to say that Covid changed a lot of things for her because it put her physical activity at rest. She says, “Earlier I would channel my mental anxiety and anxiousness into physical activity by engaging into more work or go outside and engage in some activity or sport to avoid facing my anxiety or be by myself. I would tell myself I’m overthinking and would rush to focus on my job. During Covid, like everyonelse I was forced to spend time with myself and realised I need to take care of my mental health better. “

Meanwhile, Taapsee points out that being a part of showbiz dealing with trolling and personal attacks is not easy. “I’m not going to romanticise it with fancy lines about knowing your self worth. No matter how strong you are when your job and standing is largely dependant on everyonelses perception of you, what they say and feel about you, it’s never easy. It was way more harsh in the beginning for me, not just in terms of career but also when I got on social media. She adds people’s two seconds of attention can cause actors a lot of mental health damage. “I was trying this impossible task to make everyone happy. I got burnt out and it took me years to accept the situation. I realised I wasted years trying to appease trolls rather than spending that time working on myself as an star or human being. I sacrificed a lot of time and braincells to understand this but sometimes trolling still affects me,” says Taapsee. She adds that media portals that tear actors down also affects their state of mind.

Notably, She agrees that social media has made actors more vulnerable to anxeity and comparisn. She expalins, “Exploitation of celebs is now more availiable to make a joke about but it affects everyone. We even have trolls questioning why does this star get opportunities, existential questions are discussed by people who I’m not sure are qualified to question someone’s profession. It has made actors vulnerable and the repercussion is that actors stopped using social media to display their true selves. They have started displaying the persona that people like more and sells more. You aren’t connecting with a human being but a brand." She goes on to reveal why she decided to be inactive on social media. “I disconnected with social media after a point because I couldn’t be dishonest about the person I am. I had the choice of being inactive on social media or being battered mentally so I chose the first option,” says the star.

As per the latest buzz, She also admits that she has taken therapy and is glad it isn’t taboo anymore. “The characters I play are mentally exhausting so I would travel somewhere where I could disconnect and forget about my work life. When Covid happened I didn’t have that privilege and had to face my demons. I became more vulnerable and sensitive thats when I took some therapy sessions to learn the art of dealing with myself without running away," says Taapsee.

title: Saif Ali Khan's sister Saba Pataudi recalls feeling shattered after brain tumour diagnosis at 27: ‘Your life suddenly goes numb’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Saba Pataudi , sister of star Saif Ali Khan , opened up about being diagnosed with a brain tumour when she was 27 and going under the knife in 2006. It was in the latest episode of Soha Ali Khan's All About Her podcast, where she invited her sister Saba Ali Khan and Dr Mazda Turel to talk about brain tumours and what constitutes a healthy brain. Saba opened up about the day she fainted and what happened next that led to her diagnosis.

Adding to this, Saba Pataudi has opened up about a major health scare. What Saba shared Recalling the exact moment when she felt something was off, Saba shared, “It happened very suddenly. I didn’t have any pre-symptoms or any conditions that I think led up to it. One day, I went out and thought the problem was with my stomach, which has always been a sensitive point for me. I thought I had eaten or drunk something that hadn’t agreed with me. I suddenly fainted. I could feel myself becoming very uncomfortable, so I turned to a friend and shared, ‘I don’t think I’m quite okay. Maybe we should head home.’ We were about to go out, but suddenly everything went blank. When I regained consciousness, I had already fallen on the road, just outside the building. I turned to my friend again and shared that we had to head back because I definitely wasn’t okay. It took me about 20 to 25 minutes to feel more conscious. Even then, I was still a little hazy, and my awareness hadn’t completely settled.”

Meanwhile, Immediately, Saba went for an MRI, and the doctors found a shadow in the third ventricle of her brain. She was diagnosed with a colloid cyst, a rare but non-cancerous growth filled with gelatinous fluid. Saba shared that she underwent surgery around six months after the MRI. It was identified as a pilocytic astrocytoma, a type of brain tumour generally classified as low-grade.

Notably, “It was something completely unexpected that happened to me at the age of 27, without any warning. Your life suddenly goes numb because nothing feels normal after that. One day, you’re fine, and the next day, you’re told that you’re going to have brain surgery. It’s not something as simple as having your appendix removed. It shatters you in a way, but it also empowers you because you have to deal with it. I would suddenly find myself crying without knowing why. You are trying to process news that you never expected to receive. What happened to me came with absolutely no warning,” she added.
As per the latest buzz, In May this year, Saba Pataudi celebrated her 50th birthday with family, sharing heartfelt gratitude for their love and thoughtful gifts in a series of social media post.

title: 6 special trains arranged to bring 10k CAPF personnel for Delhi protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The ministry of railways had to arrange at least six special trains at short notice to bring nearly 10,000 Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel to the national Capital for security preparations ahead of the October 10 protests, officials aware of the matter shared, adding that railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and senior ministry officials held a nearly three-hour meeting with the Prime Minister’s Office ( PMO ) on Thursday evening to discuss train arrangements, including cancellations and diversions. One train carrying CAPF troops reached Delhi on Friday afternoon while another will arrive tonight, they added.

Adding to this, The deployment of more than 26,000 personnel from CAPFs, working alongside the Delhi Police to manage the protests, is the largest in Delhi since the February 2020 assembly elections. (ANI) “The meeting was related to the arrangement, the cancellation/diversion of trains in the backdrop of the protests. 6 special trains have already been sent. Depending on the law and order situation, the ministry may make another request in the coming days,” a railways officer, who asked not to be named, shared.

Meanwhile, According to an October 6 letter seen by HT, the home ministry approved at least 110 additional CAPF companies and wrote to the Railway Board director requesting special trains and extra coaches to bring them from different states.

Notably, The deployment of more than 26,000 personnel from CAPFs, working alongside the Delhi Police to manage the protests, is the largest in Delhi since the February 2020 assembly elections, the visit of US President Donald Trump and the Delhi riots—all of which occurred in the same month.

As per the latest buzz, Officials shared the 110 additional companies are from all forces – CRPF, BSF, SSB, ITBP and CISF. Most of them are coming from Jammu and Kashmir(J&K), West Bengal and Chhattisgarh, adding to the 111 companies already deployed in Delhi. Each CAPF company has a sanctioned strength of 120-130 personnel, of whom around 75-80 are generally deployed. Together, the 221 companies will work alongside the Delhi Police.

In further updates, “Unlike elections in West Bengal, when the CRPF had taken their mine-protected anti-riot vehicles, they are not bringing the vehicles this time. The vehicles are effective, but having them in the national Capital will be bad for optics. It was a last-minute directive from the force headquarters to come to Delhi. A large section of troops who were in interior areas of Bastar are yet to reach Delhi because the orders were issued at short notice. Some of them take at least 8-10 hours just to reach the nearest railway station. But they will all be in Delhi by the morning of October 10,” a CRPF officer, who asked not to be named, shared.

On top of that, Meanwhile, people in the aviation sector shared that the CISF also sought passenger details from airlines for select flights to Delhi on Friday and Saturday. Senior police officers, who asked not to be named, shared Thursday evening that police would stop some people arriving in Delhi by air who planned to drive towards Jantar Mantar. The officer shared no group has been allowed to assemble in Jantar Mantar because prohibitory orders are in place across the New Delhi district.

To be sure, CAPF troops during elections or arrangements such as Amarnath Yatra are always moved in special trains, but the request is sent months in advance, giving time for the troops to prepare their local conveyance and railways for the trains.

title: CJP protest LIVE: Abhijeet Dipke, Das, Ranka detained at Delhi airport ahead of Jantar Mantar protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

CJP Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: The CJP has been demanding that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. CJP Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained upon landing at the Delhi airport ahead of their planned protest at Jantar Mantar against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi has been turned into a fortress, with more than 40,000 Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) personnel deployed, and barricades and spike strips installed ahead of the planned protest at Jantar Mantar. The protesters are seeking the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. ...Read More

Adding to this, Jantar Mantar 2.0: Why CJP is protesting again The CJP has been demanding that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. The group has continued to raise the issue through protests and public statements, including a demonstration in Mumbai on October 2. The latest protest has been planned at Jantar Mantar in Delhi; however, the Delhi Police shared the organisers did not have the required permission to hold the demonstration and rejected their request, citing public interest. The row over Kumar's role in the Election Commission intensified after an investigative report by The Indian Express. It reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and procedures linked to the SIR exercise. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that around 13 crore rupees voters had been removed from electoral rolls since 2024. He also linked the alleged deletions to the narrow vote-share gap between the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and the Opposition INDIA bloc in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, arguing that large-scale changes to voter lists could influence election results. The Election Commission has rejected the allegations, maintaining that major decisions, including the SIR of electoral rolls, had been taken unanimously by the full commission. Delhi turns into a fortress Ahead of the protest, security was tightened around Jantar Mantar and the roads leading to the site. Barricades were put up, with security personnel deployed at key points. Loudspeakers at three major entry and exit points issued warnings in Hindi and English against gatherings, processions, road blockades and other activities prohibited under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Delhi Police shared more than 15,000 personnel had been deployed to manage the anticipated turnout on Saturday, while the number of central force personnel in the city was expected to be around 26,000. Security measures also affected public transport. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) initially opened up that entry and exit would be suspended at 57 stations from 9 pm on Friday until Saturday. It later revised the list to 45 stations. The Railways also cancelled mail and express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday, citing the possibility of heavy road congestion. CJP protest: What's open and what's closed in Delhi Movement across Delhi has been affected by train cancellations, restrictions at Metro stations, the closure of retail liquor shops and tighter police security ahead of the planned protest. These measures have raised concerns over travel and access to several parts of the national capital. No mail and express trains at 2 Delhi stations The Railways cancelled mail and express trains at their originating stations if they were scheduled to arrive at New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday, October 10. The decision was taken amid concerns over heavy road traffic around the stations due to a planned protest in central Delhi. Entry and exit restrictions at 57 stations The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) opened up that entry and exit gates at 45 Metro stations have been closed from 9 pm on Friday. The restrictions will remain in place through Saturday until the situation returns to normal. Retail liquor shops Retail liquor outlets across Delhi will remain closed on October 9 and 10 under an order issued by the excise department. The restrictions cover specified outlets selling Indian, foreign and country liquor, including some shops located in malls. However, licensed restaurants, bars and clubs will continue to serve liquor as usual, an excise department official shared. Entry to Jantar Mantar restricted The Delhi Police has also restricted access to Jantar Mantar ahead of the protest. Even media personnel have been denied entry to the protest site. Namo Bharat's Delhi stations closed The Sarai Kale Khan and New Ashok Nagar Namo Bharat stations in Delhi will remain closed from 9 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10.

Meanwhile, CJP Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Police have also detained more than 60 people from Bangla Sahib Gurdwara, where the protesters had taken shelter overnight. Police personnel waited outside the gurdwara and detained them when they came out in the morning.

Notably, CJP protest LIVE: In visuals shared by CJP from inside the flight where Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained, the leaders can be heard shouting “Bharat Mata ki Jai” slogans.

As per the latest buzz, CJP Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Former Keralam CM Pinarayi Vijayan, among other CPI(M) leaders, including CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby, MV Govindan Master, A Vijayaraghavan, KK Shailaja, John Brittas, KN Balagopal, Brinda Karat, were taken into custody by Delhi Police upon arriving at Jantar Mantar to participate in the protest, the party claimed.

In further updates, CJP protest LIVE: A senior police officer verified that CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been detained. Teams from the southwest district police were deployed at the Delhi airport to detain them.

On top of that, Protesters and independent media persons have also been detained near Jantar Mantar. A police van was seen packed with protesters, while paramilitary personnel blocked all routes around the barricades.

title: 3 stadiums to be used as temporary detention centres in Delhi during Jantar Mantar protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Three sports facilities in Delhi will be used as temporary detention centres if the need arises amid heightened security arrangements ahead of Saturday’s joint protest call by Cockroach Janta Party and several student unions at Jantar Mantar, for which Delhi Police has denied permission, a government official aware of the developments shared on Friday.

Adding to this, Police have also identified Nirankari Samagam Ground in Burari as a possible detention site depending on the situation. (HT) According to the official, who did not wish to be named, police have informed the government about plans to set up detention facilities at Rajiv Gandhi Stadium in Bawana, the Chhatrasal Stadium in north Delhi and Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, near India Gate to accommodate people who may be detained during security operations during the proposed protest.

Meanwhile, A police officer shared that Nirankari Samagam Ground in Burari, north Delhi, may also be used for detentions. “The ground may also be used for detentions depending on the situation,” a police officer shared.
Notably, The proposed use of the three stadiums as detention facilities indicates the scale of preparations to handle the security situation.
As per the latest buzz, The arrangements come amid a series of preventive measures the Delhi Police is putting in place to prevent protesters from gathering at Jantar Mantar .

In further updates, Police personnel have been deployed at key locations, while checks and restrictions have been intensified across the Capital, particularly in central Delhi and at all entry points into the city.
On top of that, Police have also been visiting hotels, guest houses, and other accommodation facilities to ask occupants why they are visiting Delhi, as part of efforts to prevent large gatherings.
Traffic diversions are scheduled to begin at 6 am on Saturday at 30 locations across the city, depending on the prevailing law and order situation, a traffic police officer shared.

title: Public safety, past lapses: Why Delhi Police denied CJP permission for Jantar Mantar protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police has denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, citing short notice, alleged violations during earlier demonstrations and concerns over public safety and law and order. The police also defended the restrictions imposed in New Delhi , saying they were necessary to prevent overcrowding and ensure the safety of protesters, residents and commuters.

Adding to this, The Cockroach Janta Party has plans of holding a 'Chalo Dilli' protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, which has resulted in widespread restrictions across the capital. (ANI/PTI) In a letter dated October 9, addressed to CJP co-convener Saurav Das and joint secretary Balkrishna, the New Delhi district police shared the group's communication submitted on October 7 was merely an intimation of the proposed protest and did not constitute a duly submitted application seeking permission.
Meanwhile, The police shared existing guidelines require applications for programmes at Jantar Mantar to be submitted at least 10 days before the intended date.
Notably, The police shared the right to protest is a fundamental right but that granting permission also requires authorities to consider the rights of other citizens and residents.
As per the latest buzz, It cited traffic congestion, safety concerns and the potential disruption of public life as reasons for regulating demonstrations.

In further updates, The police referred to the July protests at Jantar Mantar, saying permission had been granted for a one-day demonstration but that it continued for around a month. In its statement on X, the police shared more than 200 personnel were injured during the protests and alleged that the participation of people with criminal antecedents contributed to the violence.

On top of that, Hindustan Times reported on July 27, citing Delhi Police officials, that police had identified 2,873 people through CCTV footage linked to the July 20 march towards Parliament . Of these, 989 were found to have criminal antecedents, according to the officials.

The cases included murder, robbery, sexual assault and other offences. The police claims about the criminal antecedents of those identified were attributed to officials and should not be read as convictions.

body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

According to a Business Standard report citing property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix, the office measures 950 square feet and is situated on the fourth floor of Vastu Prestige, near City Mall in Andheri West.

Adding to this, The leave-and-licence agreement was registered on June 12, with the lease commencing on July 10. The agreement will remain valid until July 9, 2031, covering a total tenure of 60 months.

Meanwhile, As per the report, the commercial premises have been leased to Kerawi Care (OPC) Private Limited, represented by its director, Vandana Verma. Roy is listed as the licensor in the agreement, while the company is the licensee.

Notably, The office space carries a monthly rent of Rs 2.1 lakhs, while the security deposit has been set at Rs 6.5 lakhs. The total rent payable over the five-year period amounts to Rs 1,39,24,584. The agreement also provides for an annual rent escalation of 5%, along with a lock-in period of 36 months for both parties.

As per the latest buzz, The terms further specify the division of property-related expenses between the parties. Roy, as the licensor, will be responsible for property taxes, maintenance charges and non-occupancy charges. Meanwhile, the tenant will pay electricity bills according to actual consumption. The report also noted that the agreement does not mention any designated car parking space for the office.

In further updates, This is not the star’s first reported real estate transaction in Mumbai. According to a Hindustan Times report citing property registration documents accessed by IndexTap.com, Roy purchased a 4,258-square-foot apartment in the Lodha Versova project in 2024 for Rs 18.94 crores. The property as per reports came with four car parking spaces.

On top of that, A separate Economic Times report published in September 2026 shared that Roy and his family reside in Versova, where they expanded their home over the years by acquiring adjoining apartments.

Apart from his acting career, Roy is known for his roles as Mihir Virani in Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi and Rishabh Bajaj in Kasautii Zindagii Kay. He also owns Ace Security and Protection, a security agency that has as per reports served several prominent Bollywood personalities, including Amitabh Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan and Aamir Khan. title: ECI fortified, 254 trains cancelled, metro affected, internet shut: Delhi braces for CJP's October 10 protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi has tightened security ahead of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10, with restrictions on mobile internet, metro access, train services and commercial establishments expected to affect daily life across parts of the national capital.

Adding to this, Security personnel are seen deployed in large numbers near Jantar Mantar, as roads leading to the protest site remain closed and barricaded amid heightened security arrangements ahead of a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in New Delhi. (Hindustan Times) The protest, organised by the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) and student groups, seeks the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The INDIA bloc has also separately been protesting against the Election Commission, accusing it of failing to ensure free and fair elections.

Meanwhile, Authorities have imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), deployed additional security personnel and restricted access to several sensitive locations.
Notably, Delhi Police has denied permission for Saturday’s demonstration, citing the late submission of the application and alleged violations during an earlier protest.
As per the latest buzz, Access to Ashoka Road towards the Election Commission of India (ECI) headquarters has been blocked with a bus near the Sansad Marg–Ashoka Road roundabout.
In further updates, Barricades have been placed outside the ECI headquarters, with security personnel deployed in large numbers.
On top of that, The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has approved a 24-hour suspension of mobile internet services in a four-kilometre radius around the Janpath-Kartavya Path area in New Delhi.

The shutdown began at 10 pm on Friday and will continue until 10 pm on Saturday. Authorities have issued the order on public security grounds under the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024. The order specifically concerns mobile internet services within the notified zone.

title: 'Final call': Dipke releases video message ahead of CJP protest, anticipates arrest upon landing in Delhi
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

CJP's Abhijeet Dipke , in a final video appeal ahead of the protest at Jantar Mantar over CEC row in Delhi on October 10, shared he was unsure whether he would be arrested upon landing in the national capital but asserted that he would not back down from the fight for free and fair elections.

Adding to this, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke speaks during a protest seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. (ANI) The CJP is leading a massive demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Meanwhile, Dipke shared he would travel from Mumbai to Delhi on Saturday morning and urged people to join the protest in large numbers. He added that he was not afraid of being detained or arrested, or of facing charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or the National Security Act (NSA).

Notably, "I am not scared (even) if I am detained or arrested. The government can slap NSA or UAPA against me. CJP wants free and fair polls and that cannot happen without (Chief Election Commissioner) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation or scrapping of SIR or neutral procedure to appoint election commissioner," he shared, asking people to come to Jantar Mantar in large numbers.
As per the latest buzz, “This is a fight to save our country's democracy,” Dipke shared, reiterating the CJP's demand for free and fair elections.

In further updates, Dipke had posted the video on both Instagram and X. He later claimed that the government had blocked the video on X, sharing a screenshot of the post and writing, “Lol they blocked the video I just posted.” The video, however, remained available on his Instagram account.
On top of that, The CJP founder also urges demonstrators to keep the protest peaceful and added that it must continue until Gyanesh resigns, he shared.
“Tomorrow, whatever happens, we will make history,” shared Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader.

title: Drishyam 3 box office collection day 8: Ajay Devgn film stays steady as it enters second week, crosses ₹257 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 8 : Drishyam 3 is emerging as one of the biggest success stories of the year. The Ajay Devgn movie saw a bumper opening at the ticket-window and crossed the ₹ 200 crore rupees mark in five days. It has also surpassed the lifetime collections of several hits, including Karuppu, Sikandar and Awarapan 2. Although the movie witnessed an expected drop in collections on Monday, it has not slowed down its box-office run.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 8: It is a sequel to the 2022 movie starring Ajay Devgn. (HT_PRINT) Drishyam 3 ticket-window report Drishyam 3 scored a huge first week in theatres. The advance bookings for Drishyam The Conclusion opened on September 27, and the movie went on to collect ₹ 27 crore rupees before its rollout. By the end of the day, the movie went on to collect ₹ 66.75 crore rupees net across India. This is the third biggest opening by a Hindi movie ever and the biggest in Ajay Devgn’s career. On Saturday, the movie collected ₹ 53.50 crore rupees, and showed huge growth on Sunday, bringing in ₹ 61 crore rupees. By the end of first week, the movie had collected ₹ 245.50 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, The latest update now states that Drishyam 3 has collected ₹ 11.73 crore rupees by 10 PM. This takes its total India net collection to ₹ 257.23 crore rupees . Drishyam 3 has already crossed the lifetime haul of its predecessor Drishyam 2, which stood at ₹ 239.67 crore rupees. It is now eyeing to surpass the collection of Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior. The 2020 historical drama remains Ajay's highest-grossing movie, with a lifetime collection of ₹ 279.59 crore rupees in net collection.

Notably, Drishyam 3 takes off right after the conclusion of Drishyam 2, and marks the return of Ajay's Vijay Salgaonkar for one last time. Ahead of the rollout, Ajay lauded director Abhishek Pathak at the trailer launch event and added, “The way he's worked the script out, the way he's shaped up the movie… Like he shared, he's grown on 'Drishyam'. You will see in this movie that he's really grown on 'Drishyam'. And just on the writing part, the way he's executed the movie, I think he's done a fabulous job. I want Lal sir and Jeethu sir to see the movie, and if we get their approval that they love this, it will make me very happy.”

As per the latest buzz, Drishyam The Conclusion is backed by Star Studio18 and Panorama Studios, with Abhishek Pathak returning to direct the third instalment. He has also co-written the movie with Aamil Keeyan Khan and Parveez Shaikh. Alok Jain, Ajit Andhare, Kumar Mangat Pathak and Abhishek Pathak are producing the movie.

title: ‘Nothing can stop youth’: Chirag Paswan on train, metro curbs ahead of protests in Delhi tomorrow
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chirag Paswan comments on Delhi metro curbs, train cancellations (PTI/ANI) The LJP(RV) President, an ally of BJP-led NDA, was asked whether transport restrictions could stop young people from reaching Delhi to demand Kumar’s resignation amid the SIR row and reports of dissent within the Election Commission.

Adding to this, “These are the youth of India, nothing can stop them," Paswan shared. "To those attempting to spread such misconceptions, I ask: how many trains can anyone really stop? How much connectivity can be blocked? How many roads can be jammed? These are India's youth; they possess the capacity to show the world the way, just as previous generations have done, and so, nothing can hold them back,” he shared.

Meanwhile, His remarks came amid heightened security arrangements in Delhi and disruptions to rail and metro services ahead of planned protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other student organisations.

Notably, The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) opened up that entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations would remain closed from 9 pm on Friday until further notice, citing security concerns ahead of the proposed protest.

As per the latest buzz, Interchange facilities will remain available at all affected stations except New Delhi metro station. Train frequency at the identified stations may also be reduced depending on the security situation, the DMRC shared.

In further updates, The decision followed a request from Delhi Police, which cited the possibility of unruly movement towards sensitive locations and recommended closing the entry and exit gates until the situation normalised.

On top of that, Indian Railways has cancelled several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations amid concerns over traffic congestion and passenger access during the protest.

According to railway officials, train services at the two stations have been suspended for a 10-hour period, from 4 am to 2 pm on Saturday. Several other services have also been cancelled, rescheduled or affected by changes to their originating stations.

title: Sonakshi-Zaheer reveal how a friend's suggestion gave their film 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran' its title
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai, Star-couple Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal on Friday shared the title of their soon-to-release movie "Tu Hai Meri Kiran" emerged from a casual conversation with friends and aptly captures its themes of one-sided love, obsession and the blurred line between reality and imagination.

Adding to this, Sonakshi-Zaheer reveal how a friend's suggestion gave their movie 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran' its title The couple, who attended Whistling Woods International's annual cinema festival "Celebrate Cinema '26" to promote the movie, shared the title came together after a friend suggested it during a dinner conversation about the project.

Meanwhile, "We were out for dinner and they were like, 'what's your next?' And I shared I'm doing this movie, which was very hard to describe in one line. So I ended up narrating the whole movie to them so that they get exact idea of what I'm doing," Iqbal shared.

Notably, "And at the end, this one friend just like, bro, this should be called 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran'. And I was like, 'yeah'. And then I called the producer and he's like, 'bro, I don't think this name is going to be available'. And it was, so luckily," he added.
As per the latest buzz, Sinha shared the title felt right as soon as it was suggested by their friend, adding that it helped them connect more deeply with the movie.

In further updates, "I thought it was so suitable, and thanks to our friend who came up with it, Swati. We had a working title before that, but ever since this name came, we felt more connected with the movie because it all just came together," she shared.
On top of that, "The recall value comes. It automatically tells you the theme of the movie. So I think it's truly apt," she added.

The title comes from the popular line "Tu Hai Meri Kiran" associated with the song from Yash Chopra's 1993 movie "Darr", in which Shah Rukh Khan played an obsessive lover fixated on a woman named Kiran, portrayed by Juhi Chawla.

title: Sona Mohapatra sticks up for Tanushree Dutta after Nana Patekar's death: ‘Demanding a woman who spoke up about her trauma just shut up?’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Sona Mohapatra has spoken up in support of Tanushree Dutta after Nana Patekar ’s death. In a video she posted on X (formerly Twitter) and Instagram, she called out the hypocrisy of those celebrating Nana’s legacy to expect Tanushree not to talk about the sexual harassment she went through. The singer also hit back at those who claimed Nana deserved more respect for his philanthropy.

Adding to this, Sona Mohapatra called out those harassing Tanushree Dutta since Nana Patekar's death. Sona Mohapatra questions what Nana Patekar followers expect from Tanushree Dutta In her X caption, Sona wrote, “Death deserves dignity. So do the living. Mourning an star is 1 thing. Demanding that a woman who spoke up about her trauma just shut up is another #India. Since when did death erase uncomfortable truths? Old age a virtue? Death = Sainthood? #TanushreeDutta #MeToo #NanaPatekar.”

Meanwhile, Mentioning that she has gotten used to being the most unpopular person in a room because she cannot keep quiet when something is wrong, she added, “Nana Patekar passed away yesterday, a celebrated star, people are mourning him, understandably so. I have no issues with that. What’s disturbing me is the way people are attacking Tanushree Dutta. Seriously, what do you expect from her?”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by 𝓢𝓸𝓷𝓪 𝓜𝓸𝓱𝓪𝓹𝓪𝓽𝓻𝓪 (@sonamohapatra)

As per the latest buzz, She mentioned that Tanushree faced a lot for calling out Nana publicly, saying, “This woman spoke up about her sexual harassment on sets with this gentleman. Fought an exhausting battle. Faced a public humiliation and professional consequences. And now, she’s supposed to forget her experience and perform what for you? Grief? That’ll comfort you?”

In further updates, She called out women for joining in the cacophony of voices against Tanushree and criticized them, “Really? Is humiliating another woman your idea of engagement?” Sona also pointed out, “Dying shouldn’t erase uncomfortable chapters of someone’s life. You can celebrate an artist’s work, mourn his passing, and offer his family compassion. But you cannot demand that a woman rewrite her own history to make your mourning comfortable.”

On top of that, Sona also pointed out that while Nana is celebrated for being ‘muffat’ (blunt), no woman would be for being ‘downright rude’. “Tanushree Dutta is entitled to her account of what happened. And if your compassion requires humiliating a woman who spoke up, it’s definitely not compassion. It’s your hypocrisy. Death deserves dignity, so do the living,” she shared.

When an Instagram-user claimed that Sona was talking about a person who donated ‘most of his income to the farmers and the poor’ and questioned why ‘only one woman’ raised her voice against him, Sona wondered why charity cancels out misconduct, mentioning Jimmy Savile from Britain. title: 'Identify other place for protests': Supreme Court calls for alternative to Jantar Mantar in Delhi
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Friday called for a rethink of Delhi’s decades-old arrangement of holding demonstrations at Jantar Mantar , recording that the Delhi Police commissioner and other competent authorities would consider designating an alternative venue with better facilities for peaceful protesters.

Adding to this, The court also stressed that any alternative site should have basic amenities, including portable cabins, toilets, drinking water and medical facilities (PTI) A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana shared the national capital needed a larger, better-equipped space where citizens could exercise their democratic right to protest without compromising public safety, access to emergency services or the interests of other residents.

Meanwhile, “It is high time that some other place with amenities for peaceful protestors need to be identified and designated,” the bench recorded in its order, adding that the competent authority should consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision.

Notably, The court also stressed that any alternative site should have basic amenities, including portable cabins, toilets, drinking water and medical facilities. It shared a venue must be spacious enough to accommodate demonstrators while allowing emergency services to reach them in the event of an incident.

As per the latest buzz, The suggestion emerged during the hearing of pleas challenging sweeping restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of the October 10 protests in Delhi. The court directed the Centre and Delhi Police to reconsider the complete stoppage of public transport, emphasising that preventive security measures must remain proportionate and cannot deprive millions of residents of access to essential services.

In further updates, During the hearing, the bench shared many of the difficulties surrounding protests arose from Jantar Mantar’s geographical location and suggested that another open space could allow demonstrations to take place with better facilities and fewer logistical complications.

On top of that, “Why don’t you find an alternative space where you can also provide better facilities?” the bench asked solicitor general Tushar Mehta, who appeared for the Centre and Delhi Police. Mehta shared he would convey the court’s sentiments to the appropriate authorities.

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, representing Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary Mariam Alexander Baby, responded that Ramlila Maidan had previously served as an alternative protest venue but was no longer being offered as an option when permission to demonstrate at Jantar Mantar was denied.

title: Sandhya Mridul backs Tanushree Dutta after ‘evil dead’ remark for Nana Patekar's death: ‘Does the harm caused by an abuser disappear with them?’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nana Patekar died in the early hours of October 8 in Goa at the age of 75 from a cardiac arrest. Tanushree Dutta , who had accused the star years ago of sexual harassment on a movie set, made an ‘evil dead’ remark after his death. It sparked backlash on social media, with even the All Indian Cine Workers Association ( AICWA ) condemned the star for making such a comment. Now star Sandhya Mridul has reacted indirectly to the star's death and asked if a person stops being an abuser after death.

Adding to this, Sandhya Mridul asked if a person stops being an abuser after death. ‘I will always stand with the survivor’ Without naming either Tanushree or Nana in her Instagram post, Sandhya wrote, “Does a person stop being an abuser when they die? Does the harm they caused disappear too? For survivors, it doesn’t." In the caption, she noted, "A survivor lives with it for as long as they live. I will always stand with the survivor."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sandhya Mridul (@sandymridul)

Notably, In her Instagram Stories, Sandhya wrote, "A person's death does not automatically erase the harm they may have caused. Abuse does not become untrue because the abuser is gone, and the experiences of survivors do not become less real in the face of public tributes.”

As per the latest buzz, She added, “It is possible to mourn someone, and it is also important to remember that there may be people carrying pain connected to them. When only praise is allowed and survivors are forgotten, it can feel like their truth disappears all over again.”

In further updates, Without naming Nana, Tanushree wrote on her Instagram Stories, “This is insane! My story timeline has exploded today. Evil is dead and my life is hopefully on track for better things!”

On top of that, In another post, Tanushree alluded to the abuse she alleged Nana had committed. On Thursday, after news broke of Nana’s death, Tanushree posted videos of her boarding a flight to Lucknow for an event. In a video, she shared, “Maine suna hai, I have heard the news. I just… today is my workday. I am going to Lucknow for an event. And I want to focus on that. What an odd day for all this to happen."

She also added, "Because I’m doing a very big event in Lucknow, and it was pretty important for me. I had my entire day planned out. I wanted to do all these Lives and post content. And now I’m worried that in the evening, that’s all the media is going to be interested in is evil dead. So, I will give my reaction once I figure out what kind of reaction I should have. So, definitely condolences to the family but...” and her video cut off midway.

title: Meezaan Jafri headlines Killer Jeans' Genes of India campaign
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Denim is now one of the most versatile and widely worn categories in Indian fashion. It is part of wardrobes across age groups and occasions, and it continues to influence how younger consumers dress for work, travel, social settings and celebrations. Genes of India builds on this shift, presenting denim as a shared part of Indian style, from Kashmir to Kanyakumari.

Adding to this, Meezaan Jafri, as brand ambassador, connects with an audience that sees denim as a core part of personal style and not as a casual alternative. His styling reflects the fits and combinations that younger consumers are choosing today. “Denim is something almost everyone in India relates to, whatever their background or city,” shared Meezaan Jafri. “What I like about Genes of India is that it doesn’t ask people to dress a certain way. It recognises that everyone wears denim differently, and that is what makes it ours.”
Meanwhile, A post shared by Killer Jeans (@killerjeansofficial)

Notably, The latest addition to the Killer line-up, Neo Flare brings a contemporary perspective to the classic flare silhouette. Designed to sit slim through the hip, thigh and knee, the fit gradually opens below the knee to create a longer, leaner profile. Neo Flare brings a fresh dimension to everyday denim and pairs effortlessly with everything from sneakers to boots.

As per the latest buzz, The collection is complemented by Selvedge Denim, known for its distinctive character, texture and craftsmanship, alongside Killer’s range of fabric innovations. K-Tech Denim offers a lighter feel, SoftPro Denim delivers a softer hand-feel, while Cool Core Denim is designed to provide comfort across changing weather conditions. Together, these innovations reflect Killer’s focus on combining contemporary denim design with fit, functionality and comfort.

In further updates, “Denim has always been something I’ve felt people can make their own. In India, that feels even more interesting because the way you wear it changes from city to city, from generation to generation, and from person to person. That’s what drew me to Genes of India; it’s not about one definition of denim, but about all the different ways we style it, live in it and make it part of who we are” shared Hemant Jain, Joint Managing Director, Kewal Kiran Clothing Limited.

On top of that, Killer’s contribution to the category begins with its products. The brand designs for Indian consumers, with attention to fit, comfort and finish, and places weight on Indian manufacturing and the craftsmanship that goes into making denim. Through Genes of India, it aims to bring that work into focus and to support a stronger domestic denim category, where consumers can find quality, trend-relevant options made in India.
Killer believes Indian denim has significant room to grow, driven by rising fashion awareness, a greater willingness to experiment and demand for quality, locally made products.

title: Student’s death triggers protests at Kota’s Rajasthan Technical University
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
A student’s death triggered protests at Rajasthan Technical University (RTU) in Kota, with police resorting to force to disperse agitating students after the demonstration escalated on Thursday.

Adding to this, The student allegedly died of a snakebite on the campus. (HT Photo/Representative ) The first-year information technology student from Jaipur was found dead in his hostel room. Students alleged that he died of a snakebite on the campus. The university administration shared he may have suffered a cardiac arrest. The exact cause of death will be established after the postmortem report, officials shared.

Meanwhile, The protesting students accused the university administration of negligence and demanded the removal of chief warden DK Yadav. They alleged that the campus dispensary closes at 2am and doctors are often unavailable, claiming that timely medical attention could have saved the student’s life.
Notably, Students claimed that snakes had been spotted on the campus on several occasions. They staged a sit-in, insisting that their demands be addressed.

As per the latest buzz, Yadav shared when Sharma was found unresponsive, the university team rushed to his room and arranged to take him to hospital in an autorickshaw. He added that doctors indicated that the student had died in his sleep between 4am and 6am. Yadav shared the circumstances would become clear after the postmortem report.

In further updates, Police attempted to persuade the students to end their protest, but when they refused to disperse, force was used. Officials shared the situation became difficult to control after some students allegedly began throwing stones.

On top of that, Additional police superintendent Subhash Chandra Mishra shared the protesters demanded that the vice-chancellor come to the spot so they could present their demands. He added that several rounds of talks were held, following which the vice-chancellor agreed to some of the demands.

Mishra shared no agreement was reached on all demands, but the students eventually called off their protest. Police assured them that the circumstances surrounding the student’s death would be investigated impartially.

That is when storytelling becomes meaningful for a destination – when a movie sparks curiosity and leads to a more personal journey.”

Meanwhile, However, the sudden popularity has also brought its share of problems. ThePrint published a detailed report on how locals are struggling to cope with the influx of tourists in the post- Hanuman Ansh era. The report opened up that rooms which normally cost Rs. 2,000-3,000 per night were being offered for as much as Rs. 7,000 during the recent rush. The massive crowds also led to traffic congestion and put pressure on local infrastructure.

Notably, This is also an example of the flip side of movie tourism, where a destination becomes so popular that it struggles to accommodate the influx of visitors. The situation has prompted authorities to consider stricter measures. As per the latest buzz, the administration is planning to introduce a registration system for visitors, initially on weekends, to regulate the crowds and ensure a smoother experience for devotees.

As per the latest buzz, On the other hand, Italy has once again caught the imagination of Indian moviegoers, and the credit partly goes to Cocktail 2 , starring Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon and Rashmika Mandanna. A significant portion of the movie's first half is set in picturesque Italian locations such as Catania, Noto, Siracusa, Castellammare del Golfo, Avola and Milan. These places have been beautifully captured on the big screen, giving viewers yet another reason to consider Italy for their next holiday.
In further updates, According to the Bombay Times report, Aloke Bajpai, Group CEO, ixigo, revealed, “ Since Cocktail 2 was rolled out, bookings on our site to and from Italy are up 38% YoY.”

On top of that, He further shared, “According to Great Indian Travel Index report, rolled out last year, YoY bookings on ixigo to cities across the Northeast grew sharply, Dimapur +77%, Agartala +48%, and Guwahati and Imphal +44% each, with shows like The Family Man helping bring these destinations into the spotlight. We are seeing the same internationally. Sicily, featured in The White Lotus, The Odyssey and Cocktail 2 , is a great example.”

The developments once again underline the influence of cinema beyond the ticket-window. While films can introduce audiences to destinations they may never have considered visiting, the growing popularity of these places also raises questions about whether local infrastructure is equipped to handle the sudden influx. Hanuman Ansh and Cocktail 2 are two contrasting examples of this phenomenon, showing how the magic of the movies can translate into real-world travel, economic opportunities and, at times, unexpected challenges.

title: Reporting Live review: Parineeti Chopra's investigative film has a story to tell, but little excitement to offer
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Hansal Mehta's Scoop is everything Reporting Live aspires to be. The basic premise is similar: a female journalist gets caught up in a mess while doing her job. There's a mafia/underworld track thrown in for good measure, too. But do the two measure up? For starters, Scoop had six episodes to flesh out its story and explore its characters, while Reporting Live has to wrap up everything in about two hours. That's a significant difference, but is it enough to explain the gap in their impact?

Adding to this, Reporting Live review: Parineeti Chopra in a still from the investigative crime thriller. The premise Directed by Dhruv Tripathi, Reporting Live revolves around Sandhya (Parineeti Chopra), a journalist waiting for her first primetime scoop. Her team includes video journalist Vinod (Deven Bhojani). When a bridge collapses in Visargao, sending a bus plunging into the river and claiming 15 lives, the incident is dismissed as an accident. But Sandhya and Vinod stumble upon a darker truth: illegal sand mining and its connection to the bridge collapse. How the duo navigates threats to their lives and careers to bring the truth to light forms the rest of the plot.

Meanwhile, What Reporting Live gets right is its pace. Initially, there's rarely a dull moment as we are introduced to Sandhya's workplace, helmed by characters played by Adil Hussain and Shekhar Suman. Being a journalist myself, I found the newsroom atmosphere particularly relatable. There's no unnecessary glamourisation of the profession (a la Alia Bhatt's Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani ). Instead, the movie is closer to No One Killed Jessica , at least in its depiction of the round-the-clock stress that comes with the job.

Notably, But that's about it. The story is decidedly predictable, with the reason behind Sandhya's boss suppressing the sand-mining expose becoming apparent well before it should. The writing by Mihir Jadhav and Dhruv Tripathi does have its tender moments, particularly in depicting the bond between Sandhya and Vinod. The actors deserve credit for bringing warmth to their equation. However, the movie misses out on the very thing its premise promises: the thrill and tension of an investigation that puts everything at stake.

As per the latest buzz, The antagonist, played by Nasser, is another case of the familiar taking precedence over the unexpected. In the OTT age, when viewers have access to stories from across the world, predictability can be poison. The background score doesn't help matters either, lacking the punch required to heighten the tension and becoming repetitive after a point.

In further updates, Performance-wise, Parineeti Chopra does a decent job, while Deven Bhojani is wonderful, making you genuinely feel for his character. Shekhar Suman fits the role of the cunning businessman perfectly. Adil Hussain, meanwhile, has an effortless likeability about him.

On top of that, Ultimately, Reporting Live is a case of a promising premise let down by predictable writing. The brisk pace and solid performances make it watchable, but the movie never quite builds the tension its subject demands. If Scoop showed how a journalist's pursuit of a story could make for compelling drama, Reporting Live is content with merely telling one. In a story about journalists chasing the truth, that's a rather underwhelming scoop.

Rishabh Suri is an Assistant Editor, movie critic, and professional overthinker of plot points. He writes for HT City, keeping pace with an industry where news cycles expire long before the popcorn gets cold. He completed his graduation in English Honours from Kirori Mal College, followed by a Master’s degree in English Literature-effectively training his brain to over-analyse classic texts before applying those exact same skills to 3-hour Bollywood blockbusters. He got into the profession when he had barely graduated from college and has been at HT ever since. At HT, Rishabh reviews films with a simple rule: skip the dense academic jargon and get straight to the point. Beyond reviews, as Assistant Editor, he helps navigate the broader circus of showbiz, tracking everything from OTT shifts to sudden ticket-window panics. In a beat driven by loud PR machinery and carefully scripted answers, Rishabh prefers cutting through the noise to focus on how stories get made and why trends shift. When he isn’t writing against a deadline, he is usually sitting in a dark theater, compulsively memorising dialogues. title: Kala Hiran case: Delhi HC seeks Salman Khan's response to application, says court lacks territorial jurisdiction
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Delhi High Court on Friday issued notice in an application filed by the producer of Kala Hiran: Battle for Legacy, seeking rejection of Bollywood star Salman Khan ’s suit seeking a stay on the movie’s rollout, on the ground that the court lacks territorial jurisdiction.

Adding to this, A still from Hiran: Battle for Legacy. What's the latest in the case? A bench of Justice Tejas Karia sought Salman Khan’s response to producer Amit Jani’s application and listed the matter for further hearing on December 16.

Meanwhile, This was after Jani’s lawyer argued that neither Khan nor his client resided or carried on business within high court’s territorial jurisdiction, since Khan resides in Mumbai, while Jani in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.

Notably, He submitted that the mere availability of the movie’s teasers, posters and other promotional material across the country, including Delhi, was insufficient to confer territorial jurisdiction on the court.

As per the latest buzz, The application further shared that the plaint does not allege that the movie or its promotional material specifically targeted audiences in Delhi or that Khan suffered any distinct injury within the national capital.

In further updates, In his suit, Salman painted a picture that the producer had repeatedly and publicly admitted by the producer, that the movie is based on him and the criminal proceedings arising from the blackbuck incident in October 1998 and even the impugned promotional material unmistakably portrayed him, through his name, likeness, mannerisms, distinctive personal attributes, iconic films and widely publicised events associated with him.

On top of that, It added that staging a dramatised trial when he had been acquitted in three of the four cases arising from the incident and during the pendency of his appeals and special leave petitions before the Rajasthan high court and the Supreme Court, infringed his fundamental right to fair trial.
The suit further shared that the teasers and promotional material expressly, as well as by innuendo, convey that he is guilty of offences that are still sub judice.

title: SC rejects plea for independent probe into CJP's July protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Notably, A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard the matter involving a plea concerning the investigation into FIRs registered in connection with the protests at Jantar Mantar.

title: Tanushree Dutta doubles down on ‘evil dead’ remark for Nana Patekar: ‘Does a person stop being an abuser when they die?’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nana Patekar died in the early hours of October 8 in Goa at the age of 75 from a cardiac arrest. Tanushree Dutta , who had accused the star years ago of sexual harassment on a movie set, made an ‘evil dead’ remark after his death. Even as the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) condemned the star for making such a comment, Tanushree doubled down on it on her social media.

Adding to this, Tanushree Dutta hopes that her life is in track for better things after Nana Patekar's death. Tanushree Dutta doubles down on ‘evil dead’ remark on Nana Patekar After attending an event in Lucknow, Tanushree wrote on her Instagram Stories that her engagement has increased since news broke of Nana’s death. Without naming him, she wrote, “This is insane! My story timeline has exploded today. Evil is dead and my life is hopefully on track for better things!”

Meanwhile, In another post, Tanushree alluded to the abuse she alleged Nana had committed. She re-put up a post written by Sandhya Mridul, which read: “Does a person stop being an abuser when they die? Does the harm they caused disappear too? For survivors, it doesn't.” She also reshared a video recounting how she refused to do an unscripted intimate step with Nana, and was only attacked for it. Tanushree also filed police complaints and with the artist association, but no action was taken.
Notably, One video that Tanushree reshared on her Instagram Stories features a content creator slamming people for calling Nana a ‘legend’, forgetting the sexual harassment allegations against him.

As per the latest buzz, On Thursday, after news broke of Nana’s death, Tanushree posted videos of her boarding a flight to Lucknow for an event. In a video, she shared, “Maine suna hai, I have heard the news. I just… today is my workday. I am going to Lucknow for an event. And I want to focus on that. What an odd day for all this to happen."

In further updates, She also added, "Because I’m doing a very big event in Lucknow, and it was pretty important for me. I had my entire day planned out. I wanted to do all these Lives and post content. And now I’m worried that in the evening, that’s all the media is going to be interested in is evil dead. So, I will give my reaction once I figure out what kind of reaction I should have. So, definitely condolences to the family but...” and her video cut off midway.

On top of that, AICWA Founder and President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta issued a strongly worded statement criticising her reaction. “At such a time, Tanushree Dutta's statement on social media, in which she used the words 'Evil Dead', is deeply objectionable, insensitive and shameful. AICWA strongly condemns it,” read a portion of his statement.

Tanushree accused Nana of sexual harassment on the set of the 2009 movie Horn 'Ok' Pleassss. In 2018, during the Me Too movement, the claim became public. An FIR was registered against Nana, who denied the allegations. In 2019, the case was closed for lack of sufficient evidence. In 2025, the Mumbai Andheri Magistrate Court officially dismissed the criminal proceedings against Nana because the complaint was filed beyond the legal limitation period.
