title: No permission for Jantar Mantar protest, Delhi Police say CJP's intimation came 'too late'
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Delhi Police on Friday shared they denied permission for the proposed October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), citing the short notice given by the organisers, their previous instances of violating their undertakings and not following lawful directions during the previous protest at the site. Delhi Police cited the prevailing public order, safety, traffic and law and order situation as key reasons behind the decision.

Adding to this, Security tightened, barricades put up at Jantar Mantar, Tolstoy Marg and Janpath areas, in view of a call for protest by the CJP on October 10, in New Delhi. (ANI Video Grab) In a press conference held at the Delhi Police headquarters, joint commissioner of police (New Delhi Range) Nupur Prasad shared that on October 7, the New Delhi police district received an application from CJP’s co-convenor Saurav Das, intimating that they will be holding a protest at protest at Jantar Mantar regarding accountability of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) on October 10.

Meanwhile, Prasad shared that the police examined the intimation letter and found that the information was received on very short notice. According to the current guidelines, she shared, an application for organising at event at Jantar Mantar is required to be submitted at least 10 days before the scheduled date of the event.

Notably, “It is also relevant to mention that, as per the past conduct of the CJP, their undertakings given on previous occasions and lawful directions were not followed. Keeping in view the non-compliance with the prescribed procedure, instances of non-compliance with laws and guidelines in the past as well, and the prevailing public order, safety and security, law and order and traffic situation, permission for the proposed sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar is not being granted,” shared joint CP Prasad.

As per the latest buzz, She reiterated that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) are already in force in the New Delhi area, under which reasonable preventive restrictions have been imposed to maintain public order and safety.

In further updates, “It is further informed that if anyone is found violating section 163 of the BNSS or is involved in vandalism and destruction of public property, appropriate legal action will be taken as per the previous directions of the courts,” she shared.

On top of that, The denial of the permission for the proposed CJP protests came amid the ongoing demonstrations by multiple opposition parties, including the Congress Party, students organisations, and civil society activists, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process of the electoral rolls.

The Delhi Police have already beefed up security arrangements across the city, especially in central Delhi areas, for the protests and while additional deployment of security personnel are being made for the proposed CJP’s protest at Jantar Mantar which already have received support from multiple organisations.

title: Katrina Kaif responds to trolls bodyshaming her, says she won't let social media narrative ‘paralyse’ her: 'Have to be your own cheerleader'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Katrina Kaif has addressed the mean comments and remarks she gets about her appearance on social media for the first time in a while. The star’s recent statement comes barely weeks after her recent public appearance drew unsanitary and mean remarks on her postpartum body. Speaking at an event for her brand in London, Katrina did not directly address the trolling but clarified that she does not let that affect her day-to-day life.

Adding to this, Katrina Kaif was of late bodyshamed when she attended the Ambanis' Ganpati celebrations. Katrina Kaif on social media trolling On Thursday, Katrina attended a public event in London to celebrate the first-year anniversary of her cosmetics brand, Kay By Katrina, in partnership with Space NK. Here, she spoke about being authentic and how she handles criticism and mean comments on social media. Videos from the event have since surfaced on social media. In one, Katrina shared, “I think we really need to be careful in letting the narrative on social media affect our self-worth. If we start trying to cater to all of them, I think that really hampers your ability to make choices for yourself. Personally, if every time I face critique or comments, I let that dictate my actions, I think I would have been paralysed with fear and unable to move ahead in my life.”

Meanwhile, Later in the event, while responding to a question, the star added, “There are times when the world is going to celebrate you and other times when you have to be your own biggest cheerleader.”

Notably, Katrina also linked this mantra to her brand's tagline. Drawing the parallel, she added, “That's really the thinking behind Kay Beauty's tagline 'It's kay to be you'. That is, you accept yourself and are true to who you are in this moment. And that's going to change day to day and in different phases in your life. There are times when you are acing everything in life, and other times when you can't get anything right. There are times when you are looking and feeling the best version of yourself, and other times when you are on a journey to get there. I think it's good to wear it all lightly and not to take yourself too seriously.”

title: Pakistani cricketer Basit Ali recalls friendship with Nana Patekar, shares how he supported him after mother's death: ‘He was a wonderful human being’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nana Patekar , one of Indian cinema's most recognisable actors, died at the age of 75 on October 8 after cardiac arrest. The veteran star was rushed to the hospital but he could not be revived. The news has left followers mourning the veteran performer, whose career spanned nearly five decades and included some of Hindi and Marathi cinema's most memorable films. Tributes have also come in from Pakistan, where the star had a strong following.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar dies at 75: Pakistan cricketers Umar Akmal and Basit Ali remember the veteran star. Pakistani cricketer Umar Akmal remembered Nana in a social media post, while former cricketer Basit Ali shared memories of his personal bond with the star. Basit spoke about a friendship that began in 1994 and lasted for years, recalling how Nana checked on him and his family during difficult times.

Meanwhile, Basit Ali shared a video after hearing the news of the death of the star. The news brought back years of memories. The former Pakistan cricketer recalled first in conversation with Nana in 1994 and described him as someone who remained in touch long after their initial meeting.

Notably, “Early in the morning I heard sad news. Our very dear brother, friend, and living legend is no longer in this world—Nana Patekar Sahab has passed away. What a person he was; he acted in movies exactly as he was in real life. We had nicknamed Latif as 'Nana'. Because of Nana Patekar, we first talked back in 1994, and it all started from there,” Basit shared.

As per the latest buzz, He remembered how Nana regularly checked on his family, particularly when his mother was in hospital. He shared the star continued to offer support after her death and reached out again when Ali faced health problems of his own.

In further updates, “Now there are so many memories. Usually, we spoke once or twice every month. When my mother was alive and in the hospital, Nana Ji called every week. He offered many prayers, talked at length with my mother, and listened to old stories. When my mother passed away, he told me, ‘Hey Basit, take care of yourself now’. And when I had my heart issue and returned home, I received a message asking about my health and telling me to call when I felt better. When I called him back, he inquired about how everything went, including the stent placement,” he added.

On top of that, Basit recalled their conversations about the star's films and the easy familiarity they shared, including the moments when Nana would jokingly dismiss his questions about particular scenes. “He was such a wonderful human being. For people who only knew him through movies, he was the exact same person in real life as well. People lauded him, and we were fortunate to have many conversations. Sometimes we would ask him about a specific scene in a movie, and he would playfully say, ‘Shut up, what do you know?’. The love and affection he gave as an elder was truly incredible,” he shared.

He also spoke about how difficult it was to accept the news, recalling that he often called Nana a 'young man' because the star did not seem his age. He shared Patekar enjoyed considerable affection among Pakistani audiences, just as he did in India and elsewhere.

title: Varun Dhawan invests in Shark Tank India's Better Nutrition, joins PV Sindhu as ambassador for biofortified food brand
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Varun Dhawan is stepping into the nutrition space with an investment in Better Nutrition, a brand that focuses on making everyday food more nutritious which featured on Shark Tank India Season 4 . The Bollywood star has also been named its brand ambassador, joining badminton star PV Sindhu. The partnership has a personal connection for Varun, who of late acquired agricultural land and is now working with the company to turn his farm into a biofortified one.

Adding to this, Varun Dhawan invests in Better Nutrition. Varun Dhawan takes his interest in farming a step further Varun Dhawan's interest in Better Nutrition comes from his own experience with farming. After acquiring agricultural land, the star began learning more about the soil, seeds and the food grown on his farm. This experience got him thinking about the connection between farming practices and the nutritional value of the food we eat every day.

Meanwhile, Now, his farm will be developed as a biofortified farm in collaboration with Better Nutrition. The move will allow him to explore the process more closely while supporting the company's efforts to improve the nutritional quality of everyday staples in India.

Notably, Talking about the partnership, the star shared in a note to afaqs, “We're working together to make my farm biofortified. And yeah, Better Nutrition is my brand now too. I really like the mission behind it, and I want to be part of that journey. You'll be seeing a lot more of me with my brand. So this is quite personal for me.”

As per the latest buzz, On his Instagram account, the star shared a video from this farm and wrote, “ So… turns out farming was only the beginning. 😄🌱 I realised nutrition could be a bigger part of the journey. After Prateek and Aishwarya at Better Nutrition reached out, I was inspired to take this farm on its own journey, as well as become an integral part of the brand itself to provide india BETTER NUTRITION.”

In further updates, View this post on Instagram What is Better Nutrition brand about? Better Nutrition sells everyday staples such as flour, dal, rice and millets. The company says its products can contain up to twice the levels of iron, zinc and other essential micronutrients found in conventional varieties.

On top of that, Its approach begins at the farm, using biofortified seeds and soil science to improve the nutritional content of crops. The company also uses X-ray fluorescence (XRF) technology to measure mineral levels in crops at the farm level. This helps it track nutrient content and check quality as the produce moves through the process.

Prateek Rastogi, co-founder and CEO of Better Nutrition, shared that the idea behind the brand is to make nutritious food a part of people's regular diets, rather than something they have to seek out separately.

title: ‘Deeply saddened Shakti Shalini will be his last film’: Director Aditya Sarpotdar remembers Nana Patekar
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nana Patekar was an integral part of the Hindi movie industry for close to 50 years. Over the last four decades, there has hardly been a year when a movie featuring the veteran star has not been rolled out in theatres. That run will come to an end with Shakti Shalini, the late star's final movie.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday morning at age 75. (HT_PRINT) Shakti Shalini director on Nana Patekar Hours after Nana's death, the movie's director, Aditya Sarpotdar , shared he was ‘deeply saddened’ that his movie would be Nana's last and spoke about his memories with the acclaimed artiste. “I never expected that Shakti Shalini will be his last movie. I'm deeply saddened that this will be his last work. I never thought that he would suddenly step away in this way. I'm unable to process what has actually happened. It (movie) is going to be a tribute to one of the best actors of our cinema,” Aditya told PTI on phone from Berlin.
Meanwhile, Shakti Shalini, the next title of Maddock Films' popular horror comedy universe, will posthumously feature Nana alongside Aneet Padda of Saiyaara fame.

Notably, According to Sarpotdar, Nana Patekar had spoken to him about 10 days ago, seeking an update on the movie's post-production, and was looking forward to watching the movie. “For him, the script was the most important thing. If he liked the script, he would do the movie; if not, then he wouldn't. I had written those two films keeping him in mind, and there's no replacement for him in Marathi cinema. He wasn't excited about it (movie), and hence it didn't happen,” the director shared.

As per the latest buzz, Shakti Shalini, produced by Dinesh Vijan via his banner Maddock Films, is as per reports expected to arrive in theatres in March 2027. Before this, Nana will be seen in two other films. The star will first be seen in the Shraddha Kapoor-starrer Eetha, slated for rollout in December 2026, and director Anant Mahadevan's The Confession of Mary.

In further updates, Nana Patekar died in Goa on the morning of October 8. He was 75. The star’s son, Malhar Patekar, verified to local media about his death. Nana was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, and was rushed to Manipal Hospital. The star was declared dead at around 5:20 am, with doctors citing a heart attack as the cause of death. Nana was cremated at his farmhouse in Pune later in the day.

On top of that, A three-time National Award-winning star, Nana is regarded as one of the finest actors in Indian cinema history. His passing drew tributes from across Indian cinema and public life, including tributes from Prime Minister Modi and several Chief Ministers.

title: Film workers' body slams Tanushree Dutta for her ‘evil dead’ remark on Nana Patekar’s death: ‘Should have kept a check on your tongue’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Tanushree Dutta has come under fire from the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) over her reaction to the death of veteran star Nana Patekar . The star posted a video on social media on Thursday in which she appeared to use the phrase “evil dead” while referring to the news. AICWA has now hit back at her choice of words, accusing her of being insensitive at a time when the movie industry is paying tribute to the veteran star.

Adding to this, Tanushree Dutta criticized for her 'evil dead' remark on Nana Patekar's death. Nana died in the early hours of Thursday after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. Doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes, but he could not be saved and was declared dead at approximately 5:10 am. A medico-legal case has been registered. Goa Police has also registered an Unnatural Death (UD) case under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

Meanwhile, AICWA Founder and President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta issued a strongly worded statement criticising Dutta’s reaction. The association shared, "AICWA strongly condemns Tanushree Dutta's ‘Evil Dead’ remark on the passing of legend Nana Patekar," and accused her of using the moment for cheap publicity.

Notably, The association also spoke about Nana's contributions beyond acting, citing his Padma Shri and his work with the Naam Foundation, which supports the families of distressed farmers. It also mentioned his service during the Kargil War while remembering his contribution to the country.

As per the latest buzz, Offering condolences to his family, AICWA questioned the timing and tone of Dutta’s video. "At such a time, Tanushree Dutta's statement on social media, in which she used the words 'Evil Dead', is deeply objectionable, insensitive and shameful. AICWA strongly condemns it," the statement read.

In further updates, View this post on Instagram ‘You should have kept a check on your tongue’ The association argued that making such remarks following a person’s death went against "basic humanity" and called for greater sensitivity during a period of mourning. A part of the caption of the AICWA post read, “To use such words for a person after his death goes against basic humanity. Until today, no one in our movie industry has made such a statement after someone’s passing. You are the first, and we pray you will be the last. People in this industry know what to say on such an occasion and when to stay silent. You should have kept a check on your tongue."

On top of that, AICWA also took issue with Dutta mentioning her soon-to-release professional commitments in the video. "You shared that today is your work day, that you are going to Lucknow for a big event, and that your whole day is planned. Do your work; nobody asked you. Whether your event is in Lucknow or London, whether you focus or not, nobody is interested. On a day when the country is mourning the loss of a stalwart, speaking about your own event and your own plans reflects a very small mindset," AICWA shared.

In her Instagram video, Tanushree shared she had heard the news about Nana but wanted to focus on an event in Lucknow. She also suggested that media attention could shift towards "evil dead" by the evening. "I will give my reaction once I figure out what kind of reaction I should have. So, definitely condolences to the family but…" she shared before the clip cut off mid-sentence.

title: Goa Police registers ‘unnatural death’ case in Nana Patekar's death, to begin investigation
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Panaji Police has registered an Unnatural Death (UD) case under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) following the death of veteran star Nana Patekar . The 75-year-old star died at his residence in Goa on Thursday morning after a cardiac arrest.

Adding to this, Rangoli artist Shreehari Pavale works on a rangoli portrait paying tribute to veteran star Nana Patekar, in Vashi, Navi Mumbai, Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (PTI) Goa Police lodges case, to probe Nana's death According to the police record, the National Award-winning star was brought dead to the casualty ward of Manipal Hospital, Bambolim, from his residence at Ocean Park, Dona Paula. ANI reported that further enquiry into the matter is currently in progress, led by PSI Nitin Naik.

Meanwhile, The filing of a police case in Nana's death is a routine matter, as he died at his home alone and was brought dead to the hospital. The police register an unnatural death case in such matters to rule out any foul play. In this instance, it was done after the hospital filed a report with the police.

Notably, Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, had told ANI on Thursday, “They shifted him to our hospital at around 4:20 or 4:30 am. We also tried our best, but he was brought dead. Then we had to file a police case because there's an MLC (medico-legal case).”

As per the latest buzz, Nana Patekar was cremated with full state honours at his Donje farmhouse in Pune on Thursday night. His body was flown in from Goa on Thursday evening. Thousands of followers turned up at the farmhouse to pay their final respects to the late star.

In further updates, After performing the last rites, Nana Patekar's son Malhar Patekar spoke to the media and shared, “A person like Nana Saheb never truly leaves us; his achievements have made him immortal. Secondly, he always believed that everyone should come together and follow a righteous path on a global scale. Thirdly, regarding the future--carrying forward the vision Nana Saheb left behind is how we will shape the life ahead.”

On top of that, The funeral was attended by several political bigwigs and actors. However, many from Bollywood could not attend as the last rites were performed very late into the night on Thursday. Explaining the decision, Malhar Patekar told reporters, “We were in Goa, and his mortal remains were to be brought to the farmhouse in the village. We expected it to arrive earlier, but it took us some time. We proceeded (with the last rites today) because the tragedy occurred early this morning, so a significant amount of time had already passed. That is why we decided to go ahead with it today.”
Nana, 75, is survived by his wife, Neelkanthi Patekar and son, Malhar.

title: Amitabh Bachchan pauses KBC shoot to pay tribute to ‘incomparable’ Nana Patekar, recalls his social work: ‘A respectful bow to your art’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Amitabh Bachchan joined the legion of Bollywood celebrities and public figures who paid tribute to the late Nana Patekar on Thursday. The veteran star died at the age of 75 on Thursday morning at his residence in Goa, and was later cremated with full state honours at his farmhouse in Pune.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan hosted Nana Patekar on KBC 16 a couple of years ago. Amitabh Bachchan pays special tribute to Nana Patekar On Thursday night, Sony TV shared a video of Amitabh, filmed on the sets of his game show Kaun Banega Crorepati , where the star spoke about Nana's demise and his memories. In the emotional tribute to his close friend, Big B fondly remembered his candour, simplicity and commitment to social causes.

Meanwhile, Amitabh described Nana as an "adwitiya kalakar" (incomparable artist), friend, well-wisher and an exceptional social worker. He shared his passing was a loss not only to the Indian movie industry but also to everyone who had known him.

Notably, "His outspokenness, his simplicity, and his courage to speak the truth and call a spade a spade are some of the qualities that set him apart from others. Some people leave our lives, but their voice, their philanthropy, and the lessons they taught remain within us. Nana was one of those people," Amitabh shared in the video.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by sonytvofficial (@sonytvofficial)

In further updates, The two celebrated actors worked together on the 1999 action thriller movie, Kohram, directed by Mehul Kumar. Remembering his co-star and friend, Amitabh added, “A personal salute to you, Nana. And a respectful bow to your art, which you lived with complete honesty and dedication,”

On top of that, The KBC host recalled Nana's appearance on season 16, when the star participated in a special episode and donated his prize money to social work. “His words not only inspired us, but the noble cause to which he dedicated his prize money was a true example of his community service. He connected with the farmers of the Maharashtra villages suffering due to inadequate rainfall and personally helped them,” he shared. Concluding his tribute, Amitabh Bachchan offered heartfelt condolences to Patekar's family on behalf of the entire KBC team.

In a career spanning around five decades, Nana Patekar worked across Hindi and Marathi cinema and was known as one of the foremost Indian actors of his generation. A three-time National Award winner, Nana worked in both acclaimed independent films and commercial blockbusters, earning a name for himself with performances in films such as Krantiveer, Parinda, Agni Sakshi, Khamoshi: The Musical, Ab Tak Chhappan, Natsamrat and Welcome.

title: ‘My friend has left me’: Emotional Anil Kapoor remembers ‘world’s biggest artiste' Nana Patekar in tribute
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Welcome's Majnu bhai, Anil Kapoor , shared a touching tribute to his on-screen brother and real-life friend Nana Patekar on Thursday evening. Nana died in Goa on Thursday morning after a cardiac arrest, and was cremated with full state honours in Pune later in the day.

Adding to this, Anil Kapoor and Nana Patekar worked together in Welcome apart from many other films. Anil Kapoor mourns Nana Patekar's death On Thursday evening, Anil Kapoor posted on Instagram to share an emotional tribute for his friend and co-star. In the heartfelt Instagram post, Anil Kapoor affectionately called Patekar "nanya", referring to him as the world's biggest artist. Equating Nana's death to the loss of another star friend, Satish Kaushik, Anil wrote, “Mera dost mujhe chhodkar chala gaya... pehle Satish aur ab mera Nanya. NANYA, tu achanak bohot jaldi chala gaya... Duniya ka sabse bada kalakaar, humein chhodkar hamesha-hamesha ke liye chala gaya (My friend has left me. First Satish and now Nanya. Nanya, you left so suddenly and so soon. The world's biggest artiste has left us forever).”

Meanwhile, Bidding an emotional farewell to his friend, Kapoor shared that he would miss Nana in his life, on movie sets, and on the big screen. "Bohot miss karunga tujhe, life mein, set par, phone par aur bade parde par," the star concluded. Along with his post, Anil Kapoor also shared a picture of himself with the late star.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by anilskapoor (@anilskapoor)

As per the latest buzz, Nana Patekar and Anil Kapoor were longtime friends. The two actors first worked together in Vidhu Vinod Chopra's 1989 movie Parinda, which collected Nana his first National Award. The two actors collaborated in many films after that, including as the beloved Uday and Majnu duo in Anees Bazmee's 2007 hit Welcome, before reprising their roles in the sequel, Welcome Back. Their chemistry and comedy timing in the comedies collected them praise and love.

In further updates, Nana Patekar passed away after suffering a severe cardiac arrest in Goa. He was taken to Manipal Hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes, but he could not be saved. Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, verified the news to ANI.

On top of that, Since the news came out, tributes have been pouring in across social media platforms, with actors, members of the movie fraternity, politicians, and followers remembering Patekar's legacy.

The late star's last rites were performed at his farmhouse, affectionately known as Nanachi Wadi, in Donje village near Khadakwasla, Pune, late on Thursday night in the presence of senior political leaders and thousands of followers.

title: Why were Nana Patekar's last rites performed at almost midnight, son Malhar Patekar reveals
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

(Pic - Mahendra Kolhe / HT) Malhar Patekar on Nana's legacy After the funeral, Malhar Patekar spoke to reporters present outside the farmhouse and addressed his father's death. He shared his father’s work had made him immortal and that his vision, particularly his social initiatives through the Naam Foundation, would be carried forward even after his demise.

Secondly, his mindset was always consistent; he would frequently repeat the line, 'Let's get together in the name of humanity and work for the betterment of the world.' Through our organisation, work was already underway in the water sector, and large-scale initiatives in education and health had begun in Kashmir as well. Thirdly, he assigned specific responsibilities to everyone before he left.”

Notably, Nana Patekar died in Goa on Thursday morning after a cardiac arrest. His body was flown to his farmhouse in Goa later in the day, where the funeral began very late into the night. The reporters asked Malhar why the family decided to go ahead with the funeral that late on Thursday. “We were in Goa, and his mortal remains were to be brought to the farmhouse in the village. We expected it to arrive earlier, but it took us some time. We proceeded (with the last rites today) because the tragedy occurred early this morning, so a significant amount of time had already passed. That is why we decided to go ahead with it today,” he responded.

As per the latest buzz, Nana Patekar died after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa on Thursday morning. The star called his friend in the wee hours of Thursday after feeling uneasy. He was taken to Manipal Hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes. title: Rajkummar Rao responds to criticism for poster of Sourav Ganguly biopic Dada: ‘Ones who made it learnt their lesson’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Rajkummar Rao is busy promoting his soon-to-release courtroom drama Prahaar: The Ujjwal Nikam Story, which hits the screens on October 16. He spoke about the Sourav Ganguly biopic, Dada, during the movie’s promotions and shared an anecdote about his interaction with the former cricketer. When asked about the movie’s poster receiving criticism, Rajkummar remarked that the team has ‘learnt the lesson’ not to rush things.

Adding to this, Rajkummar Rao will essay Sourav Ganguly in the biopic titled Dada. Rajkummar Rao on meeting Sourav Ganguly On Mashable India, Rajkummar opened up about shooting for Dada and shared, “I have met Sourav Ganguly many times and have even shot at his home and at Eden Gardens. We were in Kolkata for a while, and I have spent a lot of time with Dada. We have discussed a lot of things. We have also discussed things that I cannot reveal now, because it’s important to know personal things to understand a person's mind. He was very open about it; he laid his life bare before me. We all love him; he’s a legend. He laid the foundation for what the Indian team is today.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by RajKummar Rao (@rajkummar_rao)

Notably, On Sourav’s birthday on July 8, the makers of Dada rolled out a poster that saw Rajkummar recreating an iconic moment. The star waved an Indian flag in the poster, shirtless and wearing blue pants. However, many thought the poster was poorly made or AI-generated. Acknowledging the criticism, Rajkummar shared, “The ones who made the poster have understood, they have learnt their lesson. They have understood they need to take their time and not rush things; there’s no hurry. I think the team has learned its lesson. But they have also understood that dada’s fan following is crazy.”

title: Drishyam 3 box office collection day 7: Ajay Devgn film nears ₹250 crore mark in first week, beats Drishyam 2 lifetime haul
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 7 : It is Drishyam 3 fever at the ticket-window. After a bumper opening at the ticket-window, Ajay Devgn ’s crime thriller witnessed an expected drop in collections on Monday. But the movie remained rock steady during the week, and crossed the ₹ 200 crore rupees mark in five days of rollout. As the movie closes on its first week, let us take a look at its ticket-window performance.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 7: Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar in the movie. Drishyam 3 week 1 report card For Ajay Devgn, Drishyam 3 registered the biggest opening of his career. The advance bookings for Drishyam The Conclusion opened on September 27, and the movie went on to collect ₹ 27 crore rupees before its rollout. By the end of the day, the movie went on to collect ₹ 66.75 crore rupees net across India. This is the third biggest opening by a Hindi movie ever and the biggest in Ajay Devgn’s career. On Saturday, the movie collected ₹ 53.50 crore rupees, and showed huge growth on Sunday, bringing in ₹ 61 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, The first dip started on Monday, when the movie collected ₹ 21 crore rupees, around 65.6% lower than its Sunday figure. The decline continued on Tuesday, when Drishyam 3 collected ₹ 19.50 crore rupees, and on Wednesday with ₹ 15.50 crore rupees. The latest update on Sacnilk states that Drishyam 3 collected ₹ 13 crore rupees. This brings the total net collection to ₹ 245.50 crore rupees . Drishyam 3 has now surpassed the lifetime haul of Drishyam 2, which had collected ₹ 239.67 crore rupees net in India.

Notably, It is now eyeing the record set by Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior. The 2020 historical drama remains Ajay's highest-grossing movie, with a lifetime collection of ₹ 279.59 crore rupees in net collection.

As per the latest buzz, Drishyam 3 brings back Ajay Devgn’s Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also reprises his role from the second part in a cameo.

In further updates, Drishyam The Conclusion is backed by Star Studio18 and Panorama Studios, with Abhishek Pathak returning to direct the third instalment. He has also co-written the movie with Aamil Keeyan Khan and Parveez Shaikh. Alok Jain, Ajit Andhare, Kumar Mangat Pathak and Abhishek Pathak are producing the movie.

On top of that, The Hindi Drishyam franchise began in 2015 with the remake of Mohanlal’s Malayalam thriller. The movie quickly won over audiences and went on to collect around ₹ 110 crore rupees worldwide, making Vijay Salgaonkar a fan-favourite. Drishyam 2, which arrived in 2022, took the franchise a step further and turned out to be an even bigger hit, grossing nearly ₹ 342 crore rupees worldwide.

title: Gauahar Khan sells Versova duplex for Rs 6.01 crores, bought it for Rs 3.2 crores in 2014
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:
The property recorded an appreciation of around 88%, with the transaction registered on September 24, 2026.

Adding to this, The property transaction was registered on September 24, 2026. The apartment is located in Versova Shiv Kutir Co-operative Housing Society Ltd., situated in S.V.P. Nagar, Versova, Andheri West. The duplex occupies two floors of the building and is positioned on a higher floor.

Meanwhile, As per the registration documents, the property has a super built-up area of 2,340 sq ft (217.47 sq m), while its built-up area measures 1,872 sq ft (173.98 sq m). The documents do not mention any car parking being included in the transaction.

Notably, The duplex was sold for a consideration value of Rs 6.01 crores, with the purchasers paying Rs 36.06 lakhs as stamp duty. Khan had acquired the apartment for Rs 3.2 crores in November 2014. This means the recorded consideration value increased by Rs 2.81 crores during the period, translating into an appreciation of nearly 88% on the original purchase price.

As per the latest buzz, Based on the latest consideration value and the built-up area of 1,872 sq ft, the transaction works out to approximately Rs 32,100 per sq ft. Calculated against the super built-up area of 2,340 sq ft, the rate comes to around Rs 25,700 per sq ft. These figures are based on the consideration value mentioned in the registration document.

In further updates, Versova and neighbouring Mumbai areas such as Juhu, Lokhandwala and Bandra have also witnessed several property deals involving movie and television personalities in recent years. In June 2024, Ronit Roy and his wife Neelam Roy purchased a 4,258 sq ft apartment in Lodha Versova for Rs 18.94 crores, with four car parking spaces included in the transaction.

On top of that, Randeep Hooda also purchased a 1,530 sq ft apartment in Bianca CHS, Versova, for Rs 5.63 crores, according to property registration documents reviewed by HT. The transaction was reported in June 2025.
More of late, Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma, along with family members, purchased multiple apartments in Godrej Skyshore, Versova, for more than Rs 43 crores in July 2026.

title: Mamata Banerjee may join CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Thursday shared she may join the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, as the INDIA bloc prepares to march to Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday.

Adding to this, Mamata Banerjee reached the residence of her nephew and Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee in Kolkata (ANI Video Grab) Banerjee reached the residence of her nephew and Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee in Kolkata. She is also expected to be part of a 10-member core team of INDIA bloc leaders that will meet President Droupadi Murmu on Friday to submit a memorandum against alleged mass disenfranchisement and demand Kumar’s ouster.

Meanwhile, “I may join the protest at Jantar Mantar scheduled for October 10, but nothing can be verified now. We have maintained a relationship with them (the CJP) and have extended our support, while any further decision regarding our participation will be taken later,” Banerjee shared in Kolkata.

Notably, Banerjee had played a key role in expediting the protest plans at the INDIA bloc meeting on September 29 and had collected Congress Parliamentary Party chief Sonia Gandhi’s support. She returned here as the CJP is set to start a dharna amid the INDIA bloc’s prolonged protests.

As per the latest buzz, When asked if she would join the CJP’s dharna at Jantar Mantar, Trinamool’s Rajya Sabha floor leader Derek O’Brien shared, “As you all know we support the CJP. We have good relationship with some of their leaders. We know Abhijeet Dipke for years. Ashutosh Ranka came to Kolkata and we had lunch. I am neither confirming nor denying if Mamata Banerjee will participate in the CJP protests.”

In further updates, While the Congress remains suspicious of the CJP and dubs it as an ally of Arvind Kejriwal’s Aam Aadmi Party, Trinamool and Shiv Sena (UBT) have extended olive branches to the new outfit. During the CJP’s protests against the exam paper leak, Banerjee sent five MPs to the CJP’s platform to express solidarity.

On top of that, “I was asked to go, so I am going... A request for an appointment with the President has been made for the 8th or 9th on behalf of the INDIA Alliance leaders; my name has been included in that list,” Banerjee shared.

INDIA bloc lawmakers will march from Parliament to Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday to meet President Droupadi over the raging issue of mass disenfranchisement through SIR. They will also demand Kumar’s ouster. The Rashtrapati Bhavan, however, has not yet finalised the Opposition’s appointment to meet Murmu, who was in Himachal Pradesh for the past three days.

title: ‘Modi may have power, but we have the streets’: CJP’s Dipke leads Bengaluru protest against SIR
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijit Dipke shared on Thursday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi “may have the power now, but we have the streets and we will reclaim our power from here,” as thousands gathered at Bengaluru’s Freedom Park to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Adding to this, Abhijit Dipke, Prakash Raj and Dhruv Rathee joined thousands at Bengaluru’s Freedom Park to protest SIR and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. (AP Photo/) At a “People’s Tribunal” organised by civil society groups and the CJP, Dipke alleged that the deletion of voters was being used to disenfranchise people opposed to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Meanwhile, The protest is witnessing a large Gen Z participation. The chants were punctuated by cries of “Inquilab Zindabad” and slogans demanding Kumar’s resignation.

Notably, Dipke shared people whose names had allegedly been recorded as belonging to deceased voters were present at the protest. “People who were declared dead are standing here alive. So the death that has taken place is not the death of these people. It is the death of the democracy of this country,” he shared.
As per the latest buzz, Dipke had also posted that “mass detentions being done before the 10 October protest in New Delhi. Modi thinks he can silence dissent by putting people behind bars.”
In further updates, “The more people you detain, the more people will show up!” Dipke warned.
On top of that, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and star-activist Prakash Raj addressed the gathering too.

Rathee questioned the alleged removal of 70 lakh voters in West Bengal before the elections and their subsequent addition to the rolls. He also questioned the deletion of more than 40 lakh names in Bihar and the subsequent disclosure of the names following a Supreme Court direction. “In UP, over 14 lakhs were ‘added’ suddenly. Who are these people? While in Goa, even though EROs wanted to add, ECI didn’t allow,” he shared.

title: Prasanna Bisht starrer Bokshi release postponed to December 4 after CBFC review over witchcraft and gruesome violence
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Bhargav Saikia’s folk-horror movie gets an ‘A’ certificate with minimal modifications after being referred to the Revising Committee.

Adding to this, Directed by Bhargav Saikia and written by debutant screenwriter and executive producer Harsh Vaibhav, Bokshi has now been cleared by the Revising Committee with an ‘A’ certificate and minimal modifications. The makers have decided to push the rollout to December to accommodate the certification-related delay and allow more time for a full-scale theatrical campaign.

Meanwhile, Lorien Motion Pictures revealed the revised rollout date on October 8, confirming that the folk-horror movie will now arrive in select cinemas across India on December 4. The production house shared an official statement explaining the decision. The statement read, "Due to its supernatural themes, depiction of witchcraft, and gruesome violence, BOKSHI was of late referred by the CBFC's Examining Committee to the Revising Committee for further review. We are thrilled to share that the Revising Committee has now cleared the movie with an "A" certificate with minimal modifications.

Notably, It further shared, “To ensure a seamless theatrical rollout, we have made the difficult decision to postpone the rollout of BOKSHI in India, originally set for 9 October 2026. We are working hard behind the scenes to bring you the movie in the best possible manner. We deeply appreciate our partners, media, content creators, and, above all, our audience for your patience and unwavering support. This is just a brief pause. BOKSHI will now rollout in select cinemas on 4 December 2026!"

As per the latest buzz, The movie’s trailer, rolled out a few weeks ago, has as per reports received an encouraging response, particularly among younger audiences and followers of horror and genre cinema. Bokshi blends folk-horror, coming-of-age elements and mystery, with its story following Anahita, a troubled teenager whose school trek to a remote prehistoric site leads her towards an ancient legend.
In further updates, The movie stars Prasanna Bisht, Mansi Multani and Siddharth Shaw in pivotal roles, while Shernaz Patel lends her voice to the titular character, Bokshi.

On top of that, Bokshi marks Bhargav Saikia’s feature directorial debut and is produced under the banner of Lorien Motion Pictures. The multilingual movie features Hindi, English and Nepali, along with Boksirit, a fictional language created specifically for the movie by Dutch linguist Jan van Steenbergen.

The movie premiered at the International Movie Festival Rotterdam in 2025 and has subsequently been showcased at several international genre movie festivals, including Sitges International Fantastic Movie Festival, Neuchâtel International Fantastic Movie Festival and SXSW Sydney.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

We shot his scenes in Mumbai rather than Chambal. We shot at JW Marriott, while he was also shooting for Vishal Bhardwaj's O Romeo. He had got his dabba and was eating it in between in conversation with me. He loved talking about food. He wrapped his portions in two-and half hours. He had to stand on a tall surface because we were to add VFX. He played a soldier and knew how to uncock the gun. He shared ‘yeh mujhe mat sikha main jaanta hoon’ and just did it quickly. "

Anil sir gave him cues for the shot though he was not needed there. That scene echoed in the climax and a lot of people reached out to me that they were surprised. title: Exclusive| Juhi Chawla: Nana Patekar was legendary in his own rustic way
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Juhi Chawla and Nana worked together in classic Bollywood films including Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992) and the delayed crime drama Gang (2000). She tells us, “I’m thinking of the times we spent together and feeling sad that somebody I worked with is no more. On the sets of Raju..I remember him as a unique presence and iconic star. His style of acting was so rooted and being senior I was always overawed by him. I remember him playing the dafli and singing the song Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman in the movie."

Adding to this, Juhi Chawla Speaking about Gang which took years to make she recalls, “It was fragmented shooting. I remember a scene that I was nervous about and he sat me down and gave me a long lecture on how to approach the scene. I remember sitting there intimidated and listening intently. ”

Meanwhile, Also sharing memories off screen she adds, “He had also invited us for Ganeshotsav at his house in Dadar during the 90s. I remember going to his simple home and his mother made sure we ate before we left. We sat on the floor and ate typical Maharashtrian food in thalis. Ofcourse I watched him in so many films, he was legendary in his own rustic way. He added so much colour and character to every movie. His presence was felt in each movie.”

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mahesh Manjrekar who directed the landmark 2016 Marathi drama movie Natsamrat, and had known Nana Pateka r since their theatre days tells us, “This is the biggest loss for me after my mother and father. We have lost Vikram Ghokhale and now Nana, the pillars of the Marathi movie industry. I cant believe he is no more, it’s a feeling I cant explain. I was looking forward to working with him again but couldn’t find a subject that could justify his talent."

Adding to this, Mahesh Manjrekar Recalling their days as newcomers in the industry he says, “I knew him for almost 42 years, having met during our theatre days. I remember we once visited his movie sets and considered him as the pride of Maharashtra even back then. Someone tried to shoo us away from the sets because we were not known back then and he lost his cool.”

Meanwhile, He adds that just a few days his wife Medha Manjrekar and he were planning to meet Nana . “He used to call her Sarkar (like he did in Natsamarat, the movie in which they acted together.) He was like family to us and would keep checking on Medha especially after she was diagnosed with cancer,” says Manjrekar.

title: Shah Rukh Khan mourns death of his friend and co-star Nana Patekar, recalls when he told him ‘don't lose the actor to become a hero’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan is mourning the death of his friend and co-star Nana Patekar . In a note he penned on Instagram on Thursday, he recalled how Nana once asked him not to lose the star in him while pursuing a career as a hero. Nana died on October 8 at the age of 75 in Goa due to a cardiac arrest. Shah Rukh’s eulogy for him came in the evening.
Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan and Nana Patekar first worked together in the 1992 movie Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman. (Follow live updates about Nana Patekar here )

Meanwhile, Shah Rukh posted a still with Nana from their 1992 movie Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman. He recalled shooting with him, writing, “When I first met him, out of awe and awkwardness I fiddled with my hair. He slapped my hand away and shared ‘hero ki tarah Baal mat bana...tu star hai’! (Stop fixing your hair like a hero, you’re an star).”

Notably, The star also wrote about Nana’s straightforward nature, “He didn’t flatter you. He didn’t tell you what you wanted to hear. He told you what you needed to hear. That was Nana. Straightforward. Rough, honest and had the most beautiful smile.” Shah Rukh added, “He always had a strange way of showing affection. He would shout at you first, and then somewhere between the third or fourth insult, you realised you were being hugged. He loved me and I loved him back.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shah Rukh Khan (@iamsrk)

In further updates, Shah Rukh further wrote about his relationship with Nana, “He was a mentor, a teacher, a critic and a friend who beat me and everyone else around him in carrom game after game and relished his victories,” adding, “Nana your intensity, laughter, madness and love will always stay with us. I just wish we had time to have more conversations, another argument, another cup of tea and a game of carrom.”

On top of that, The star wrote about how much he will miss his friend, “You have left a void not only in the world of cinema but in the hearts of all Indians and the world. All I can say is, I will miss you dearly and carry your words in my heart till the end of time....’hero banne ke chakar mein star mat khona’. (Don't lose the star to become a hero)” He ended his note with, “May your soul rest in peace Nana and Allah bless you. The Heavens will be blessed to have you... a masterful star and an unbeatable carrom champion. Love you and miss you dearly!! Too soon my Hero Star! RIP.”

After Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman, Nana and Shah Rukh worked together in 2002 for Shakti: The Power. It was their last movie together. Nana Patekar’s funeral will be held at his Pune farm on Thursday. His body is expected to have been brought there at 5 PM for a ‘darshan’ for followers.

title: Atul Kasbekar says Nana Patekar had prepared firewood for his own funeral with ‘spectacularly morbid humour’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nana Patekar died on October 8 at the age of 75 due to a cardiac arrest. Photographer Atul Kasbekar took to his Instagram on Thursday after the news broke to eulogise the star and share memories of him. In a poignant moment, he remembered how Nana had prepared firewood for his funeral with ‘morbid humour,’ telling the photographer he was keeping them dry so attendees wouldn’t cry at his cremation due to it.
Adding to this, Nana Patekar died at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa on Thursday. (ANI ) (Follow live updates about Nana Patekar here )

Meanwhile, Atul penned a long note on his Instagram and posted a monochrome photo of the star, writing, “Nana Saheb. What a man. What a loss. I shared a wonderfully warm relationship with Nana Patekar. We didn’t meet often, but whenever we did, it felt like we’d met yesterday.” He also called the star ‘Unpredictable. Intense. Fiercely individualistic.’

Notably, The photographer recalled meeting Nana at his Pune farm to shoot a photo for one of his series, and the feast he and his crew were served. “Every assistant, spot boy and driver was seated in his main dining area, with Nana Saheb personally walking around serving extra rotis and helpings of his famous mutton,” wrote Atul, adding, “No hierarchy. No fuss. Just extraordinary generosity from a man who could intimidate an entire movie set with one raised eyebrow.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Atul Kasbekar (@atulkasbekar)

In further updates, Atul then recalled Nana showing him around his property, including the gym where he pulled off a dozen tricep dips. “Stone cold. No warm-up. Show-off!” wrote the photographer of the video that had gone widely shared then. He then recalled seeing the firewood Nana had prepared for his own funeral.

On top of that, “And then, in a moment of spectacularly morbid humour, showed me a stack of firewood he’d prepared for his own funeral. He’d kept it dry, he explained, because wet wood smokes, and he didn’t want people crying at his funeral merely because the smoke got into their eyes! Only Nana Saheb could turn his own cremation into a comedy routine,” wrote Atul.
The photographer also wrote that the death of the star feels like a ‘punch in the guts’, adding, “Rest easy, Nana Saheb. There will never be another quite like you.”

title: Rhea Chakraborty launches ‘Caught Blushin’ with Staze Beauty, inspired by her viral The Traitors look
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Seeing an opportunity to turn that beauty moment into a product, Staze Beauty collaborated with Rhea to create and launch Caught Blushin’, a blush designed with Indian skin tones in mind. With a blendable, buildable formula, the blush delivers an effortless flush that can be customized from a subtle wash of colour to a more defined look. The launch marks the beginning of the Rhea x Staze makeup line, with more beauty products to follow as part of the collaboration.

Adding to this, The collaboration stems from a shared passion for makeup and beauty, bringing together Rhea’s personal approach to makeup and Staze’s expertise in creating high-performance, versatile products that fit seamlessly into everyday beauty routines.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the collaboration, Rhea Chakraborty shared, “Makeup is something that has always really excited me. I love experimenting with different looks, playing with colour and finding little things that make me feel good. Staze is a brand I’ve used and genuinely liked, so when my blush look got so much love, and people started recreating it, the idea of creating something together felt very natural.

Notably, When I first spoke to Saahil about the collaboration, I knew Staze had what it takes to bring this idea to life. Their understanding of beauty, combined with the depth and breadth of their experience, gave me the confidence that we could create something that was not just exciting, but also relevant and accessible for people. I wanted to create a blush that I would personally want to use — something that works beautifully on Indian skin tones, is easy to build and, importantly, is accessible.

As per the latest buzz, That’s really how Caught Blushin’ came about. I’ve been closely involved in the process of creating it, which makes this collaboration especially close to my heart. I’m really excited about the Rhea x Staze makeup line and look forward to creating more products that feel true to me, my approach to beauty and the way I love experimenting with makeup.”
In further updates, A post shared by Rhea Chakraborty (@rhea_chakraborty)

On top of that, Saahil Nayar, Business Head, Staze, shared, “At Staze, we are constantly looking at the beauty moments that move from culture into everyday conversations and, eventually, into people’s makeup bags. Rhea’s blush look was one such moment. The response to it was immediate and organic, and it felt like the perfect opportunity to turn that moment into a product.

What made this collaboration particularly exciting was how naturally Rhea and Staze connected over a shared passion for makeup and beauty. Her enthusiasm and genuine passion for the category came through from our very first conversations. I have also admired the entrepreneurial journey she has built for herself, and it was clear to me that we had the right person to collaborate with — someone who brings her own perspective, curiosity and understanding of beauty to the table.

title: Salman Khan postpones Mumbai event as Khamoshi co-star Nana Patekar's death leaves the film industry in mourning
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Salman Khan ’s scheduled Mumbai event on Thursday was postponed following the death of veteran star Nana Patekar , who passed away at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. The two actors had shared screen space in Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s Khamoshi: The Musical (1996), and the decision to postpone Salman’s event came as the movie industry began mourning Patekar’s death.

Adding to this, Salman Khan postpones Mumbai event after Nana Patekar’s death at 75; Khamoshi co-star’s demise leaves Bollywood in shock. Salman was expected to attend an event hosted by GB Realty at Taj Lands End in Bandra on Thursday. The two actors worked together in Khamoshi, in which Nana played Joseph, the father of Manisha Koirala’s Annie, while Salman played Raj. Seema Biswas also featured in the movie, which remains one of Sanjay's early and much-remembered works.

Meanwhile, Nana died on Thursday, October 8, at his Goa residence after suffering a cardiac arrest. The doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes through CPR before he was declared dead at approximately 5:20 am. He was 75.

Notably, Nana's death has led to an outpouring of grief from the entertainment industry. Rajpal Yadav, who worked with him on the soon-to-release movie Vanvaas, shared an emotional tribute for his co-star.

As per the latest buzz, Other personalities, including Rajinikanth, Kamal Haasan, Chiranjeevi, Jr NTR, Allu Arjun, Ranveer Singh, Alia Bhatt, Sanjay Dutt and Akshay Kumar among others, also paid their respects. Cricket star Virat Kohli mourned the star’s death, calling Patekar “a true legend.”

In further updates, Born Vishwanath Patekar on January 1, 1951, in Maharashtra, Nana Patekar began his career in theatre before making his movie debut with Gaman in 1978. Over the years, he became known for playing complex and often intense characters, with his voice, dialogue delivery and screen presence becoming instantly recognisable.

On top of that, His breakthrough came with films such as Parinda (1989) and Prahaar (1991). He later appeared in Agni Sakshi, Khamoshi: The Musical, Shakti: The Power, Ab Tak Chhappan, Apaharan and Taxi No. 9211, among several others.

Nana also showed a very different side of himself with comedy. His performance as gangster Uday Shetty in Welcome (2007) became one of the most popular comic characters of his career. He returned to the role in Welcome Back in 2015. His other notable films included Raajneeti (2010) and the Marathi drama Natsamrat, which went on to become one of the most acclaimed performances of his later career.

title: Exclusive| Helen: I remember Nana as a very respectful actor and such a nice human being
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Helen, 87, played Nana Patekar’s mother Maria in Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s directorial debut Khamoshi: The Musical (1996). The movie was the story of Joseph (Nana) and Flavy Braganza (Seema Biswas), a deaf couple in Goa and their daughter Annie (Manisha Koirala)

Adding to this, Helen Helen recalls, “Khamoshi was a beautiful movie and having played Nana’s mother, I remember him as a very respectful star and such a nice human being. Our song from the movie Gaate The Pehle Akele continues to be a special memory, I remember him being on set and I’m just sad to learn of his sudden passing. I recall we had a lot of fun on that song even between the shots, the scene where I played the piano and we danced on the beach in Goa. Now, all those moments are fond memories. “

Meanwhile, She adds, “All of us have to go one day but as Salim saab keeps saying ‘Love each other or perish’ (popularized by the memoir Tuesdays with Morrie by Mitch Albom). I remember how Sanjay had come to Salim saab’s house to convince me to do Khamoshi because I had been away from the acting world. Today I’m glad I did that movie and met a wonderful star like Nana and the rest of the cast.”

title: ‘Broke nameplates, snatched caps’: Delhi cops claim assault during protests, DCP says youth under ‘wrongful influence’
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police personnel have alleged that they were physically assaulted while trying to maintain law and order and enforce restrictions during an Opposition protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Several officers claimed they were pushed, kicked and attacked while detaining peaceful demonstrators. Track live updates

Adding to this, Several police personnel described their experiences during India bloc's protest in Delhi. (ANI/PTI) The allegations came after Delhi Police forcefully detained Opposition MPs, led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , for staging a protest demanding the resignation of the CEC over mishandling of the voting system and revision of electoral rolls.

Meanwhile, Constable Devender Sandhu shared police personnel were calmly asking protesters to leave the restricted area and board police buses when some demonstrators allegedly began pulling and pushing officers.

Notably, "We were peacefully explaining to them, under protection, that the curfew of 163 is in effect here, Please leave," Sandhu told ANI. He added that officers were asking protesters to sit in the buses and claimed they were handling the situation calmly.

As per the latest buzz, According to Sandhu, the confrontation escalated when protesters allegedly broke the officers' nameplates and snatched their caps. "They broke our nameplates first, then they snatched the caps off our heads and threw them away," he shared, alleging that police personnel were subsequently pulled from behind and pushed to the ground.

In further updates, Sandhu shared he suffered injuries to his waist and the back of his head. He maintained that police had not used force against the protesters and were only carrying out detentions.

On top of that, "I was hurt quite a bit; I also got a deep injury on my waist and here on the back of my head," he shared. Sandhu alleged that officers "didn't hit anyone there" and were detaining protesters peacefully before the confrontation began.

Delhi Police DCP Shrishti Pandey on Thursday shared the alleged targeting of police personnel during protests was a matter of concern and claimed that "some form of wrongful influence" was leading young people towards such behaviour.

title: Exclusive| Aditya Sarpotdar on directing Nana Patekar in Shakti Shalini, one of his final films: ‘He was a family friend; was excited to see it’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

For filmmaker Aditya Sarpotdar, working with Nana Patekar on Shakti Shalini was more than an opportunity to direct the legendary star. Nana was not just someone Sarpotdar had admired on-screen, but also a family friend. The news of Nana's sudden death on Thursday (October 8) came as a shock to the director.

Adding to this, Aditya Sarpotdar; Nana Patekar “It’s very shocking for me. Just a few days ago, I had a long call with him about how he was excited to see the final movie,” Sarpotdar tells HT City exclusively, recalling their last conversation. The movie, which stars Aneet Padda and is expected to rollout later this year or early next year, had already been completely shot.
Meanwhile, “He was my grandfather’s friend. So I have seen him, grown up around stories of him.”

Notably, That connection made Shakti Shalini meaningful for Sarpotdar. He had pursued Nana for the role and was grateful when the veteran star agreed to come on board. “I pursued him to do the part and he was gracious enough to agree to do it. And once he was a part of it, to him it was not just about his role, but the whole movie,” he further adds.

As per the latest buzz, Conversations with Nana quickly went beyond Shakti Shalini, “With him, it was cinema always. It was all about all the experiences he’s kind of come from, what he’s learned from, and he would impart that to everybody around him.”

In further updates, Aditya was particularly struck by Nana’s enthusiasm for cinema even after more than five decades in the industry, “I told him that what I really take away from every conversation I have with him is his enthusiasm about movies, even after working in movies for more than 50 years. It is something that I really want to hold close to me when I am growing as a filmmaker. I look up to this quality of his.”

On top of that, Their collaboration had been a long time coming. Aditya had first met Nana for a Marathi movie nearly a decade earlier, but the project did not work out because of dates and other issues. “I remember telling him that we couldn’t make that work, but we have to make this work… and never would have I thought that this would be my last chance to work with him.”

Rishabh Suri is an Assistant Editor, movie critic, and professional overthinker of plot points. He writes for HT City, keeping pace with an industry where news cycles expire long before the popcorn gets cold. He completed his graduation in English Honours from Kirori Mal College, followed by a Master’s degree in English Literature-effectively training his brain to over-analyse classic texts before applying those exact same skills to 3-hour Bollywood blockbusters. He got into the profession when he had barely graduated from college and has been at HT ever since. At HT, Rishabh reviews films with a simple rule: skip the dense academic jargon and get straight to the point. Beyond reviews, as Assistant Editor, he helps navigate the broader circus of showbiz, tracking everything from OTT shifts to sudden ticket-window panics. In a beat driven by loud PR machinery and carefully scripted answers, Rishabh prefers cutting through the noise to focus on how stories get made and why trends shift. title: Nana Patekar once turned down Raj Kapoor's film offer: 'I could not tell him if I disagreed'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Mumbai, Raj Kapoor once offered a role to Nana Patekar but the star turned it down.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar once turned down Raj Kapoor's movie offer: 'I could not tell him if I disagreed' In an interview with PTI in December 2024, Patekar recounted the story behind his decision to say no to the legendary star-filmmaker, whose son Rishi Kapoor later became his close friend.
Meanwhile, "I was shooting at RK Studios when Raj Kapoor ji asked me, 'Will you work in my movie?' I thought, 'Raj Kapoor is asking me! He was my father's hero.' But I shared no.

Notably, "I told him, 'In my house, you are everyone's favourite hero, including my mother and father. If we ever have a difference of opinion over a scene, I would not be able to tell you anything. And if I did, I would feel that I was disrespecting you. That is why I can't work with you'," Nana shared recalling the conversation.
As per the latest buzz, The star, who died on Thursday at the age of 76, shared he had the same dilemma when other stalwarts of Indian cinema Dev Anand and V Shantaram approached him.

In further updates, "I shared the same thing to Dev Anand sahab as well. Once, V Shantaram also asked me, and I told him, 'I don't see you as a common man or an ordinary director. You are very big for me, and I can't imagine working with you'," he shared.

On top of that, Patekar, who delivered intense and raw performances in many critical hits such as "Parinda", "Krantiveer", "Yeshwant", "Ab Tak Chhappan" and "Agni Sakshi", also recalled his "beautiful" friendship with Rishi Kapoor, who passed away in April 2020.
The two actors starred together in the 1995 movie "Hum Dono", in which they played estranged brothers.

title: Nana Patekar's final screen appearances: Shraddha Kapoor's Eetha, Aneet Padda's Shakti Shalini and The Confession of Mary will release posthumously
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nana Patekar , one of Hindi cinema's most recognisable actors, died at 75. The veteran star passed away at his home in Goa on October 8 after suffering a cardiac arrest. The star was found unconscious in the early hours of Thursday and was taken to a private hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes. He was declared dead at around 5:20 am. His death brings to a close a career spanning over four decades, during which he worked across Marathi theatre, parallel cinema and some of Bollywood's biggest commercial films.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar's last three films are Eetha, Shakti Shalini and The Confession of Mary: Here's when they rollout. (AP Photo/) Even after his death, however, his work on screen is not over. Three completed films featuring the star are still awaiting rollout and will be rolled out posthumously.

Meanwhile, The Confession of Mary is perhaps the most notable of his remaining films. The movie has been directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Ananth Mahadevan , with Patekar playing Father Benedict, a priest accused of murdering a woman. The story takes inspiration from the 1966 Mariyakutty murder case in Kerala. Adil Hussain, Ashish Vidyarthi, Gautam Rode and Joy Sengupta also feature in the movie.

Notably, The official synopsis reads, “Marie's ravaged dead body was found in the thickets and all evidences pointed to Father Benedict's involvement in the case. In a stirring conflict of conscience and faith, Benedict refuses to divulge the confession that Marie had made to him. Benedict becomes the first priest to be sentenced to death ... But the Church and the Universe bring together elements that lead to a cathartic climax.”

As per the latest buzz, Subhash Kale, co-producer of Nana-starrer, shared that the star was supposed to come to Mumbai to complete the dubbing of the movie. In conversation with ANI, he shared, “We had spoken just the day before yesterday about the dubbing. There was one line that he had to dub. He told me, ‘I am coming to Bombay.’ He was supposed to come to Bombay tomorrow, and he also had a shoot scheduled in Bombay for a movie. So he told me, ‘I’ll come tomorrow, and we’ll do that one line’.”
In further updates, The project was selected to premiere at the Toronto International Movie Festival 2025. And is awaiting the rollout.

On top of that, The next movie is Laxman Utekar's Eetha is a biographical movie based on the life of Vithabai Narayangaonkar, the celebrated Maharashtrian Lavani and Tamasha artist. Shraddha Kapoor, Randeep Hooda and Anant Joshi headline the movie, with Nana Patekar also playing a part. The teaser was unveiled a few months ago and the movie's rollout was postponed. Now, the soon-to-release musical drama is scheduled to rollout on December 4, 2026.

The third movie is most likely will be last project on big screen which is Maddock Films' soon-to-release movie, Shakti Shalini. This is a horror-comedy from the production house's horror-comedy universe which has had films like Stree, Bhediya, and Munjhya. Aditya Sarpotdar has directed the movie. Aneet Padda , Vishal Jethwa and Vineet Kumar Singh are also part of the cast.

title: Exclusive | Muzaffar Ali recalls casting a 25-yr-old Nana Patekar in Gaman, his acting debut: He wasn't manufactured for Bollywood
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nana Patekar was all of 25 when filmmaker Muzaffar Ali spotted him for the first time at a stage play. Hewent on to cast Nana in Gaman, his debut as an star, and the rest is history. Today, as we mourn the loss the star, Muzaffar goes down memory lane to recall his first encounter with Nana.

Adding to this, Muzaffar Ali, Nana Patekar “It was in 1976, when I was casting for Gaman, that I saw a Marathi version of The Threepenny Opera in Dadar. I was mesmerised by the nimble, sharp performance of a young twenty-five-year-old star. He was like a Kalari sword—swift, precise and dangerous—in his words as much as in his body language. From that day, Nana Patekar became vital to my life," Muzaffar tells HT City in an exclusive chat.

Meanwhile, Muzaffar further recalls how Patekar stood out to him amid the emerging pool of Marathi talent that he encountered during the making of the movie, “He was a phenomenon beyond the cliched metaphors of Bollywood. A parallel world of extraordinary Marathi talent was emerging from the soil of Maharashtra, and I was keen to absorb that energy into Gaman. Nana was one of the young forces I discovered there.”
Notably, Their association went beyond the movie, with Nana also contributing to the visual and publicity aspects of Ali’s work, Muzaffar recalls.

As per the latest buzz, “Nana was far more than a talent I could consume within the limited frame of a single 35mm production. He was also a graphic designer, and he took care of my stickers, publicity material and outdoor media. Our association therefore moved naturally between cinema, theatre, design and life," shares the 81-year-old.

In further updates, “Very often, we would be called together on stage. Nana would say, with that characteristic mixture of mischief and affection, that I owed him five thousand rupees—and that even if I returned it ten times over, he would never accept it.”
On top of that, For Ali, Patekar’s roots in theatre and Maharashtra were central to what made him such a distinctive performer.

He says, “There was something wonderfully irreverent about him. He was not manufactured for Bollywood. He arrived from another tradition—from the theatre, from Maharashtra, from a culture of performance where the star had to command the stage before he could command the camera. Like Smita Patil, he represented a new face of Indian cinema emerging from Maharashtrian soil. He carried with him the raw intelligence of theatre and the instinctive immediacy of the street. He did not merely act a role; he occupied it. His words had an edge, his silences had weight, and his body seemed to speak even when he was still.”
