title: 'EC at centre of assault': 42 ex-judges defend India's poll process in open letter amid protest against Gyanesh Kumar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Forty-two former judges and retired veterans of constitutional office have expressed concern over what they described as a sustained campaign against the Election Commission of India, the judiciary and other constitutional institutions.

Adding to this, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi stops Delhi Police from detaining Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and others during the INDIA bloc MPs' protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar near Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi. (AICC/ANI Photo) In an open letter, the signatories shared they had no political brief and were speaking out because “silence is no longer a neutral choice”. They alleged that constitutional bodies were facing attacks driven by political interests and warned of the consequences of undermining public trust in the country’s democratic institutions. "Our concern is grave. India's constitutional bodies are under sustained attack. The Election Commission of India stands at the centre of this assault," the letter read.

Meanwhile, The former judges questioned allegations of “vote theft” made without supporting evidence and objected to constitutional authorities being publicly described as “thieves”, “puppets” and “compromised”.
Notably, “Criticism of institutions is a democratic right. Denigration is not,” the letter states.

As per the latest buzz, They also shared election officials had been publicly named and warned of reprisals if there was a change in government, while alleging that no court had found the charges against constitutional authorities to be proven.

In further updates, The signatories strongly defended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, describing it as part of the Election Commission’s constitutional mandate to maintain accurate voter lists.

On top of that, The letter shared Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Commission to revise electoral rolls at any time. It also noted that intensive revisions had been conducted repeatedly since the first general elections.

“The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is part of that very design. Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Commission to revise the rolls at any time. Intensive revisions have been carried out repeatedly since the first general elections. The last SIR was completed about two decades back. No one called those revisions a conspiracy,” the letter read.

title: Rohit Shetty reveals Nana Patekar refused fees for Golmaal Again cameo, told him to donate it to orphanage
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran Bollywood star Nana Patekar 's sudden demise has left the entire movie industry in shock. Several actors and filmmakers have expressed their grief over losing a great artiste and shared fond memories of the veteran star. Filmmaker Rohit Shetty , who worked with Nana in Golmaal Again , opened up that the star refused to take a fee for his cameo in the movie.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar's still from his cameo in Golmaal Again. Rohit Shetty remembers Nana Patekar Mourning Nana's death, the filmmaker posted on Instagram and shared a picture of the star. He penned a note remembering his special bond with Nana and wrote, "Dear Dada, I will miss your late-night calls. No hello and no formalities but a straight, "Aye Shetty, kya kar raha hai? ,(Hey Shetty, what are you doing?) And I would purposely reply "Kaun bol raha hai? (Who is speaking?)", to irritate you only to get a "Saale, Nana bol raha hoon! (Nana speaking)"
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rohit Shetty (@itsrohitshetty)

Notably, He also recalled Nana being his biggest critic and supporter at the same time. He wrote, "After my rollout, you were one of my biggest and most honest critics. You never sugar-coated anything. 'Yeh waali tune achhi banayi (This is good),' 'Yeh waali mujhe achhi nahi lagi (This I didn't like),' 'Yeh waali superhit hai (This is superhit)' and 'this you tried to make a hit.' And then, in your own way, you would remind me, 'Abay, tu khud star hai... tujhe itne stars ki zaroorat nahi hai (“Hey, you’re a star yourself… you don’t need so many stars).'"

As per the latest buzz, Rohit further recalled his special bond with Nana, which was why the veteran star refused to take a fee for his cameo in Golmaal Again. He wrote, "I will never forget when you did a cameo in Golmaal Again. I asked you, "Dada, aapki fees?".

In further updates, And you looked at me and shared, 'Ch****ya, tujhse paise lunga? Ek anathashram ka number deta hoon, wahan donate kar de (Idiot, would I take money from you? I’ll give you the number of an orphanage instead; donate it there).' That was you Dada. Straight. Unfiltered. Generous. And always genuine. I will miss being called Shetty by you. WILL MISS YOU DADA."

On top of that, Nana Patekar may have had only a brief appearance in Golmaal Again, but his presence in the 2017 horror comedy was instantly recognisable. The star appeared as himself in a cameo, while his distinctive voice also became a recurring gag in the movie. Whenever a character was possessed, they would mimic Patekar's voice.

Nana Patekar died at the age of 75 following a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa on October 8. His son, Malhar Patekar, verified his death to local media. The star was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, and was rushed to Manipal Hospital. Doctors attempted to revive him with cardiac massage for 45 minutes before he was declared dead.

title: Aneet Padda starrer Shakti Shalini may not clash with Shah Rukh Khan starrer King; makers eyeing for March release, reveals report

title: ‘Everyone’s time will come, my time will come too’: Nana Patekar at last public event
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

At his last public event, veteran Bollywood and Marathi star Nana Patekar , who passed away on Friday morning following a cardiac arrest, had foretold that ‘his time would come too’ but that he was hopeful that he could do something worthwhile before it did.

Adding to this, New Delhi, Oct 08 (ANI): (File Photo) Veteran star Nana Patekar passed away at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, on Thursday. (ANI Photo) (ANI Photo) Speaking at the installation ceremony of the new managing committee of the Samraat Club held in Goa on October 4, Patekar, was speaking in reference to former Goa chief minister and union defence inister Manohar Parrikar.

Meanwhile, “Everyone has to go one day. I don't know when my time will come, whether today or tomorrow, your time will come too. But, are you capable of doing what needs to be done before that? Are you making the effort? If you stay limited to your own family and circle... one needs to give back to society,” Patekar had shared on the occasion.

Notably, “What I like about Narendra Modi's ideas, I do like, but also learn to speak up about what you do not like (about him). What is an andolan at the end of the day? It is saying what you do not like. Even a small child grumbles when they are not happy. If there is something I do not like, then it is certainly my duty to raise my voice about it. But there's also a manner in which one raises their voice. One must never use foul language about anyone. That language can be reserved for friends or at home,” Patekar had also shared.

As per the latest buzz, “Manohar Parrikar is my friend. He was younger than me, but his stature was such that one had to look up to him. He was destined for great things and he made sure he would do what it takes (to get there). Despite his limits as an individual he achieved a great deal,” Patekar had shared on the occasion.

In further updates, Rajashree Khandeparkar was installed as the state president of the Samraat Club at an event that was attended by several among the who's who of Goa including Utpal Parrikar, the son of Manohar Parrikar BJP state leaders among others.
On top of that, Patekar, who owned a home in Dona Paula, an upscale locale of the state capital Panaji, was a frequent visitor to the state.

“Shocked and deeply saddened to learn about the demise of veteran star Shri @nanagpatekar Ji. With his remarkable journey across theatre, Hindi and Marathi cinema, his powerful performances and distinctive artistry left an indelible mark on Indian cinema. My heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, admirers and the entire movie fraternity. May his soul attain Sadgati. Om Shanti,” Sawant shared via a post on X.

title: Nana Patekar messaged friend at 2:30 AM saying he was unwell, reveals doctor; adds actor was “brought dead” to hospital
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In conversation with ANI, Dr. Salkar shared, “Nana Patekar was brought dead to the hospital. He was declared dead by 5:30 am. We had tried our best to save him, but he was brought dead. Cardiac massage was given for almost 45 minutes to an hour, but he just could not be saved.”

Adding to this, According to Dr. Salkar, Nana Patekar had as per reports messaged a friend around 2:30 AM saying that he was not feeling well. However, as it was nighttime, the friend did not see the message immediately.
Meanwhile, The friend later called Nana and went to his residence at around 4 AM. By then, the star was as per reports sweating and his condition was deteriorating.

Notably, “As per what we recalled, at around 2:30, he sent a message to his friend that he was not feeling well. But as it was nighttime, his friend could not see the message. So he just called him. He went to his house at around 4 o'clock. By that time, he was sweating and all,” Dr. Salkar told ANI.

As per the latest buzz, The people present at the residence then began taking primary measures before arranging medical assistance. Dr. Salkar shared Nana was gradually becoming unconscious, following which his caretaker was sent to the hospital to seek help.
In further updates, Dr. Salkar shared the hospital’s emergency response team went to Nana Patekar’s residence and began cardiac massage as he was completely unresponsive.

On top of that, “He was slowly becoming unconscious. So they sent his caretaker to the hospital. He took our ambulance. When our ER team went there, they started cardiac massage because he was totally unresponsive,” he shared.
The star was subsequently shifted to Manipal Hospital at around 4:20 or 4:30 AM. Doctors continued their efforts to revive him, but he could not be saved.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nana Patekar died of a cardiac arrest on October 8 at the age of 75. Tributes have been pouring in from across the movie industry and political circles as the sudden death of the veteran star has left many in shock, with those who worked closely with him struggling to come to terms with the loss.

Adding to this, Indian star and filmmaker Nana Patekar has died at the age of 75. (AP Photo) (AP Photo/) ‘It is a huge grief, a very big loss for the industry’ Subhash Kale, co-producer of the soon-to-release Nana Patekar-starrer crime thriller The Confession, also known as The Confession of Mary, shared the star was expected to return to Mumbai soon to complete the movie's dubbing. In conversation with news agency ANI, Subhash recalled his last conversation with Nana. He shared, “It is a very big loss, and it is unbelievable… unbelievable. I found out at around 7:30 this morning, as soon as I woke up, and I was completely shaken when I heard the news. Then, to confirm it, I immediately called Malhar, and it was verified. It is a huge grief, a very big loss for the industry. A very big loss! So sudden…”

Meanwhile, He went on to add that they had spoken just two days earlier about the dubbing, with only one line left for the star to record. “Yes, The Confession, which is set to rollout. We had spoken just the day before yesterday about the dubbing. There was one line that he had to dub. He told me, ‘I am coming to Bombay.’ He was supposed to come to Bombay tomorrow, and he also had a shoot scheduled in Bombay for a movie. So he told me, ‘I’ll come tomorrow, and we’ll do that one line.’… Whenever he came to Mumbai, the first call would be to me: ‘I am coming to the studio.’ We would sit together, have a lot of fun, joke around, sing songs… He was just incredible. What can I say now? I am unable to speak at this moment. I have to leave for Goa now, so…" he added.

Notably, Nana Patekar died in Goa on the morning of October 8. He was 75. The star’s son, Malhar Patekar , verified to local media about his death. Nana was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, and was rushed to Manipal Hospital. Doctors attempted to revive the star for around 45 minutes but were unsuccessful. The star was declared dead at around 5:20 am, with doctors citing a heart attack as the cause of death.

As per the latest buzz, A three-time National Award -winning star, Nana is regarded as one of the finest actors in Indian cinema history. His passing drew tributes from across Indian cinema and public life, including tributes from Prime Minister Modi and several Chief Ministers.

title: Nana Patekar: The outspoken star who had friends across parties
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Widely acclaimed for his on-screen performances, star Nana Patekar has long occupied a unique space in Maharashtra’s public life. Beyond cinema, he is known for extensive social work, most notably relief initiatives for drought-hit farm families, and for warm relationships across the state’s political spectrum.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar has died at the age of 75. (Reuters) Over the decades, the star cultivated warm ties across party lines and hosted senior leaders from Maharashtra’s rival political parties for the Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations at his home in Mumbai and later at his farm near Pune.
Meanwhile, Yet, his willingness to speak his mind and confront the powerful landed him in row, drawing flak even from close allies.

Notably, During 1995–1999, when the Shiv Sena–BJP combine was in power and Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray was at the height of his influence, Nana Patekar publicly called him out for disparaging Marathi literary figures. “Balasaheb, you have collected an image in our hearts and even you don’t have a right to destroy it,” he shared.
As per the latest buzz, Many feared a backlash but Balasaheb took the critique in stride and the their friendship endured till his death in 2012.

In further updates, Nana Patekar had even attempted to broker peace between Balasaheb Thackeray and journalist Nikhil Wagale who had been attacked by Sena workers following his criticism of the Sena leadership.
On top of that, In an interview, Nana Patekar shared he stopped visiting Matoshree with Balasaheb’s death.

“When Balasaheb Thackeray was alive, he used to call me whenever he wants. We used to speak on phone or he used to ask me to come to Matoshree for meeting. But after his death phone calls from Matoshree stopped and my relation with that home ended,” Patekar shared.

title: Kangana Ranaut moves Delhi High Court seeking removal of AI-generated, obscene content online, summons issued
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and Member of Parliament Kangana Ranaut has moved the Delhi High Court seeking the removal of certain AI-generated, obscene content about her from the internet. The star alleged that the content maligns and defames her and infringes on her personality rights.

Adding to this, Kangana Ranaut during the ongoing Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo/Arun Sharma) (PTI) Kangana moves Delhi HC Kangana, the BJP MP from Mandi, moved the HC on Thursday. Her lawyer objected to the existence of sexual and pornographic content, fake news, as well as AI-generated content, wrongly attributing statements to the star-politician.

Meanwhile, Kangana's legal team emphasised that they were seeking relief only against the obscene and allegedly fake online content, and not against memes about her. The lawyer shared that while there were also memes and other objectionable satirical content, he was not pressing for relief against them at this stage.

Notably, Hearing Kangana's plea, Justice Vikas Mahajan issued a summons to the defendant parties in the star's lawsuit seeking protection of her personality rights. According to a PTI report, the court indicated that it would pass an interim order in the matter.

As per the latest buzz, In the same hearing, the court also shared it would pass an interim order on a separate personality rights lawsuit by Telugu star Vijay Deverakonda, as it issued summons on it. Vijay's lawyer had alleged unauthorised commercial exploitation of the movie star's personality by third parties through various means, including the sale of merchandise bearing his persona's attributes. The star's team further shared there were AI-generated social posts, instances of impersonation, false endorsements, and the use of foul language.

In further updates, Kangana isn't the first star to move court to protect her personality rights and seek takedown of AI-generated content about her. In the last few months, several public figures, including many actors, have approached the high court seeking protection of their personality and publicity rights.

On top of that, This includes actors Aishwarya Rai Bachchan , Abhishek Bachchan, and Salman Khan, as well as star and Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan. Art of Living founder Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, podcaster Raj Shamani, and cricketer Abhishek Sharma have also approached the high court for protection of their personality rights.
The high court had granted all of them interim relief.

title: After Satish Kaushik, Anupam Kher loses another friend, Nana Patekar, to cardiac arrest; tears up in video message: 'It's not fair'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Tributes have been pouring in from across the movie industry and political circles after veteran star Nana Patekar passed away at the age of 75 following a cardiac arrest. Bollywood star Anupam Kher also expressed his grief over Nana's demise and teared up as he recalled fond memories he shared with him over the years.

Adding to this, Anupam Kher lost two of his friends Nana Patekar and Satish Kaushik to cardiac arrest. Anupam Kher breaks down into tears recalling memories with Nana Patekar Anupam posted on Instagram and shared an emotional video recalling his memories with Nana. He opened up that he is currently in Washington, DC, and learnt about the tragic news right after he finished his play, Jaane Pehchane Anjaane. The star added that there could not have been a sadder piece of news, especially when he is 1,000 km away from India. He shared that while he was being appreciated after his show ended, he was hit by the sad news of Nana's death as soon as he entered the backstage area.

Meanwhile, Anupam further recalled that whenever he met Nana, he would pretend to be angry with him, and to make him happy, Anupam would sing a song for him. He added, "it's terrible, it's not fair. Some people, we think will never go, and Nana was one of them. He was larger than life. He had the largest heart in the world. Nana's anger was all kindness. It's not right, he should have not gone."
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Anupam Kher (@anupampkher)

As per the latest buzz, The star added that he had worked in several films with Nana and had spent a lot of time with him. He recalled of late passing by Nana's house and promising him that he would visit the next time he was in town. He broke down in tears as he shared, "He shouldn't have left like this, this is wrong. This shouldn't have happened. With some people this thing should never happen. There was a sense of belonging in his scolding. He would sometimes even scold without any reason."

In further updates, Calling him one of the greatest actors in Indian cinema, Anupam further recalled how Nana would call him out of the blue to praise his work. He admitted that he did not know how to react to Nana's death. He added, "I so sad. I just met him a couple of months back. It's shocking, unreal and real at the same time. He was just 75 and a healthy, strong 75-year-old man. I'll miss you. I'll miss you more than words could ever say. It's tough, and I am sorry to his family and loved ones. We have lost one of the finest actors and human beings in India."

On top of that, He further wrote in the caption that Nana would have hated the idea of tributes. The emotional note penned by the star read, "NANA PATEKAR THE GREATEST? A couple of hours ago, I received the heartbreaking news that my friend Nana Patekar, one of the finest actors and human beings in Indian cinema, is no more. I had just finished our performance and taken the curtain call. As I walked into the wings, my director Gajendra told me, "Nana is no more." After that, I had to meet people, pose for photographs, smile, sit down for a meal... while trying to absorb what I had just heard. It was terribly difficult."

Anupam added, "But somewhere, I felt that Nana would have wanted me to finish my work. Fulfil my responsibility to the people who had come to see us. And then, perhaps, remember him. Actually, knowing him, I can almost hear him dismissing the very idea of a tribute: 'अरे, तो क्या हो गया? मर गया तो कौन-सी बड़ी बात है? सभी मरते हैं! (Oh, so what? What’s the big deal if someone dies? Everyone dies!)'

title: A Nana Patekar classic is a rare Bollywood film remade in Hollywood; Marvel star Vincent D'Onofrio took over his role
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

Bollywood has been accused of ‘copying’ Hollywood films for far too long. There are filmmakers whose filmography sections on Wikipedia have a separate column describing ‘adapted from’, so endemic is this in Hindi cinema. Even today, when studios buy rights for official remakes, Bollywood has often been caught playing catch-up. The reverse - Hollywood remaking a Hindi movie - is a rarity. But it did happen in 2015, and it happened with the movie that first shot Nana Patekar to stardom in the 80s.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar won his first National Award for the 1989 rollout, Parinda. The Nana Patekar classic remade in Hollywood In 1989, Vidhu Vinod Chopra made Parinda, often regarded as one of the first Bollywood films to set a template for depicting the underworld and gangsters realistically. The movie starred Anil Kapoor and Jackie Shroff as brothers who live and work under Anna ( Nana Patekar ), a dreaded don. The movie, which also starred Madhuri Dixit, was a commercial success with its music becoming quite popular. Tumse Milke, sung by Suresh Wadkar and Asha Bhosle, topped the charts. Critically acclaimed, Parinda went on to win two National Movie Awards and five Filmfare Awards, and was India's official selection for the 1990 Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Movie. Nana Patekar won his first National Award for the movie.

Meanwhile, In 1998, Parinda was remade in Tamil as Aasai Thambi. But the surprise remake was revealed in 2012, when Vidhu Vinod Chopra shared he was set to adapt the movie for American audiences with a Hollywood cast. Abhijat Joshi co-wrote the screenplay titled Broken Horses. Anton Yelchin and Chris Marquette were cast as the two leads, alongside Vincent D’Onofrio as Julius Hench, this movie’s Anna.

Notably, Set in the American Midwest, Broken Horses was shot in the style of the typical American Westerns with sprawling ranches, cowboys, gunfights, and a signature musical score. Tom Stern, the cinematographer long associated with Clint Eastwood films, was on board, while Oscar-nominated composer John Debney composed the score. Reliance Entertainment and Fox Star Studios came on board to produce and distribute the movie worldwide. At 1 hour and 41 minutes, Broken Horses was considerably shorter than Parinda, which ran for almost 2.5 hours.

As per the latest buzz, The biggest casting coup for the movie was Vincent D’Onofrio. Even though he was still two years away from playing the Kingpin in the Daredevil series, the star was already a known and respected name, having worked in Full Metal Jacket, Men In Black, and The Cell. Apart from this, he had spent 10 years starring in Law & Order: Criminal Intent, one of America’s most-watched TV shows. The casting of Anton Yelchin was equally impressive. At the time, only 24, Anton had already starred in the Star Trek reboot and Terminator Salvation.

In further updates, Despite a stacked cast and a competent crew, Broken Horses did not fare well. The critics called it ‘overwrought’, and it has an approval rating of only 26% on Rotten Tomatoes. Made on a modest budget of around $15 million, Broken Horses was a commercial disaster, earning less than ₹ 1 crore rupees in India and just $65K in the US. Its global ‘haul’ of less than $300K was one of the lowest for a mainstream Hollywood movie that year.

On top of that, The failure of Broken Horses did not dampen Parinda’s legacy, though. Over the years, it has been included in News18's 2013 list of the "100 greatest Indian films of all time", Mint's list of "70 iconic films of Indian cinema", Filmfare's "100 Filmfare Days" series, the "70 iconic movies of independent India" list and the book 100 Bollywood Films by Rachel Dwyer. Filmmakers Anurag Kashyap, Nikkhil Advani, and Dibakar Banerjee have credited the movie for impacting their journeys. Nana Patekar’s performance has been hailed as one of the first ‘realistic’ depictions of a violent villain in mainstream Hindi cinema.

Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: 'Amit ji, I received far more than I ever wished for': When Nana Patekar made Amitabh Bachchan feel proud with his humble take on life
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Nana Patekar has died at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa. The star was found unconscious in the early hours of Thursday and was taken to a private hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes. He was declared dead at around 5:20 am.

Adding to this, Star's old Kaun Banega Crorepati conversation with Amitabh Bachchan on fame, village life goes widely shared. As tributes have been pouring in since morning, a resurfaced clip from his appearance on Amitabh Bachchan 's Kaun Banega Crorepati 16 offered a particularly clear insight into a lesser-known side of him.

Meanwhile, Away from the camera, Nana often spoke about having little interest in the lifestyle that came with being a movie star. He preferred spending time away from Mumbai and repeatedly spoke about his connection to his village. During the conversation with Amitabh, Nana explained why he never felt completely at home in the movie industry and why he preferred returning to his village after completing his work.

Notably, "I don't really belong to the movie industry," he shared. "I come here, do my work, and then run back. I've never been someone who attends parties here. That lifestyle doesn't appeal to me. It's just not who I am. I come from a village, and I will always remain a village man. That's where I feel most at home."

As per the latest buzz, Nana also spoke about how having fewer needs had made his life simpler and, in his view, happier. He told Bachchan that he had already received much more from life than he had expected.

In further updates, “Amit ji, I received far more than I ever wished for. Life has given me a lot. When your needs are limited, everything becomes much easier. I truly enjoy that life. In the city, people have walls around their homes. Where I live, we have mountains around us, and we live amidst them. Life is so simple there.” Amitabh, visibly moved by what Nana had shared, responded, “It makes us very proud to see that.”

On top of that, Nana's filmography included Krantiveer, Agneepath, Welcome, Ab Tak Chhappan and The Attacks of 26/11. Nana remained active as an star even in his seventies. His recent work included Vishal Bhardwaj's O' Romeo , in which he appeared alongside Shahid Kapoor and Triptii Dimri, and a cameo in Subedar with Anil Kapoor and Radhika Madan.

Alongside her work at Hindustan Times, her bylines have appeared in several international publications. Known for her in-depth interviews, feature stories and engaging storytelling, Monica enjoys exploring the human side of entertainment. From breaking news and long-form features to music coverage, explainers and on-camera conversations with artists, she is passionate about telling stories that connect with audiences across the world. title: Grief and tears: Nana Patekar's relatives, friends gather at Goa hospital
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Panaji, Tears welled up as Nana Patekar's nephew Sachin Patekar, unable to contain his grief, arrived at Goa Medical College and Hospital near Panaji, where the star's mortal remains were brought for postmortem on Thursday.

Adding to this, Grief and tears: Nana Patekar's relatives, friends gather at Goa hospital Relatives, friends and well‑wishers, including star Sayaji Shinde, gathered in quiet grief outside the state-run hospital, paying tribute to the star, remembered not only for his versatile performances but also for his commitment to social causes.
Meanwhile, The sombre mood outside the GMCH mortuary in Bambolim near the state capital grew heavier when Sachin, overcome with emotion, broke down.
Notably, Patekar's close friend, star Sayaji Shinde, rushed to the hospital from a shooting assignment in the state as soon as he heard the news of his demise.

As per the latest buzz, Patekar, 76, was rushed in an unconscious state from his Dona Paula residence near Panaji to a private hospital where he was declared dead early on Thursday. The body was later shifted to GMCH.
In further updates, Police have registered a medico-legal case in connection with his death.
On top of that, Shinde shared he got to know about Patekar's death through a news channel, after which he rushed to the GMCH.
"It was shocking… I saw the news on a channel this morning... I was shooting nearby, so I rushed here. It was shocking; what more can I say," he told reporters.

title: Tanushree Dutta says she has ‘heard the news’ of Nana Patekar's death, wants to focus on work: ‘Condolences to family’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nana Patekar died of a cardiac arrest on October 8 at the age of 75. Star Tanushree Dutta , who accused Nana of sexually harassing her during the Indian Me Too movement, seemingly reacted to the news of his death. She made multiple posts on her Instagram Stories, even talking about his death in one of them and sending condolences to his family.

Adding to this, News of Nana’s death broke early on Thursday. Tanushree has been active on her Instagram since morning. She posted a prayer to Durga and a note in Hindi that translates to: “A golden shadow walks with me, one I have collected from the temples.” Tanushree also posted selfie videos of her walking through the airport and eating a sandwich for brunch.

Meanwhile, Tanushree then seemed to address the elephant in the room and shared, “Maine suna hai, I have heard the news. I just… today is my workday. I am going to Lucknow for an event. And I want to focus on that. What an odd day for all this to happen. Because I’m doing a very big event in Lucknow, and it was pretty important for me. I had my entire day planned out. I wanted to do all these Lives and post content. And now I’m worried that in the evening, that’s all the media is going to be interested in is evil dead. So, I will give my reaction once I figure out what kind of reaction I should have. So, definitely condolences to the family but...” and her video cut off midway.
Notably, Tanushree did not name Nana in the video. She then posted videos of her boarding her flight to Lucknow.

As per the latest buzz, In 2018, Tanushree accused Nana of sexual harassment on a movie set during the Me Too movement. She shared that the incident took place on the set of the 2009 movie Horn 'Ok' Pleassss. Her speaking out became a catalyst for the movement in India, along with Sri Reddy’s protest in Hyderabad, prompting many others to speak out against sexual harassment and abuse in the workplace.

In further updates, Tanushree claimed to have filed a complaint against him with the Cine & TV Artists Association ( CINTAA ) in 2008, but no action was taken. An FIR was registered against Nana, who denied the allegations. In 2019, the case was closed for lack of sufficient evidence. In 2025, the Mumbai Andheri Magistrate Court officially dismissed the criminal proceedings against Nana because the complaint was filed beyond the legal limitation period.

title: When CM Yogi Adityanath praised Nana Patekar for working to prevent farmer suicides ‘without any publicity’, called him ‘sensitive human’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Nana Patekar was celebrated for his intense performances on screen, but his contribution away from films was just as meaningful. The star had often used his platform to support people in need, particularly farmers in Maharashtra struggling with the devastating impact of farmer suicides. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had previously lauded Nana for extending support without turning his charitable work into a publicity exercise.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar once helped the farmers without any publicity. When Nana Patekar helped farmers Speaking at the launch of Shankar Mahadevan 's song Khaki Ka Sitara in August this year, CM Yogi recalled Nana's work among farmers. He shared, "Nana Patekar is not only an star; he is an equally sensitive human being. When farmers in Maharashtra had started committing suicides on a large scale, the person who extended a helping hand to those farmers was none other than Nana Patekar."

Meanwhile, The CM also recalled being surprised when Nana met him and introduced himself while working to support farmers. "I was very surprised. Such a big star was working for farmers, but it was true," he shared, adding that Nana had carried out his efforts "without any publicity or fanfare".

Notably, Nana had also lent his support to the Uttar Pradesh Police's cyber-security awareness campaign. He featured in a short movie aimed at educating people about online threats, including digital arrest scams. Yogi thanked the National Award-winning star for using his acting skills to contribute to the police's public awareness initiative.

As per the latest buzz, His philanthropic efforts extended beyond Maharashtra as well. The Nirmala Gajanan Foundation, an NGO run by Nana, collaborated with the Indian Army to provide rehabilitation assistance worth ₹ 42 lakh to 117 families in the Rajouri and Poonch districts who were severely affected by cross-border shelling following Operation Sindoor.

In further updates, Nana had previously stressed that helping those in distress should be viewed as a collective responsibility rather than an act of charity. In conversation with the media, the National Award winner shared, "It is our responsibility to help when such incidents take place in the nation. They are our brothers and sisters. It is a collective responsibility for all of us. We haven't done any favours to any of them. This is what everyone should do."

On top of that, The star also lauded fellow star Johnny Lever for quietly helping people in need. Nana pointed out that several members of the Hindi movie industry contributed to charitable causes without seeking publicity. "People from our movie industry also do a lot for people in need, but never come to the forefront. Johnny Lever is one of them. If we don't do it, then who else will? The government did a lot, but don't be dependent on them, do something by yourself too. I feel satisfied when I become the reason for someone's happiness," shared Nana Patekar.

Nana Patekar died on October 8 at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. The veteran star had as per reports messaged a friend at around 2.30am saying that he was not feeling well and also called him. By the time his friend reached his residence, Nana had become unconscious.

title: Nana Patekar passes away at 75 after severe cardiac arrest at Goa residence
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Dr. Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, verified the news and shared that a medico-legal case (MLC) has been registered. Further details regarding the circumstances of his death are expected following the post-mortem examination.

Adding to this, “Veteran star Nana Patekar passed away at 5:20 AM today after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence. Despite 45 minutes of continuous CPR, he could not be revived. A medico-legal case (MLC) has been registered, and a post-mortem will be conducted,” Dr. Shekhar Salkar shared.

Meanwhile, Nana Patekar began his movie career with the 1978 movie Gaman . While his early years in cinema were gradual, he went on to establish himself as one of the most distinctive actors in Hindi and Marathi cinema.

Notably, His performances in films such as Salaam Bombay! and Parinda brought him wider recognition. Salaam Bombay! , directed by Mira Nair, was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Movie. In Parinda , Patekar played a gangster, a performance that collected him the National Movie Award and Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Star.

As per the latest buzz, The making of Parinda was also physically demanding for the star. He suffered serious burns while filming a real-fire sequence and spent months recovering in hospital. Earlier, he had also been stabbed during the shooting of Salaam Bombay! .
In further updates, Patekar later moved behind the camera with Prahaar: The Final Attack , which he directed and starred in. For the 1991 movie, he underwent training with the Territorial Army.

On top of that, Patekar remained active on screen in the years leading up to his death. His most recent rolled out movie was Subedaar , the Amazon Prime Video action drama starring Anil Kapoor. The movie premiered on March 5, 2026, with Patekar making a special appearance as Lance Naik Nana Waghmare.

Before that, he had a substantial theatrical role in Vishal Bhardwaj’s O’Romeo , which rolled out on February 13, 2026. He played Ismail Khan, the chief of the Mumbai Intelligence Bureau, in the movie starring Shahid Kapoor and Triptii Dimri.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nana Patekar ’s funeral will be held at his farmhouse on the outskirts of Pune on Thursday, a representative of the star’s social organisation informed. title: A chilling don, a vigilante, and a sadistic wife-beater: The roles that earned Nana Patekar his 3 National Awards
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The style of acting that Nana Patekar brought to Bollywood in the 1980s was unprecedented. In an industry where slowness of dialogue delivery and ‘thehraav’ were rewarded, Nana brought the angst and rage of the 80s, channelling them through his fast-talking and imbuing his characters with unusual quirks and ticks. This led to him winning three National Movie Awards in a nine-year period. The films and the performances that won him these prestigious awards were as diverse and different as they could be. A look at the three stellar performances that made Nana Patekar a three-time National Award winner.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar won his third and final National Movie Award for Agni Sakshi in 1997. Best Supporting Star for Parinda (1989) Loosely inspired by On The Waterfront, Vidhu Vinod Chopra ’s Parinda is considered one of the first Bollywood films to set a template for how the underworld and gangsters could be depicted realistically. In this movie, Nana Patekar portrayed Anna in a manner that would pave the way for the Manoj Bajpayees and Ajay Devgns to follow suit years later. His Anna lorded over the city. He was kind, but brutal; menacing, but jovial. The kind of restraint Nana brought to this otherwise bloodthirsty character made him all the scarier. It won him his first National Award and his maiden Filmfare Award.

Meanwhile, Mehul Kumar’s Krantiveer catapulted Nana to stardom. The movie was the third-highest-grossing Hindi movie of 1994 and the first smash hit of Nana’s career as a leading man. In this movie, the star showed that he could bring ‘performance’ to even a masala entertainer. If not for Nana, Krantiveer would have been a typical 90s’ Bollywood revenge saga, with some social messaging added for good measure. But Nana elevated it to cult classic status. His lines became iconic, and his scenes are ‘widely shared’ on YouTube three decades later. In Pratap, Nana presented an evolution of Bachchan’s Angry Young Man. This one was frustrated, but not silent. The Best Star win also meant that Nana was now seen as a ‘leading man’ and not just a character star.

Notably, Bollywood made three ‘unofficial’ remakes of Julia Roberts’ Sleeping With The Enemy, all rolled out in 1996. Yaraana had Rishi Kapoor and Madhuri Dixit’s star power, while Daraar was hailed for Arbaaz Khan’s chilling debut. But the most successful and most critically acclaimed of these was Agni Sakshi, starring Nana, Manisha Koirala, and Jackie Shroff. Nana played Vishwanath, a sadistic, controlling, possessive, and abusive husband who makes his wife’s life a living hell. Even after she escapes his clutches, he stalks her and her new partner. One particular scene where Nana first assaults Madhu (Manisha) and then applies medicine to her wounds himself was a chilling display of Nana’s range as an star and the way he owned the screen without overshadowing his co-performers.

As per the latest buzz, Nana Patekar continued acting through the 2000s and 2010s, delivering many strong performances. Many are surprised that he never won another National Award , given the kind of strong presence he had in films like Ab Tak Chhappan, Kaala, and Natsamrat, to name a few. He did win a Best Villain Filmfare Award for his role as a kidnapping mafia kingpin in Prakash Jha’s Apaharan, but the National Award eluded him.

In further updates, Nana Patekar died on Wednesday morning at his Goa residence. He was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, and was rushed to Manipal Hospital. Doctors attempted to revive the star for around 45 minutes but were unsuccessful. His last performance was in Vishal Bhardwaj’s O’Romeo, which rolled out earlier this year.

title: Tukaram Mundhe reveals Nana Patekar's last words to him just 8 days before his death: ‘Those words will stay with me’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Nana Patekar has died at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa. The star was found unconscious at his residence in the early hours of Thursday and was taken to a private hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him for nearly 45 minutes. He was declared dead at around 5:20 a.m.

Adding to this, ‘I could never have imagined...’: Tukaram Mundhe remembers Nana Patekar, reveals their last conversation 8 days ago. Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Department of Oncology at Manipal Hospital, shared Patekar remained in asystole during the resuscitation attempt, which means there was no electrical activity in his heart. A medico-legal case has been registered and a post-mortem examination is expected to be carried out.

Meanwhile, While followers and colleagues across the movie industry mourned his death, those who knew Nana Patekar personally remembered a side of the star that audiences rarely got to see. Tukaram Mundhe , who described Nana as a close friend, shared an emotional tribute following his death.

Notably, Sharing a photo of Nana Patekar, the Commissioner of Food and Drug Administration of Maharashtra opened up that he had spoken to the veteran star eight days ago before his passing. He wrote, “Nana Patekar is no more. I have lost not merely an exceptional artist, but an extraordinary human being and a dear friend, someone whose warmth and affection touched everyone around him. We spoke just eight days ago. I could never have imagined that it would be our last conversation. His last words to me were: 'Love you, Bala.' Those words will stay with me for the rest of my life.”

As per the latest buzz, Tukaram added, “Some people leave behind memories. A few leave behind a part of themselves in our lives. Nana was one of them. Goodbye, my friend. You will be deeply missed, and forever remembered.”

In further updates, Nana spent more than four decades in films and theatre, gradually becoming known for a screen presence that was difficult to imitate. Whether he was playing a hard-edged cop, a troubled man or a comic character, he brought a certain intensity that became his trademark.

On top of that, His filmography included acclaimed performances in Krantiveer, Agneepath, Ab Tak Chhappan and The Attacks of 26/11. At the same time, films such as Welcome showed audiences his ability to bring humour and warmth to mainstream cinema. His performances in films including Parinda and Salaam Bombay! also established him as one of the most formidable actors of his generation.

Even in his later years, Patekar continued to remain connected to the movie industry. He appeared in Housefull 5 alongside Akshay Kumar, Abhishek Bachchan and Riteish Deshmukh. He also played a police officer in Vishal Bhardwaj's O' Romeo , starring Shahid Kapoor and Triptii Dimri, and made a cameo in Subedar with Anil Kapoor and Radhika Madan.

title: ‘Swear on your mom’: Nana Patekar didn't want to hear Welcome story, here's how Anees Bazmee convinced him to play Uday Shetty. Watch
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Nana Patekar passed away at the age of 75 on October 8, leaving behind a legacy of some of the most iconic roles and performances in Indian cinema. While he was known for playing gritty, intense characters, often portraying the quintessential angry man troubled by the country's realities, Nana also had a terrific comic side. He made audiences laugh with his impeccable comic timing in films such as Welcome and Welcome Back. However, not many know how the star came on board Welcome and what convinced him to play the unforgettable Uday Shetty.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar in Welcome with Akshay Kumar and Katrina Kaif. How Anees Bazmee convinced Nana Patekar for Welcome During an appearance on The Kapil Sharma Show Season 2, filmmaker Anees Bazmee revealed how he convinced Nana Patekar to essay the role of Uday in Welcome. He shared he had always been a fan of Nana and believed that whenever the veteran star took up a comedy role, he would excel and show audiences how comedy was meant to be done. Anees also recalled his hilarious conversation with Nana over the phone. He shared, "I called him and told him I want to meet you. He replied, 'Kai ko? (Why?)' I told him that I want to narrate a movie to you."

Meanwhile, However, when Anees went to Nana's house to narrate the movie, the veteran star told him, "I don't want to listen to the story, you swear on your mom that this movie is right for me and I should do it." Anees, however, insisted that Nana read the script and went on to narrate the story to him for nearly three hours.

Notably, Anees opened up that Nana hugged him after hearing the narration and told him, "Main kacchi mitti hai, tere set pe aayega, jis roop mein dhalna hai dhaal lena (I’m like wet clay. I’ll come to your set, and you can mould me into whatever form you want)." Anees added that while people often say Nana had a temper and was difficult to work with, he found the veteran star to be one of the easiest actors to work with.

As per the latest buzz, Nana Patekar’s performance as Uday Shetty in Welcome (2007) remains one of the most memorable comic turns of his career. Directed by Anees Bazmee, the movie saw Nana step away from the intense, serious roles he was often associated with and embrace comedy. As Uday, Nana played a feared underworld don who desperately wants to get his sister Sanjana married into a respectable family. Uday could intimidate almost anyone, but became helpless and increasingly frustrated when it came to his sister’s love life.

In further updates, Nana’s chemistry with Anil Kapoor, who played his partner-in-crime Majnu Bhai, became the heart of the movie. Their constant arguments and exaggerated reactions won over the internet and made their characters iconic. Uday Shetty's lines such as "Control, Uday, control" and "Kya karun, maar bhi nahi sakta isse, pyaar jo karta hai mujhse" became part of popular culture.

On top of that, The movie, which also featured Akshay Kumar, Paresh Rawal, Katrina Kaif and Anil Kapoor in lead roles, emerged as a huge ticket-window success. Nana was also a part of the movie's sequel, Welcome Back, but didn't feature in the recent movie of the franchise, Welcome To The Jungle.

On October 8, Nana was brought to the hospital around 4.30 am and was declared dead by 5.30 am. Despite attempts to revive him, including cardiac massage for 45 minutes to an hour, he could not be saved, the doctor from Manipal Hospital revealed.

title: ‘Renowned shot’: How Nana Patekar became a national-level shooter, won medals in his 50s
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

When you mention shooting with reference to an star, chances are you mean the kind with a camera. But for Nana Patekar , the word was relevant in its other meaning too. A National Award-winning star, Nana was also a professional shooter, competing in the rifle shooting competition at state and national levels for decades. His prowess in shooting even collected him the title of a ‘renowned shot’.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar competed and won medals in rifle shooting competitions nationally. Nana Patekar’s tryst with shooting Nana’s move to shooting was late in his life. He began to practise with a rifle only in his 40s. Recalling how he began his shooting journey, he told Times of India in 2011, “I used to be the chief guest in all the prize distribution ceremonies of shooting competitions. I tried my hand at a lot of guns, and my aim improved. I started hitting tiny targets like a mineral bottle caps.”

Meanwhile, Around 2001, when he was 49, he turned to competitions. Nana competed in the 50m rifle prone and 300m big-bore events, training extensively at ranges such as Balewadi in Pune and Mhow. His experience training with the Indian Army for his 1991 movie Prahaar made him a natural at this.

Notably, In 2004, Nana won a silver medal in the 300m big-bore event at the 48th National Shooting Championships held at the BSF's Reoti Range in Indore. Three years later, he won the team bronze with Maharashtra, scoring 549/600 and finishing 13th out of 49 participants in the same competition. His performance in 2007 collected him the title of ‘renowned shot’. The tag meant that the star could import a rifle duty-free. "Let me get this new rifle, I can assure you I will shoot 590 points out of 600," Nana had shared back then, with unabashed cockiness.

As per the latest buzz, Nana continued to participate in National and State-level shooting events till into his 60s. Even after that, he would shoot recreationally, practising at various ranges around the country. The star was known to carry his equipment to outdoor shoots whenever he found a range nearby.

title: All about Nana Patekar’s family: Wife Neelakanti Patekar cleared IIT entrance but chose theatre, won awards and returned to cinema with Chhaava
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Veteran star Nana Patekar died in the early hours of Thursday after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa.

Adding to this, Who is Neelakanti Patekar? All about Nana Patekar’s wife, IIT connection, acting career, awards and Chhaava role. For decades, Nana was one of Indian cinema’s most recognisable actors, known for performances that could be fierce, vulnerable, unpredictable and completely different from one movie to another. But away from the screen and the constant attention that came with his stardom, he kept one part of his life particularly private: his marriage to Neelakanti Patekar.

Meanwhile, Nana and Neelakanti as per reports met through Marathi theatre. At the time, Neelakanti was working as a bank officer while continuing to explore acting. Their friendship gradually grew into a relationship, and the two got married in 1978, when Nana was still working his way up in the movie industry.

Notably, Their marriage began with happy years, but they also faced an unbearable personal tragedy. The couple had a son, but their first child died at just two and a half years old. They later welcomed their second son, Malhar.

As per the latest buzz, The loss became one of the most difficult chapters of their lives. They continued to move forward with their respective careers and family life, but their relationship changed over the years. Eventually, Nana and Neelakanti began living separately, while remaining married.

In further updates, Although Nana and Neelakanti remained married, they eventually began living separately. Nana has spoken about their relationship in the past and acknowledged that their marriage had gone through a difficult period.

On top of that, In an interview reported by Indian Express, Nana shared, “Neelkanti and I shared numerous years of happiness together. We supported each other through thick and thin. But, over the years, we developed certain irreconcilable differences and grew apart. Today, we continue to be married but stay separately.”

Born in Pune, Neelakanti grew up moving between cities as her father, who worked in the Central Excise Department, was transferred frequently. She studied Physics and, at her father’s urging, appeared for the IIT entrance examination. She cleared the exam, but chose not to pursue that route.

title: CJP Bengaluru protest LIVE updates: ‘We’ll hit streets till CEC Kumar resigns', says Dipke, Dhruv Rathee also on stage
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Bengaluru CJP protest LIVE updates: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke speaks in the presence of YouTuber Dhruv Rathee during the party's protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Freedom Park, in Bengaluru on Thursday. Bengaluru CJP protest LIVE updates: The Freedom Park protest, revealed by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) row, has begun. CJP leaders, along with Dhruv Rathee and Prakash Raj, reached the protest site, following which video testimonials on SIR exclusions were played. The demonstration is also expected to witness a People's Tribunal where people from across Karnataka are expected to raise concerns over alleged wrongful deletions from voter lists. A “Chappal protest” will follow. ...Read More

Adding to this, Star and activist Prakash Raj is participating in the protest, while YouTuber Dhruv Rathee has been revealed as a special guest. Rathee verified his participation after Prakash Raj revealed his presence at Freedom Park. JNU student leader Aishe Ghosh, Neha Bora, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and other youth and civil society representatives are also expected to attend. The CJP and allied groups have demanded that deletions made during the SIR exercise be scrapped and the pre-SIR electoral rolls retained. They have also sought the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging irregularities in the electoral process. Dhruv Rathee says ‘not here for regime change’ YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was among the popular faces who joined the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s Bengaluru protest on Thursday. In his first remarks at the stir, he shared he did not participate in the protest for ‘regime change", news agency PTI reported. Slamming the Election Commission of India (ECI) over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), he alleged that there is ‘zero transparency and zero accountability’ from the poll body. Star Prakash Raj's request to people for partcipation in anti-CEC stir On Wednesday, star Prakash Raj Raj urged the people to participate in Bengaluru's anti-CEC protest called by the CJP as he also revealed Dhruv Rathee's participation. “Please come in large numbers! Stand with all the cockroaches who will be there. Aishe Ghosh will be there. Neha Bora will be there. All young organisations will be there. Civil Society will be there. And the victims of SIR from across the districts of Karnataka will be there. Let's come together to raise our voice in solidarity against this draconian SIR," Raj shared in the video. 'People's tribunal' at Freedom Park Raj also opened up that a "people' tribunal" will held in Bengaluru in which "victims of SIR" from across Karnataka will be present. Raj, a critic of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, took to social media to make the announcement. "People's Tribunal by Cockroaches (Cockroach Janata Party)..Dipke...Ashuthosh.. Sourav and all the youth organisations and the civil society...the victims of SIR from across the state will be present." "Requesting all the citizens to participate in this fight to save our democracy. Come join us tomorrow, 8th October at Freedom Park... Bengaluru," he shared.
Meanwhile, Bengaluru CJP protest LIVE updates: "Who are they to take away our votes? This is serious wrongdoing," star Prakash Raj alleged, raising slogans of "Vote chor, gaddi chor."
Notably, Raj shared the issue was not simply about the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, but about scrapping the SIR.

As per the latest buzz, "Our fight is not merely for the resignation of Kumar. Even if he goes, another person, Agyanesh Kumar, may come in his place. That's not what we want. We want the SIR to be scrapped totally," he shared.

In further updates, Bengaluru CJP protest LIVE updates: Star-activist Prakash Raj on Thursday demanded scrapping the SIR exercise, alleging it was not merely about deletion of votes, but an attack on the dignity and rights of citizens.

On top of that, CEC Gyanesh Kumar is "acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah," he alleged, addressing a protest christened 'people's tribunal,' held by civil societies and the CJP here against the SIR.

Raj hitting out at the Centre, and the EC for "insulting the voters", shared politicians approached voters every five years seeking their blessings and votes, but they were now being forced to seeks restoration of their votes.

title: Security tightened ahead of INDIA bloc protest against Gyanesh Kumar for 3rd day
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Security has been tightened around Sansad Marg, Ashoka Road, Janpath Road and other parts of central Delhi ahead of the Opposition Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA)’s protest for a third day on Thursday against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police have deployed around 5,000 personnel and barricaded roads. The government has also approved the deployment of additional central paramilitary forces in Delhi.

Adding to this, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra staging a sit-in against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Wednesday. (PTI) The Le Meridien roundabout, where protesters gathered on Wednesday, was also being covered as part of the security arrangements. Police shared they have scanned footage from 150 body cameras worn during the protest and found footage of their personnel being targeted.

Meanwhile, Officials shared police had little time to make arrangements around the roundabout on Wednesday as the protest was largely impromptu. The deployment has now been strengthened in anticipation of a larger gathering on Thursday.

Notably, The Opposition has hit the streets of the national capital since Tuesday. On Wednesday, Opposition lawmakers protested for over three hours, bringing central Delhi to a halt to push for Kumar’s resignation.

As per the latest buzz, Police on Tuesday registered a case against Congress leaders for entering the headquarters of the All India Radio while trying to march to the Election Commission of India (ECI) office.

In further updates, On Wednesday, police alleged that some Congress leaders manhandled women police personnel, bit male staff and attacked other personnel during the protest. Congress leaders alleged that their lawmakers and workers were dragged, thrashed and shoved into buses, resulting in injuries.

On top of that, HT reported the Union home ministry approved the deployment of 110 central paramilitary force companies in Delhi from October 8 to 12. As many as 111 companies have already been deployed. The Central Reserve Police Force will provide the largest contingent, with 85 companies. The deployment of seven companies of its specialised anti-riot unit, the Rapid Action Force (RAF), has also been approved.

The Indo-Tibetan Border Police will send seven companies, the Sashastra Seema Bal 10, and the Central Industrial Security Force one company from Thursday. One paramilitary company has a sanctioned strength of 120-130 personnel, of whom around 75-80 are generally deployed.

title: Paresh Rawal once revealed Nana Patekar demanded ₹1 crore salary when even heroes hesitated for it, made producer wash dishes after serving him mutton
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Veteran star Nana Patekar died at the age of 75, leaving behind a career that defied the usual rules of the movie industry. He was never an star who needed to play the conventional hero to command attention. Last year, star Paresh Rawal offered a glimpse into the rare stature Nana enjoyed, even as a character artiste. He recalled a time when Nana demanded ₹ 1 crore rupees for a role, a figure even leading heroes were hesitant to ask for at the time, and remarkably, he got it. Paresh also shared a hilarious anecdote that perfectly captured Nana's unapologetic personality.

Adding to this, Paresh Rawal recalled how Nana Patekar once made producer clean dishes. Nana Patekar made producer was dishes In a conversation with Lallantop in 2025, Paresh spoke about what set Nana apart from other character artistes and recalled the incident involving the producer. He shared Nana once asked for ₹ 1 crore rupees at a time when even leading heroes were hesitant to demand such a fee, and ended up getting the amount despite being a character artiste.

Meanwhile, He then recalled how Nana once made a producer wash the dishes after having a meal at his house. Paresh shared in Hindi, “There is a producer, I won’t take the name. Nana told him, come home. He asked, ‘Do you eat mutton?’ He ate. Nana shared, ‘You ate, right? Now go clean the dishes.’ This is Nana Patekar, Baap hai voh (He’s a legend). He’s completely different, man. That soil is different. He had taken one crore rupees rupees, and at that time, there was a huge uproar. Heroes didn’t used to demand that amount. Nana Patekar asked for it, and got it.”

Notably, Nana died at the age of 75 at his residence in Goa after suffering a cardiac arrest. He was rushed to hospital, but doctors could not save him despite attempting cardiac massage for 45 minutes to an hour. A doctor at Manipal Hospital told ANI that the veteran star had texted and called a friend at around 2.30am after feeling unwell. However, by the time his friend reached his residence, Nana had become unconscious.

As per the latest buzz, Nana's career in the movie industry spanned more than four decades. After making his movie debut with Gaman in 1978, he gradually established himself through powerful performances in films such as Salaam Bombay!, Parinda, Krantiveer and Agni Sakshi. His performance in Parinda collected him the National Movie Award for Best Supporting Star, while Krantiveer won him the National Movie Award for Best Star.

In further updates, Over the years, Nana proved that he did not need to be the conventional leading man to dominate a movie. From gritty dramas such as Ab Tak Chhappan and Apaharan to comic turns in Welcome and Welcome Back, he repeatedly demonstrated his versatility and left a lasting impression whenever he appeared on screen.

title: How did Nana Patekar die? Doctor reveals actor's final hours, says he texted friend at 2:30 am before slowly losing consciousness
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The entertainment industry is in shock following the sudden death of veteran star Nana Patekar at the age of 75. The star suffered a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa and was rushed to Manipal Hospital, but doctors could not save him. Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, has now shared details of what happened in the moments leading up to the star's death.

Adding to this, Doctor reveals what happened before Nana Patekar died. Moments before Nana Patekar's death The doctor told ANI, "Nana Patekar was brought dead to the hospital around 4:30, and he was declared dead by 5:30. We tried our best to save him, but he was brought dead. Cardiac massage was given for 45 minutes to 1 hour, but he just couldn't be saved."

Meanwhile, The doctor then revealed what happened before the veteran star's death, saying, "As per what we recalled, at around 2:30, he sent a message to his friend that he was not feeling well. But as it was nighttime, his friend could not see the message. So he just called him. He went to his house at around 4 o'clock. By that time, he was sweating and all. They moved him, all those primary things. But he was slowly becoming unconscious... So they sent his caretaker to the hospital... He took our ambulance."

Notably, When the emergency team reached Nana's residence, he was given cardiac massage but remained unresponsive. The doctor added, "They shifted him to our hospital at around 4:20 or 4:30 am. We also tried our best, but he was brought dead. Then we had to file a police case because there's an MLC (medico-legal case). The body has now been taken to the Goa Medical College for post-mortem. His family was not there. His friends were there with him and a caretaker."

As per the latest buzz, Nana is survived by his wife, Neelkanti, and son, Malhar Patekar. The veteran star also had two brothers, Ashok and Dilip Patekar. Tributes from across the Indian movie industry poured in following the star's sudden death. Jr NTR, Akshay Kumar , Riteish Deshmukh, Kiara Advani and Rakul Preet Singh were among the celebrities who took to social media to express their grief.

In further updates, The veteran star was last seen on the big screen in O'Romeo. Helmed by Vishal Bhardwaj , the movie also featured Shahid Kapoor, Triptii Dimri and Farida Jalal in key roles. Rolled out in February this year, the movie failed to make a mark at the ticket-window, although Nana's performance was appreciated by critics.

On top of that, Apart from this, the star was also seen in two OTT projects, including a cameo in the Prime Video movie Subedaar and the series Sankalp. Directed by Prakash Jha, Sankalp was a socio-political drama that also featured Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub, Kubbra Sait and others in key roles. The show is available to watch on MX Player.

title: Nana Patekar dies: A titan who challenged Bollywood's perception of 'hero' and changed the grammar of cine acting
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

There are stars, there are superstars, and then there are artistes. In a career spanning almost 50 years, Nana Patekar never strived to be anything more than an star. And that is what made him an artiste, perhaps one of the finest Hindi cinema has seen. For a man like him to emerge in the 80s, challenge the notion of what a ‘ Bollywood hero’ is supposed to look like and then change the rules by which the game was played was no mean feat. Nana’s success paved the way for many actors, who did not want to take the ‘road more travelled’ to stardom.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar, a three-time National Award winner, died aged 75 on Thursday morning. Not a star, but an star Born Vishwanath Patekar into a Marathi family in 1951, Nana began his acting career in his late 20s. There was no grand launch, no face on the giant poster, but a quiet debut with the 1978 Marathi movie, Mimagaman. He worked in several Marathi films in the next few years, before playing Nathuram Godse in a small role in the British television series Lord Mountbatten: The Last Viceroy. In the mid-80s, as his acting began to be appreciated, Nana’s screen time increased. One of the earliest Hindi films that got him noticed was Aaj Ki Awaz (1984). And then, two years later, Ankush happened.

Meanwhile, The 1986 movie, directed by N Chandra, focused on four unemployed young men whose wayward ways are corrected by a mother and a daughter in their neighbourhood. When the daughter is sexually assaulted, the youngsters take the law into their own hands. Nana’s energetic performance, fast-talking dialogue delivery, and pensieve stare made him stand out. This was the role that gave rise to what would later become the Nana template.

Notably, As the 90s rolled in, Nana had established himself as an acclaimed star. His appearance in Mira Nair’s Oscar-nominated 1987 movie Salaam Bombay collected him praise. And then, for Parinda, he collected his first National Movie Award for Best Supporting Star. But the tag ‘supporting star’ stuck. His performances were being lauded, but he was almost always cast alongside more ‘saleable’ names in big films. He decided to change that himself.

As per the latest buzz, In 1991, Nana turned director with Prahaar, the story of a retired Army officer who decides to dole out justice in his own way. The movie featured Madhuri Dixit alongside Nana, who starred in the lead role himself. The movie was a moderate success at the ticket-window and later became a cult favourite on cable TV. Tiranga and Krantiveer completely transformed him into a ticket-window draw in the mid-90s. The former was a masala action movie in which he starred alongside the veteran Raaj Kumar. The latter was a social drama in which he played another renegade vigilante. Krantiveer also gave one of Nana’s earliest ‘widely shared’ scenes. Despite not looking the part and not acting like a star, Nana Patekar was one, now. For Krantiveer, he won the Best Star National Award. He was a leading man, now.

In further updates, Throughout the 90s and 2000s, Nana starred in smaller films and appeared in supporting roles in blockbusters, balancing both aspects of his career and refusing to be assigned a single label. Was he a ‘hero’ or a ‘character star’? Nobody could box him. In 2004, he played his last major leading role in a commercially successful movie, Ab Tak Chhappan.

On top of that, Nana Patekar had dabbled in comedy in the 90s as well. His performance in the famous Love Rap from Krantiveer was on TV sets for months, a cultural phenomenon. But till the 2000s, comedy was a part of his repertoire in a role. In 2007, he appeared in Welcome, an ensemble comedy in which he played his zaniest role to date. Uday Shetty became an icon, and Nana Patekar proved that he was more than just a ‘serious’ star. Performances in Bluffmaster, Phir Hera Pheri, and Hattrick had already hinted at his superior comic timing.

As accomplished an star as Nana was, row followed him. In 2008, Tanushree Dutta accused the star of sexually harassing her on the sets of the movie Horn 'Ok' Pleassss. She filed a complaint with CINTAA (Cine & TV Artists Association) that year, repeating the allegation in 2013 and 2018. Nana denied all allegations. In 2018, CINTAA apologised to Tanushree, admitting that the "chief grievance of sexual harassment wasn't even addressed (in 2008)" but added that since the case was more than three years old, they could not reopen it.

title: Akshay Kumar mourns the death of Welcome co-star Nana Patekar: ‘It’s hard to believe you're gone, Nana ji'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Meanwhile, Akshay specifically remembered working with Patekar on Welcome, the 2007 comedy in which the two shared screen space alongside Anil Kapoor, Katrina Kaif , Paresh Rawal and Mallika Sherawat. Nana’s portrayal of Uday Shetty became one of the most iconic performances of the movie, while Akshay played Rajiv.
Notably, “I feel fortunate that we got to work together in Welcome, and then again more of late in Housefull 5. There are so many memories from those sets that I’ll always hold close,” Akshay wrote.
As per the latest buzz, Akshay further described Patekar as “truly one of a kind” and shared it was difficult to come to terms with his death.
In further updates, “It’s hard to believe you’re gone. Thank you for all the memories. You will be missed more than words can say,” he added.
On top of that, Patekar’s death has left the Hindi movie industry mourning the loss of one of its most acclaimed performers, whose career spanned decades.

title: When Nana Patekar quit films at peak of his career to fight in Kargil War, lost 20 kg at the front serving Indian Army
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The death of star Nana Patekar sent shockwaves across the industry and the nation on Thursday morning. The 75-year-old passed away after a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, his son Malhar verified to local media. A three-time National Award winner, Nana was known as much for his powerhouse performances as he was for his philanthropy and his association with the Indian Army. The star was part of the Territorial Army and often raised funds for veterans and their families.
Adding to this, But unlike most actors, Nana's love for the Army sent him to the frontlines during war, in what is one of the most extraordinary stories from the Kargil War .

Meanwhile, In 1999, as the Kargil War raged on, the Indian armed forces battled in the harsh terrain of Kargil against the Pakistani forces. At this juncture, Nana Patekar, already a two-time National Award winner by this point, paused his career and sought special permission from the Defence Minister to go to the frontlines.

Notably, Earlier this year, the star appeared on Kaun Banega Crorepati, where he told Amitabh Bachchan how he came to serve at the front during the Kargil War. Nana had lived and trained with the Maratha Light Infantry of the Army for three years in the early 90s while writing his movie Prahaar. When the Kargil War broke out, he reached out to the senior officers from the division, requesting to join the men on the front, but he was denied. He was told that only the defence minister could approve it.

As per the latest buzz, "I knew our Defence Minister George Fernandes ji, so I called him," Nana recalled on KBC, "Even he shared it is impossible. I told him that even though the training for commission is six months, I trained for three years. He was surprised and asked me about it. After learning of my experience with the Maratha Light Infantry, he asked me, ‘When do you want to go?’

In further updates, Nana spent over a fortnight at the front close to the LoC in August 1999, helping the soldiers and even working in the hospital at the base for a few days. The star recalled being part of the Quick Response Team (QRT) during his time in Kargil. "I was 76 kg when I reached Srinagar. By the time I came back, I was 56 kg," he recalled when talking about the gruelling circumstances there.

On top of that, Nana Patekar’s son, Malhar Patekar, verified to local media that the star died on October 8 morning. Nana was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, and was rushed to Manipal Hospital. Doctors attempted to revive the star for around 45 minutes but were unsuccessful. The star was declared dead at around 5:20 am, with doctors citing a heart attack as the cause of death.
