title: ‘Don’t know if I’ll be here tomorrow’: Nana Patekar's final public appearance was just 4 days before cardiac arrest, spoke about mortality
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Nana Patekar died in the early hours of Thursday after suffering a cardiac arrest at his Goa residence. According to Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Department of Oncology at Manipal Hospital, the star was found unconscious at his apartment and was rushed to a private medical facility.

Adding to this, **EDS: FILE IMAGE** Veteran star Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026, at the age of 75 after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. Patekar is seen during the trailer launch of his movie 'O'Romeo', in Mumbai, in this file photo dated Wednesday, Jan. 21, 2026. (PTI Photo)(PTI10_08_2026_000002A) (PTI) Doctors attempted to revive him for around 45 minutes, but the star could not be saved. He was declared dead at approximately 5:10 am. Dr Salkar shared the star remained in asystole, meaning there was no electrical activity in the heart, throughout the resuscitation efforts. A medico-legal case has been registered and authorities are expected to conduct a post-mortem examination. Just days before his death, Nana Patekar spoke publicly in Goa about life, mortality and whether he was doing enough with the time he had.

Meanwhile, The veteran star, who died at 75, had attended the Samraat Club International installation ceremony in Dona Paula on October 4. Dressed in a white kurta and scarf, he addressed the gathering and spoke about former Goa chief minister Manohar Parrikar, whom he remembered as a close friend. His comments about how little time any person is guaranteed now carry a different weight following his death.

Notably, Speaking at the event, he shared, “Pramod Sawant is the Chief Minister of Goa. During your father's time, Manohar Parrikar was my friend. I was proud to call him my friend. He was younger than me, but his stature was such that you had to look up to him. It is unfortunate, but we were lucky that such a person was born among us and that he chose to do what he did. He had taken up a mission. There are so many people who dedicate themselves to a cause. How great is it that, within such a short life, someone can accomplish so much? He would even take a gas cylinder and go there, and then go back to that bridge and do what had to be done. You need to have that kind of passion and determination.”

As per the latest buzz, He added, “We all have to go someday. I don't know whether I will be here tomorrow or not. Every person's life will eventually reach that point. But before that happens, I have to ask myself: am I able to do what I want to do?”

In further updates, Nana went on to speak about his own responsibilities and whether a person's world should remain limited to their family and immediate surroundings. He also spoke about political views, protest and the need to disagree without losing basic decency.

On top of that, “I have to ask myself whether I have tried. If my world is limited to my children, my wife and my home, then what is my purpose? I have to give something back here, don't I? I like some of Narendra Modi's ideas and I don't like some of them. We should learn to say that. He does not always get everything wrong. What is a protest ultimately? It is when something does not feel right to us, when something is not happening the way it should. Even a small child cries when it is hungry. That is its way of protesting. The definition of protest should change with age, shouldn't it? If I don't like something, I must speak about it. But there is a way of speaking. If I have something to say about you, I will never use filthy, abusive or offensive words against anyone. Don't speak in public with anger and abuse. Among friends, we may fight, grab each other and say things to one another, but that should remain between us. When we speak publicly, there has to be some basic decency. That has to be maintained, otherwise there is no meaning to it,” he shared.
At a recent event, Nana was seen having fun and was playing Shamel, a traditional Goan percussion instrument, during an event in Panaji, Goa.

title: Nana Patekar dies at 75 due to cardiac arrest; was found unconscious at Goa residence
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Nana Patekar , one of the most respected performers in Hindi and Marathi cinema, has died at the age of 75. The star, whose career spanned more than four decades, was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, following a cardiac arrest.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar Patekar was as per reports taken to Manipal Hospital after being found unconscious at his home. Doctors attempted to revive him through continuous cardiopulmonary resuscitation for around 45 minutes, but he could not be revived. He was declared dead at around 5:20 am on Thursday. Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, verified the death to ANI.

Meanwhile, Born Vishwanath Patekar on January 1, 1951 in Maharashtra, Nana began his movie career with the 1978 drnama Gaman. He went on to establish himself as an star capable of bringing unusual intensity to his performances.

Notably, His breakthrough came with films such as Salaam Bombay! and Parinda. He later delivered acclaimed performances in films including Prahaar: The Final Attack, Tirangaa, Krantiveer, Agni Sakshi, Khamoshi: The Musical and Ab Tak Chhappan.

As per the latest buzz, Patekar's performance as Krantiveer collected him the National Movie Award for Best Star, while his work in Agni Sakshi brought him another National Movie Award for Best Supporting Star. He also became a hugely popular mainstream star through films such as Welcome, where his portrayal of the eccentric gangster Uday Shetty introduced his work to a new generation of audiences.

In further updates, Beyond acting, Patekar was also a director and theatre artiste. He directed Prahaar: The Final Attack, a movie centred on the lives and struggles of soldiers. His contribution to cinema and the arts was recognised with the Padma Shri in 2013.

title: Nana Patekar passes away: Last rites to be held at actor's farmhouse
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

SUMMARY Veteran star Nana Patekar, one of Indian cinema’s celebrated performers, passed away in Goa on Thursday, October 8. He was 75. An official confirmation from Manipal Hospital, Goa, verified to ANI that the star was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula and was rushed to the hospital. He was as per reports declared dead on arrival. As per various reports doing the rounds online, the star, known for his powerful performances across Hindi and Marathi cinema, was rushed to the hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him. According to Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, medical teams performed CPR for around 45 minutes. He was sadly declared dead at 5:20 am. While the current cause of death is reported to be a cardiac arrest, an official post-mortem report establishing the cause of death, is awaited. Born Vishwanath Patekar, Nana Patekar was one of the most respected actors in Hindi and Marathi cinema. Over a career spanning several decades, he was known for his powerful performances and distinctive screen presence. Patekar made his Hindi movie debut with 'Gaman' in 1978 and went on to deliver acclaimed performances in films including 'Parinda', 'Prahaar: The Final Attack', 'Krantiveer', 'Agni Sakshi', 'Khamoshi: The Musical', 'Ab Tak Chhappan', 'Apaharan' and 'Natsamrat'. He was a recipient of three National Movie Awards and several other honours, and was awarded the Padma Shri in 2013 for his contribution to cinema and the arts. He shared he learned about the star's passing immediately after completing a performance. "I had just finished our performance and taken the curtain call. As I walked into the wings, my director Gajendra told me, “Nana is no more.”????" Anupam Kher shared he continued with his professional commitments despite struggling to process the news. "After that, I had to meet people, pose for photographs, smile, sit down for a meal… while trying to absorb what I had just heard. It was terribly difficult." 11:48 (IST) Oct 08 Nana Patekar funeral: From Vishwanath Patekar to Nana Patekar Nana Patekar was born Vishwanath Patekar into a Marathi family in Murud-Janjira, in Maharashtra's Raigad district. Movies such as 'Krantiveer', 'Prahaar', 'Ab Tak Chhappan', 'Natsamrat' and 'Welcome' became important milestones in his career. Patekar was also known for taking on characters that demanded emotional intensity. His performances often combined restraint, aggression and a distinctive dialogue delivery that became part of his identity as an star. 11:46 (IST) Oct 08 Nana Patekar cardiac arrest: Last rites to be held with state honours Ganesh Thorat also shared that Nana Patekar's last rites would be conducted with state honours. The decision reflects the star's standing in Maharashtra and his contribution to Indian cinema. Patekar built a career across Marathi and Hindi cinema, earning recognition for his intense performances and distinctive screen presence. He also remained connected with theatre and social causes throughout his career. His passing has prompted tributes from several colleagues, actors and public figures from across the country. Many remembered his acting ability, forthright personality and contribution beyond films. 11:45 (IST) Oct 08 Nana Patekar funeral: Nana Patekar's contribution to Indian cinema Nana Patekar established himself as one of the most recognizable performers in Indian cinema. His career included critically acclaimed dramas, action films and mainstream entertainers. His notable films include 'Krantiveer', 'Agni Sakshi', 'Ab Tak Chhappan', 'Raajneeti', 'Natsamrat' and 'Welcome'. His performances collected him recognition across Hindi and Marathi cinema. 11:38 (IST) Oct 08 Rajinikanth SHOCKED to learn about Nana Patekar's demise: 'Can’t believe my dear friend Nanaji is no longer with us' Superstar Rajinikanth expressed shock at the death of veteran star Nana Patekar, saying he couldn't believe his “dear friend” was “no longer with us.” Remembering the late star, Rajinikanth took to X and offered his condolences and prayed for his soul to rest in peace.
Adding to this, “I can’t believe my dear friend Nanaji is no longer with us. My deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. May his soul rest in peace,” Rajinikanth tweeted.

Manikandan, Dileepan, Nitish Veera, Sampath Raj and Ravi Kale.
Notably, The movie follows Karikalan "Kaala", the leader of Dharavi, who tries to save his land from getting seized and his people from being evicted by Haridev, a ruthless minister.

As per the latest buzz, President Droupadi Murmu and Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan on Thursday expressed grief over the passing of veteran star Nana Patekar and extended condolences to his family members.
In further updates, Nana Patekar, one of Indian cinema's most celebrated performers, passed away at the age of 75 in Goa.

On top of that, An official confirmation from Manipal Hospital, Goa, shared that the star was found unconscious at his Dona Paula -- Goa residence -- and was rushed to the hospital. Doctors declared him brought dead.

Taking to X, President Murmu shared, "Deeply saddened by the passing of veteran star Shri Nana Patekar. Through his powerful and deeply evocative performances, he brought to life a wide range of human experiences."

title: Nana Patekar dies at 75 after suffering from cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Veteran star Nana Patekar died on Thursday morning after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. The star was 75 when he breathed his last.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar dies at 75. While talking to local media, Malhar Patekar, son of Nana Patekar, verified that the veteran star passed away on October 8 at the age of 75. He was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. He was rushed to the Manipal Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival due to a heart attack.
Meanwhile, The veteran star was declared dead at around 5:20 am. Doctors at a private hospital attempted to revive him for about 45 minutes. However, they were unsuccessful.

Notably, Over a career spanning several over four decades, Nana Patekar has worked extensively in both Hindi and Marathi cinema, while also trying his hand at writing and direction. He was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2013 for his contribution to cinema and the arts.

As per the latest buzz, He made his Hindi movie debut with Muzaffar Ali’s Gaman in 1978 and gradually established himself as an star capable of making an impression even in relatively small parts. During the 1980s, Nana appeared in films such as Aaj Ki Awaaz, Ankush, Pratighaat, Andha Yudh, Mohre and Salaam Bombay!. His work in Salaam Bombay! (1988), directed by Mira Nair, brought him greater recognition. However, it was his performance as gangster Anna in Vidhu Vinod Chopra’s Parinda (1989) that became the major turning point in his career. His portrayal of the volatile crime lord collected him the National Movie Award for Best Supporting Star as well as the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Star.

In further updates, He made his directorial debut with Prahaar: The Final Attack, in which he also played an Army officer. Nana continued to take on varied roles in films such as Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman, Angaar and Tirangaa. In Angaar (1992), his portrayal of Majid Khan collected him the Filmfare Award for Best Villain. His biggest recognition of the decade came with Krantiveer (1994), in which he played Pratap Narayan Tilak, a troubled man who transforms into a force against corruption and injustice. The performance won him the National Movie Award for Best Star.

On top of that, Nana followed Krantiveer with another acclaimed phase of his career. In Agni Sakshi (1996), he played a psychologically complex character in a story centred on an abusive and obsessive husband. The performance collected him his second National Movie Award for Best Supporting Star.
The star was last seen in the movie Subedaar. Rolled out on Prime Videonin 2026, the movie also featured Anil Kapoor and Radhika Madan in lead roles.

title: Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus offices face Income Tax raids weeks before Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's film release
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Namit Malhotra is gearing up for the rollout of his soon-to-release movie, Ramayana . However, according to a report by CNBC-TV18, just a few weeks before its rollout, the Income Tax Department as per reports launched searches at the Mumbai offices of the filmmaker's company, Prime Focus Ltd.

Adding to this, Namit Malhotra backed Ramayana to rollout on Diwali 2026. IT Raids at Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios The Income Tax Department's action as per reports began on October 7 and continued into Wednesday morning, with searches also being carried out at the premises of individuals associated with Prime Focus. The searches are shared to be linked to certain foreign remittance transactions, although details about the specific transactions being examined have not been disclosed. The development also weighed on Prime Focus' stock, which as per reports dropped around 8% in morning trading on October 7.

Meanwhile, Founded by Namit Malhotra in 1997, Prime Focus Studios began in Mumbai and has since grown into a global company providing visual effects, post-production, animation and technology services to the movie and television industries.

Notably, Prime Focus is also closely associated with DNEG, the Oscar-winning visual-effects company that became part of the wider Prime Focus ecosystem. DNEG has won eight Oscars for Best Visual Effects, including for Inception, Interstellar, Blade Runner 2049, First Man, Tenet, Dune: Part One and Dune: Part Two. Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Ltd is now also backing Ramayana, which is being mounted as a global-scale cinematic spectacle.

As per the latest buzz, Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is an epic mythological movie based on Valmiki's ancient Sanskrit epic. The movie is backed by Namit Malhotra and Yash under Prime Focus Studios, Monster Mind Creations and DNEG. It stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Yash as Ravana, along with Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutta in key roles.

In further updates, Mounted on a reported budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees, the movie is shared to be one of the most expensive and ambitious projects in Indian cinema. Talking about the movie at San Diego Comic-Con, Namit shared, "Ramayana is like Avatar meets Gladiator in the world of Lord of the Rings like so if you can put that together. Lord Vishnu, who's the protector of all life, has to come as an avatar to bring balance and restore life back."

On top of that, He added, "So god descends as a human and goes through his life in a human form to really understand how humans feel, ultimately to fulfil their duty. Then it's mounted in the back of this massive spectacle woven into the fabric of the screenplay. It's all about emotions. The underdog story of sacrifice, of revenge, and absolutely cutting-edge execution. It's a story that is not only going to entertain you but also going to enlighten you."
The movie will rollout in two parts, with the first part hitting theatres on Diwali 2026.

title: Oppn protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation to continue in Delhi after day 2 of detentions
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Opposition hit the streets of the national capital for a second consecutive day on Wednesday to push for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation as lawmakers protested for more than three hours, bringing central Delhi to a halt and angering the Bharatiya Janata Party .

Adding to this, Around 6pm, the Gandhis and many Congress workers were bundled in buses and detained. (@INCIndia X) The Opposition – which already revealed another stir on Thursday - has also sought time from President Droupadi Murmu to discuss the controversial special intensive revision and Kumar’s removal.

Meanwhile, At least 200 lawmakers from the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA), packed in three buses, first had lunch in Janpath and then attempted to march to Jantar Mantar but were stopped by a 5,000-strong police force at the intersection of Janpath and Ashoka Road, triggering an impasse. The Samajwadi Party – the second-largest constituent of the bloc – was not a part of the protest.

Notably, For more than three hours, the buses carrying opposition leaders were not allowed to proceed, and the busy intersection was barricaded, bringing traffic to a halt on Ashoka Road, Raisina Road and Janpath.

As per the latest buzz, There was also an impromptu sit-in outside the Shangri La hotel at 4pm when the MPs were stopped by police, with Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lying flat on her back on the street, clutching a copy of the Constitution, with five-six leaders around her. Rahul Gandhi resisted police attempts to put him inside a van for detention. Other INDIA bloc leaders such as Mahua Moitra jostled with security personnel who tried to detain them.

In further updates, Around 6pm, the Gandhis and many Congress workers were bundled in buses and detained. Further drama ensued minutes later when a bus carrying Rahul Gandhi suffered a punctured tyre on KG Marg. After few minutes, another bus carried the MPs away. Gandhi was taken to the Barakhamba police station and he was rolled out around 8pm.
On top of that, Delhi police spokesperson shared a total 91 INDIA bloc leaders and workers were detained.

“We are not going to stop protesting till Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us,” Gandhi shared.

title: Soundarya Rajinikanth defends Katrina Kaif amid postpartum trolling: ‘You have to give that woman that respect’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Katrina Kaif , who welcomed her son Vihaan in November last year, has faced social media trolling over her postpartum weight gain after she made a public appearance on the occasion of Ganesh Chaturthi. Her appearance sparked online discussion, with several users sharing her before-and-after pregnancy photos and commenting on her looks. Several stars have spoken out in her support, with Soundarya Rajinikanth being the latest to address the scrutiny surrounding Katrina’s appearance after childbirth.

Adding to this, Soundarya Rajinikanth has defended Katrina Kaif. What Soundarya shared In an interaction with Nayandeep Rakshit on his YouTube channel, Soundarya Rajinikanth shared, “I have two children and it is not easy. When you have to go through that process, your body changes and having a child post a particular age is even more difficult. I had my second child when I was past my 35. Not easy. You have to give that woman that respect. Because what a woman can do physically, you can’t blame men because they can’t. It is not biology.”

Meanwhile, She went on to add, “But you need to accept and acknowledge that a woman does. We are not asking the guy, ‘Why don’t you get pregnant?’ But when we do go through that, my heart went out when that whole thing happened. It was not fair. It was not kind. Women go through a lot but it is special to be a woman.”

Notably, Soundarya, daughter of Rajinikanth and Latha, married businessman Ashwin in 2010, and their son, Ved, was born in 2015. The couple separated in 2016 and were granted a divorce in 2017. In 2019, the producer married businessman Vishagan. Their son, Veer, was born in 2022.

As per the latest buzz, Meanwhile, Salman Khan also criticised the trolls who body-shamed Katrina over her postpartum weight gain. He questioned why people were commenting on the star’s weight and appearance when she had of late become a mother. He shared, “Pregnant hone ke baad everyone puts on weight” (everyone puts on weight after becoming pregnant), adding that she would get fit again when she returned to films. He also shared Katrina should be allowed to spend time with her family.

In further updates, Katrina gave birth to her and Vicky Kaushal ’s son Vihaan in November 2025. Of late, Katrina was spotted at the Ambani family’s Ganesh Chaturthi celebration. Several videos and photos of her surfaced online, with many commenting on her weight gain after childbirth. Neither Katrina nor Vicky has reacted to the online chatter.

title: ‘Extremely difficult, nothing easy about it’: Saiyami Kher looks back on 10 years in Bollywood, says she misses watching stories with heart
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

It has been 10 years since Saiyami Kher debuted in Bollywood with Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra’s Mirzya. The movie might not have worked as intended, but from then till her recent rollout, Priyadarshan’s Haiwaan, the star says she has faced everything from nasty comments to being made to feel insecure. However, in an interview with Hindustan Times, she says that everything that followed it has always been worth it. “I’ve always wished to be an star for a long time,” she says.

Adding to this, Saiyami Kher says she faced nasty comments in the beginning of her career. From insecurity to feeling validated When I ask Saiyami to describe the feeling of being an star in Bollywood for 10 years, she says, “You know, when you climb a really high mountain, and the journey to the top is tough? But looking back from the top, the view is spectacular. It was tough, but it all feels worth it; that’s what it feels like.” She adds, “These ten years have been extremely difficult, and there has been nothing easy about it. When I started out, obviously, there were a lot of nasty comments passed. People are still brutal about beauty standards with the newcomers.”

Meanwhile, The star says that every time she has battled the insecurities that come with being an star, a filmmaker has validated her. “I feel extremely grateful that every time I doubted myself, questioned myself and my place in the industry, there has been a filmmaker to back me out of nowhere,” says Saiyami, adding, “From Rakesh sir to Anurag Kashyap to Neeraj Panday to R Balki to Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari, these were all filmmakers on my bucket list. And I got the chance to work with them.”

Notably, Saiyami hopes that the movie industry will learn to embrace realness, not just in beauty standards but also in its stories. “I feel that we need to celebrate realness much more. When I watch Tabu , she blows my mind away because of how real she is,” says the star, adding, “When it comes to cinema too, we had a phase from 2015 to the pandemic where we told such good stories. For me, that was real cinema.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Saiyami Kher (@saiyami)

In further updates, “I’m hoping that kind of cinema is celebrated again. I wish such real stories came back because that’s what I like watching. I just hope that we bring heart back to cinema, which I feel has been missing for a few years now. We are making these big films, but I don’t think they move anybody. I was a huge fan of Hrishikesh Mukherjee’s work. I liked the web series Gullak . I have been missing cinema like that as an audience,” Saiyami rounds off, with hope of a better next decade.

On top of that, Despite having a Master's degree in Journalism and over a decade of experience in print and digital media as a field reporter and sub-editor at organisations such as The Times of India and Reader's Digest, Neeshita Nyayapati remains a movie buff first and a Chief Content Producer second. She fell in love with movies in childhood and believes nothing matches the magic of watching a good movie that moves you with a warm tub of popcorn in hand. Her love for writing about cinema follows that. Come Friday, you'll find her at her happy place, the movies, catching the latest rom-com or masala offering, for reviews or otherwise. As for the rest of the week, she's here reporting the juiciest news in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada and Hindi or bringing out the best of celebs in interviews. While her niche is Telugu cinema, Neeshita likes to dabble in a little bit of everything to stay up to date. From movie announcements to scandals and hard news angles, she has explored it all. A good book, a comforting cup of hot chocolate, puppy kisses and a stunning beach view are all she needs to unwind. Her passion for biking and travelling has taken her to various places across the country. She has found peace in everything from the frozen lakes of Gangtok to the coffee plantations of Coorg and the dense forests of Bandipur, to the monasteries of Darjeeling. But no matter where she goes, Neeshita loves coming across inspiring and moving stories. Read More

Here’s a look at how the movie has performed at the ticket-window so far.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 6: Ajay Devgn’s biggest opener now eyes Drishyam 2's lifetime record. (HT_PRINT) Drishyam 3 midweek report card Last Friday, Drishyam 3 delivered a record opening for Ajay Devgn. By the end of the day, the movie went on to collect ₹ 66.75 crore rupees net across India. This is the third biggest opening by a Hindi movie ever and the biggest in Ajay Devgn’s career.

Meanwhile, While it dipped on Saturday, bringing in ₹ 53.50 crore rupees, the movie recovered on Sunday, bringing in ₹ 61 crore rupees. title: Ranbir Kapoor becomes the new brand ambassador of Mantra Group
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As part of the association, Ranbir will feature in a new brand movie alongside Rohit Gupta, Managing Director of Mantra Group. The partnership comes as the company looks to strengthen its presence across existing markets while exploring new opportunities in India and international markets.

Adding to this, Founded in Pune in 2007, Mantra Group has grown from a first-generation entrepreneurial venture into a larger real estate group over nearly two decades. While Pune continues to be an important market for the company, its portfolio has expanded across different segments and geographies.

Meanwhile, In recent years, Mantra has also entered new areas of business. The Group expanded internationally through its entry into branded residences in partnership with luxury brand Jacob & Co. Its entry into Mumbai has opened opportunities for large-format developments, while its presence in Pune has continued to grow across residential and luxury real estate.

Notably, The company has also built associations across design, architecture and luxury. Its luxury vertical Burgundy has worked with designer Manish Malhotra, while Ganti Associates is among the names associated with its developments.

As per the latest buzz, The partnership with Ranbir is based, in part, on similarities in the journeys of the star and the Group. Both began their respective journeys in 2007 and have since developed identities of their own. While Ranbir has taken on varied roles during his career, Mantra has expanded across markets, formats, design and development.

In further updates, Rohit Gupta, Managing Director, Mantra Group, shared, “When we started Mantra in 2007, our focus was on building a strong business in Pune and earning the trust of the families we served. Over the years, that foundation has given us the confidence to think beyond individual projects and look at what we can build as a Group. Today, we are at a very different point in that journey. We have expanded into new markets, entered new categories and built relationships with some of the most recognised names across luxury, design and lifestyle. Ranbir comes at a time when we felt the brand needed a personality who could represent this evolution. There are several parallels in the journeys we have taken, from starting out in the same year to building our own identities and constantly evolving. We are delighted to have him as the face of Mantra as we enter this next phase, with several important milestones ahead.”

On top of that, Ranbir Kapoor shared, “What appealed to me about Mantra is that it has built its journey over time, but has also continued to evolve. There is a clear ambition to grow, explore new markets and think differently about the spaces and experiences it creates. I also found the journey interesting because there are some parallels in how we have both built our identities over the years. Mantra has strong roots, but it is also looking ahead and creating its own space. I am happy to be part of this next chapter and look forward to what we build together.”

The association will be accompanied by one of Mantra's larger brand and consumer campaigns, titled ‘The Festival of Choices’. The campaign will bring the Group's portfolio together under one platform, with inventory opening across its projects and a range of consumer benefits across Mantra and Burgundy.

title: BJP claims Rahul Gandhi tried to push woman cop ‘in his eagerness to make a reel’ during Opposition protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi detained on way to Jantar Mantar; Priyanka refuses to budge | Track LIVE updates

In further updates, *Shri Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress President & Leader of Opposition (LoP), Rajya Sabha, addressed the media in New Delhi today.*

On top of that, Addressing the media, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge shared, "All of us in the INDIA alliance will stage a protest at Jantar Mantar today; all key leaders will be present together. We will continue to protest in this manner until our demands are met."

"Secondly, the Election Commission is repeatedly making mistakes at the behest of Modi ji. When Modi ji orchestrates such errors, it implies an attempt to destroy democracy in this country; he pays no heed to the Constitution. Therefore, we decided that it is our duty to convey the people's concerns to the entire nation. No matter how many cases are filed against us or how much intimidation is attempted, we will not be cowed; we will keep smiling and moving forward."

title: Prakash Raj urges people to join anti-SIR protest in Bengaluru with Abhijeet Dipke and Saurav Das, calls it ‘most important’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and activist Prakash Raj has been vocal about his criticism of the SIR process. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, has scheduled a mass Chappal protest and People's Tribunal at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on October 8, 2026, starting at 10:30 am. Prakash Raj has taken to his social media account to urge more people to join the protest and show solidarity.

Adding to this, Star Prakash Raj is expected to be present at the protest on October 8. (PTI Photo)(PTI10_03_2026_000411B) (PTI) What Prakash Raj shared Taking to X on Wednesday morning, Prakash Raj urged people to join the protest and shared, “Tomorrow. 8th October, Bengaluru Freedom Park. There is going to be a state-level tribunal where victims of SIR, who are the evidences, will come across the State, to Bangalore Freedom Park. All the cockroaches, Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and all the young youth organisations and the civil society of Karnataka will be there.”

Meanwhile, "Please come in big numbers. Attend this most important protest and the tribunal which is questioning SIR, which has created trauma to every citizen of this country. Especially those victims who have suffered in Bengaluru. Please come, and the general public… this is not just the question of vote. It is an attempt to kill democracy, our constitution. Come in large numbers and by evening, I will announce a special guest. A voice with a spine. You will be surprised, keep guessing. But tomorrow, we will be there from morning. Please walk in, stand and show your solidarity for this great protest which is erupting in the country against this draconian SIR," he added.

Notably, Meanwhile, Abhijeet Dipke left for Bengaluru to attend the People’s Tribunal on SIR and hold an interaction with local residents who were allegedly wrongfully removed from the voters’ list. On Thursday morning, he is scheduled to hold a ‘chappal protest’ at Freedom Park. On October 10, he is scheduled to hold a protest in Delhi and seek the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

As per the latest buzz, He assured all those willing to participate in the ongoing protests that they were not alone. “I just want you to know that you are not alone. None of us are. We are all in this together.” Dipke shared the larger objective should be to build a country where young people can raise their voices without their parents fearing for their safety. “I hope we can build an India where, someday, when our own children take to the streets to raise their voices, we won’t have to fear for their lives the way our parents fear for ours today,” he shared.

In further updates, The CJP on October 2 held a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged discrepancies in the SIR processes. The protest attracted a massive crowd, with celebrities, including Shabana Azmi, Naseeruddin Shah, Vishal Bhardwaj and Vishal Dadlani in participation. Earlier, speaking at the protest at Shivaji Park, a ground associated with landmark political rallies, Dipke warned of "Jantar Mantar 2.0" if Kumar did not step down.

title: Guneet Monga Kapoor-led Women in Film India and Google Flow join hands to enable AI-powered filmmaking for new creative possibilities
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Their joint-initiative will invite emerging and established storytellers to explore AI-powered filmmaking with Google Flow, and put their creative stories on screen.

Adding to this, The initiative will invite participants to experiment with AI-assisted filmmaking using Google Flow, giving them a space to develop original ideas, explore new visual possibilities and discover new ways to bring their stories to life. It is designed for filmmakers to learn, create, take risks and see how new tools can push their craft further.

Meanwhile, Operating as a comprehensive workspace built on Google’s advanced Gemini Omni and Veo models, Google Flow offers filmmakers an intuitive canvas to arrange scenes, batch edit clips and layer audio.

Notably, “WIF India is excited to create Filmathon with Google Flow because it gives filmmakers a real space to experiment,” shared Guneet Monga Kapoor, Founder and CEO, WIF India. “There is so much talent and so many stories waiting to be explored. We want to encourage filmmakers to stay curious, try new things and see where their ideas can go when they have access to a new creative tool. We are really looking forward to seeing the films that come from this.”

As per the latest buzz, “Google Flow is already gaining remarkable momentum in India. Through the Filmathon, in collaboration with WIF India, we can’t wait to see the short films storytellers across the country bring to life — and how they expand the boundaries of artistic expression through this technology,” shared Dr. Arathi Sethumadhavan, Director, International Activations & Product Insights, Technology & Society, Google.

In further updates, “Our collaboration with Google Flow gives filmmakers access to a new creative studio while keeping the most important part of filmmaking where it belongs: with the storyteller and the story. We are excited to see what filmmakers across the country create,” shared Rabia Chopra, Head of Programming and Strategy, WIF India.

On top of that, The Filmathon will bring together filmmakers at different stages of their journey - from people beginning to explore visual storytelling to established creatives looking to try something new. Through the programme, participants will have the opportunity to learn, experiment and create and their cinematic visions.

The selected top 5 films will be showcased at the International Movie Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa in 2026, bringing the Filmathon into conversation with India’s wider filmmaking community. It is an opportunity for filmmakers to move from experiment to screen, and for audiences and the movie industry to see how new tools are being used by storytellers in India.

title: Rahul Gandhi calls every FIR a "medal", sets target of 100 as opposition takes protest to Jantar Mantar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday described the criminal cases filed against him as a "medal", as opposition MPs moved to Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The protest follows a day of confrontation with Delhi Police and a closed door at the Election Commission, and it signals that the INDIA bloc intends to keep the pressure on well beyond a single sit-in.

Adding to this, Rahul Gandhi shared that Delhi Police registering FIR against him for protesting against CEC Gyanesh Kumar is a medal for him. (File Photo/PTI) "There are 45 FIRs against me, my goal is 100 FIRs. Every FIR is a medal for me," Gandhi shared. The remark came as Delhi Police registered a fresh case against him and Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with their supporters, for allegedly forcing their way into Akashvani Bhawan during the opposition's march against the CEC.
Meanwhile, Track live updates from protests over CEC Gyanesh Kumar row

Notably, The march is the latest step in the campaign by the INDIA bloc (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance) against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties allege that the exercise is stripping millions of genuine voters of their right to vote and that it forms part of a larger plan of "vote theft". The Election Commission has defended the SIR as a routine clean-up of voter lists, and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has rejected the charge.

As per the latest buzz, Gandhi shared the protest began after the Election Commission refused to engage with elected representatives. "Members of Parliament wanted to meet the Election Commissioners yesterday, specifically, the three Election Commissioners. They refused to meet us. The Delhi Police stopped us and shared that we could not protest there," he shared. The opposition says the refusal left MPs with no institutional route to raise their concerns.

In further updates, He then set out what the opposition will do on Wednesday and what it wants from the poll body. "Today, we intend to go to the designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, sit there, and declare to the nation that, for us, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar is not a legitimate Election Commissioner of this country," Gandhi shared. The declaration goes beyond a policy objection and challenges the standing of the man who heads the commission.

On top of that, Gandhi also widened the charge to the top of the government and the Sangh leadership. "Modi ji, Amit Shah ji, Mohan Bhagwat, and Gyanesh Kumar have destroyed the country's democracy," he shared, adding that those responsible are traitors and that action will be taken against them. "Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," he shared, leaving no room for a negotiated outcome.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge shared every INDIA alliance partner will join the demonstration and that the protest will continue until the demand is met. "Whatever the Election Commission is doing, Narendra Modi is behind it. That means Modi himself is trying to destroy democracy," Kharge shared. He added that party members want to go to the people and tell them that their rights are being snatched away.

title: ‘Like your movie, money is also Ata Pata Laapata’: CJI warns Rajpal Yadav over his conduct, says even actor's advocates could be cast in his films
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Rajpal Yadav appeared in person before the Supreme Court on Wednesday after the Court’s stern warning over his failure to deposit the amount due in a cheque-bounce case. As per the latest update from news agency ANI, the star told the Court that he would pay ₹ 2 crore rupees and showed a demand draft of ₹ 1.15 crore rupees. A buyer of his property, who is to pay the remaining ₹ 85 lakh, was also present in court.

Adding to this, Rajpal Yadav appeared before the Supreme Court over his failure to deposit the noted amount due in a cheque-bounce case. (File) (HT_PRINT) What the SC told Rajpal Yadav A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed Yadav to deposit ₹ 2 crore rupees towards the amount due to the complainant by October 13. The Court shared it would consider his plea against the Delhi High Court order which had convicted Yadav and imposed a three month sentence on him (for failing to make good payments against a loan from a private party) after the payment is made.

Meanwhile, Yadav’s counsel told the Court that he had gone to the Courts’ Registry to make the payment, but RTGS was not permissible. He therefore brought the ₹ 1.15 crore rupees demand draft. On the remaining ₹ 85 lakh, counsel shared the buyer of Yadav’s property was present and would make the payment.

Notably, The Court made it clear that the extensions were being granted only to secure payment to the complainant and warned Yadav over his conduct.“Law should not be utilised like this”, it shared. Justice Joymalya Bagchi questioned whether Yadav had suffered imprisonment and indicated that the Court could consider enhancement of his sentence.

As per the latest buzz, The case relates to a loan of around ₹ 5 crore rupees allegedly taken by Yadav from M/s Murli Projects Pvt Ltd in 2010 for his movie Ata Pata Laapata. Seven repayment cheques of ₹ 1.05 crore rupees each were subsequently dishonoured, leading to the cheque-bounce proceedings. The unpaid amount increased over the years with interest and other charges.

In further updates, After passing the order, the bench had an informal exchange with Yadav, who spoke about the losses suffered on account of Ata Pata Laapata. He shared around ₹ 200-250 crore rupees had been lost on the movie and that the producers had also suffered.

On top of that, The CJI referred to the movie’s title while commenting on the case. “Like your movie, your money is also Ata Pata Laapata, gayab (missing)”, the CJI remarked in jest. The CJI then advised him to make a good movie and entertain people. In jest, he added that advocates appearing before the Supreme Court were also good actors and could be cast in his films.
Rajpal Yadav also told the Court that despite the losses from the movie, he was being pursued over the ₹ 5 crore rupees liability.

title: Virat Kohli’s spokesperson refutes claim that cricketer was paid Rs. 5 crores to visit Premanand Ji Maharaj
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:
Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma have regularly visited Premanand Ji Maharaj's aashram in Vrindavan.

Adding to this, Responding to the allegation, Kohli’s spokesperson issued a statement categorically denying the claims and shared that the cricketer’s visits to Premanand Ji Maharaj are driven by his personal faith and reverence.

title: Raza Murad defends Sanjay Leela Bhansali losing his temper on set, says he has seen him shouting at Ranveer Singh, Priyanka Chopra, Deepika Padukone
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

There have been several reports about filmmaker Sanjay Leela Bhansali losing his temper on set, with some actors also admitting to witnessing his anger. Veteran star Raza Murad , who has worked with some of the biggest directors in the industry, compared Bhansali with Raj Kapoor, calling both filmmakers "perfectionists", and opened up about Bhansali's temperament on set.

Adding to this, Raza Murad talks about Sanjay Leela Bhansali losing his temper on sets. Raza Murad on Sanjay Leela Bhansali losing his temper on big stars In a chat with Vickey Lalwani, Raza addressed reports that Bhansali is moody and gets angry with technicians. He shared the filmmaker tends to lose his temper when he is consistently unable to make others understand what he is trying to say. He added, "It's not like he is angry right from the start. And, of course, every person has their own temperament, and that anger isn't personal; it's related to work because it isn't happening properly. So, it's fine if he's getting angry. And, it's not like he only loses his temper at his assistants. I have seen him shouting at bigger stars as well."
Meanwhile, Raza admitted that he had seen Bhansali lose his temper with stars such as Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone and Priyanka Chopra, adding that the filmmaker wants things done his way.

Notably, He further compared Bhansali with Raj Kapoor and shared, "They want what they want. Time, shift, money, set, dates were of least importance to them. It's okay if it takes eight days instead of four days. And when they are on set, they mean business. 'Hum kaam karne ke liye aaye hain (We have come here to work). And this has happened twice with me."

As per the latest buzz, The veteran star's association with Raj Kapoor includes Prem Rog (1982), Ram Teri Ganga Maili (1985) and Henna (1991), while he later collaborated with Bhansali on Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013), Bajirao Mastani (2015), Padmaavat (2018) and Gangubai Kathiawadi (2022). All of these films were successful at the ticket-window. Raza has a career spanning more than five decades and has built a reputation for playing supporting and villainous characters in several successful films.

In further updates, Bhansali is currently busy with the post-production of his soon-to-release movie, Love & War. The movie reunites him with Ranbir Kapoor after Saawariya and with Alia Bhatt after Gangubai Kathiawadi. It also stars Vicky Kaushal in a lead role.

On top of that, Written by Sanjay Leela Bhansali and Ila Bedi Dutta, the movie also features Supriya Pathak in a key role. Earlier reports suggested that Ranbir and Vicky play Indian Air Force officers whose lives become intertwined with Alia's character, setting up a love triangle against the backdrop of a larger conflict.
The movie was originally slated to rollout this year but has now been postponed to January 21, 2027.

title: ‘Students, not anti-nationals’: Bombay HC backs Pune protesters’ right to protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Protesters demanding greater transparency in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) exams have the right to agitate if they believe there are lapses in the recruitment process, and the government should restore their trust, the Bombay high court shared on Wednesday.

Adding to this, Thousands of job aspirants have been protesting at three sites in Pune. (PTI) The court shared the protesters’ grievances are serious even as it asked the students to return to classes. It directed the government to file an affidavit within three weeks providing a department- and reservation-wise break-up of nearly 70,000 vacancies. “They are students, not anti-nationals,” shared a bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna.

Meanwhile, The bench was hearing Pune resident Amit Supekar’s petition seeking directions to authorities to provide designated space to the protesters. Supekar sought action against simultaneous “illegal” public agitations.

Notably, Thousands of job aspirants have been protesting at three sites in Pune despite denial of police permission. The protests are the latest in a series of such agitations. In July, student protests over examination irregularities forced the then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. Job aspirants and student unions, who were agitating against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams for nearly a month, revealed a suspension of their sit-in after the Jharkhand government conceded to almost all their key demands.

As per the latest buzz, The bench noted that Pune is an educational hub. It added that most students there are genuinely interested in studies. “They are not interested in coming on the roads to agitate. ...if they are agitating, it means the grievances are serious. These students work hard for competitive examinations, and if they find any hanky-panky in the examination procedure, they have every right to protest.”

In further updates, Advocate general Milind Sathe, who appeared for the state, told the court that the demands include resignation of the MPSC chairman, reduction of examination fees to ₹ 100, and conducting all examinations offline. He shared the state has accepted one of their demands. He added that a representation seeking action against the chairman has been sent to the governor.

On top of that, The court stressed the importance of fair and impartial examinations. It added that the students are genuinely interested in making a career. “See the plight of the parents who have sent their children to study in Pune. These children are innocent. All parents in the country are in crisis,” it shared. “No message should go across the country that it [Pune] is not a fit place for students, or the parents will also have their apprehension.” The bench assured it would look into how the state is dealing with the issue.

The court shared it endeavors to ensure fair examinations and that the recruitment moves at a fast pace. It urged the students to withdraw the road-blocking, warning that prolonged agitation can hamper their career trajectory.

title: ‘Hope you have learnt a lesson’: SC gives stern warning to Rajpal Yadav, directs actor to deposit ₹2 crore by October 13
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The Supreme Court on Wednesday extended time till Tuesday for star Rajpal Yadav to comply with its direction to deposit ₹ 2 crore rupees towards part payment in a cheque bounce case after he furnished a demand draft of ₹ 1.15 crore rupees and sought an extension to pay the remaining sum.

Adding to this, Rajpal Yadav appears before the Supreme Court in an alleged multi-crore rupees cheque-bounce case, in New Delhi, Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. (PTI Photo)(PTI10_07_2026_000097B) (PTI) What the SC told Rajpal Yadav A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant told the star, who was present in court, to deposit the remaining ₹ 85 lakh by Tuesday (October 13). Following this, the court will take up his petition challenging the conviction and three-month sentence imposed by the Delhi High Court.

Meanwhile, Warning of strict action, the bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, shared, “You comply with our order to deposit ₹ 85 lakh and for the remaining amount, we will lay down a schedule. Ideally, your client should be in jail. Your conduct still does not satisfy us but since you have brought ₹ 1.15 crore rupees, we are willing to give you breathing time.”

Notably, The star claimed that the remaining money could not be arranged because the sale of a property he seeks to sell could not be completed within the stipulated time due to the period of ‘Shraddh,’ which is not considered good for such transactions. He was accompanied in court by the purchaser of his land parcel who agreed to transfer ₹ 85 lakh by way of a demand draft.
As per the latest buzz, The court warned the star, “In your appeal, it is our discretion to issue notice and to enhance your punishment to two years imprisonment.”

In further updates, Advocate Vikrant Yadav appearing for the star told the court that destiny is taking a turn for the better for the star as he is now getting films to act in and direct. The court interacted with Rajpal Yadav and shared, “What are you doing these days? Are you getting any serials or are you without work?”

On top of that, The star, responding in Hindi, shared that in 13 years he has acted in over 250 films but after making this movie, he has been incurring losses worth over ₹ 22 crore rupees. What was much worse, he shared, was the loss of reputation due to the ongoing case as he had to remain in jail for over six months.

Rajpal had taken a loan of over ₹ 5 crore rupees for the production of a movie in 2010 from M/s Murli Projects Limited, with a commitment to repay ₹ 8 crore rupees on which he defaulted. The firm filed a criminal case against Yadav ending in his conviction and sentence of three months in May 2024.

title: Salman Khan vs Kala Hiran: Delhi High Court seeks reply from actor on Amit Jani’s plea seeking stay on proceedings
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani hears filmmaker Amit Jani’s contention that Salman’s latest suit overlaps with an earlier matter pending before the High Court.

Adding to this, During the hearing, Jani’s legal team contended that Khan has effectively initiated parallel litigation concerning the same subject matter. On that basis, counsel argued that proceedings in the subsequent suit should remain stayed until the earlier matter is finally decided. Representing Salman Khan, Senior Advocate Ravi Prakash undertook to place the star’s formal counter-affidavit on record in response to the application.

Meanwhile, The court also sought clarity on the precise basis of the relief being pursued by Khan. Explaining the background, Prakash submitted that the star had initially approached the court seeking protection of his personality and publicity rights. The proceedings resulted in interim protection being granted to Khan in December 2025.

Notably, According to Khan’s counsel, following the interim order, the filmmakers rolled out promotional material and gave interviews to the media that allegedly drew direct parallels between the movie and aspects of the star’s life, including the widely known 1998 blackbuck poaching case in Rajasthan. Khan’s legal team argued that the alleged depiction was sufficiently identifiable with the star’s persona and could cause significant reputational harm.

As per the latest buzz, The star subsequently sought the court’s intervention to prevent the circulation of promotional and publicity material connected to the movie and to restrain its proposed rollout. The dispute escalated further in July 2026, when the Delhi High Court directed the removal of the movie’s initial digital teaser and certain promotional posts from social media. The court also directed the filmmakers not to use Salman Khan’s name, likeness or identifiable characteristics without his consent.

In further updates, The proceedings later turned towards the question of the movie’s proposed distribution and rollout. During those hearings, Jani’s side submitted that Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy was neither complete nor submitted to the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC) for theatrical certification at that stage. The filmmaker’s side also maintained that an official trailer for the movie had not yet been rolled out or circulated.

On top of that, The possibility of a direct-to-digital rollout also came into consideration during the proceedings. While the movie’s theatrical status and certification position were raised before the court, the bench also considered Khan’s apprehensions regarding the possibility of the movie or related promotional material being disseminated directly through digital platforms, including an OTT rollout.

Amit Jani’s side has continued to oppose the reliefs sought by Salman Khan, maintaining its position against the star’s requests for injunctions. The latest hearing, therefore, focused on the procedural objection raised by the filmmaker regarding the overlap between the present proceedings and the earlier matter pending before the High Court.

title: Disha Patani on 10 years in Bollywood: ‘I don’t want to be defined by one role or image’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ten years after stepping into Bollywood with M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story, Disha Patani looks back at a decade that she describes simply as “a period of discovery”. From learning the basics of being on a movie set to becoming more confident about her craft, the star says the biggest change has been within herself.

Adding to this, Disha Patani “When I did M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story, everything was new to me. I was learning how a set works, how to face the camera, how to understand a character and how to take direction,” she recalls. While she was “very instinctive” at the time, Patani says she now has a better understanding of her craft and is “more comfortable trusting” herself.

Meanwhile, Yet, she does not want that confidence to turn into complacency. “I never want to reach a point where I feel like I know everything or that I can do something without putting in the work,” she says. For her, the uncertainty that comes with every new character is what keeps acting exciting. “I think the bigger fear would be losing that curiosity.”

Notably, That curiosity is also pushing Patani towards unexplored territory. She wants to take on characters with greater contradictions and roles where “the physicality or the glamour isn’t the focus and the character itself carries the movie”. Psychological dramas, character-driven thrillers and action projects with challenging characters are on her wish list.

As per the latest buzz, As she begins her next decade, Patani says she wants to take more risks and work across different filmmakers, languages and genres. “I don’t want to be defined by one particular kind of role or image,” she says.

title: Kriti Sanon recalls GIVA ad controversy on the Kareena Kapoor Khan show: “My choli had become like a six-person panel discussion on prime-time news”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The National Award-winning star revisited the backlash over her festive campaign and the scrutiny around women’s clothing on What Women Want Season 6.

Adding to this, The conversation touched upon moral policing and the disproportionate attention often directed towards women in the public eye. Recalling the aftermath of the GIVA campaign, Sanon shared, “I couldn’t believe… when my choli had become like a six-person panel discussion on prime-time news.” Kareena immediately acknowledged her sentiment, responding, “I know.”

Meanwhile, The row dates back to GIVA’s Raksha Bandhan campaign featuring Sanon. The star was seen in a contemporary Indo-western ensemble comprising a white bralette-style choli, a sheer cape and an embroidered skirt. The campaign featured festive celebrations, including Sanon tying a rakhi on a pet dog, but the styling became a talking point on social media.

Notably, Star-politician Kangana Ranaut also reacted to the campaign at the time, criticising Sanon’s outfit and comparing the top to a “bikini”. Following the backlash, GIVA issued a public apology and withdrew the campaign from its television and digital platforms.

As per the latest buzz, Sanon had responded to the criticism at the time, questioning the focus on women’s clothing and arguing that fashion and cultural identity should not be reduced to what a woman wears. She wrote, “Also, when will we stop telling women what to wear?? Ethnic fashion has evolved over the years, but still a woman's respect for her culture is measured with just her clothes!! Culture & Traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline!”

In further updates, The star’ latest comments on What Women Want bring the episode back into focus, particularly the extent to which a fashion choice can become a larger public debate when a star is at the centre of it. Her recollection also underlines the scrutiny that female actors can face over their appearance, even when the conversation begins with a commercial campaign.

title: Drishyam 3 box office collection worldwide day 5: Ajay Devgn’s thriller races towards ₹350 crore, eyes Tanhaji and Singham Again’s lifetime haul
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings worldwide day 5: Drishyam The Conclusion is turning into another major ticket-window success for Ajay Devgn , with the thriller now closing in on the lifetime worldwide collection of Drishyam 2. The latest figures prove that the movie viewers are enjoying the movie, with the third installment continuing to draw audiences across India and overseas markets.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings worldwide day 5: Ajay Devgn’s movie clocks ₹341 crore rupees worldwide on first Tuesday. Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings According to trade tracker Sacnilk, the movie has collected ₹ 341.90 crore rupees worldwide in just five days. Its international run has also been strong, with overseas markets contributing ₹ 81.50 crore rupees, with ₹ 9.50 crore rupees coming in on first Tuesday. Meanwhile, In India, Drishyam 3 has recorded ₹ 216.50 crore rupees in net collections by day 5. The movie has been screened across 82,299 shows, giving it a substantial theatrical presence and allowing the franchise to maintain its momentum across multiple markets.

Notably, View this post on Instagram How Drishyam 3 compares with Ajay Devgn’s previous films Drishyam 2, rolled out in 2022, ended its worldwide theatrical run at around ₹ 342.31 crore rupees. With ₹ 341.30 crore rupees collection already crossed, Drishyam 3 has reached approximately 98.9% of that figure and needs only a small additional push to overtake its predecessor.

As per the latest buzz, Drishyam 3 is co-written, produced, and directed by Abhishek Pathak. Produced by Panorama Studios and Star Studio18. It is a sequel to the 2022 movie Drishyam 2. Ajay Devgn, Jaideep Ahlawat, Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Prakash Raj, Ishita Dutta, and Mrunal Jadhav star in the movie, which features an ending different from the Malayalam counterpart directed by Jeethu Joseph and starring Mohanlal.

In further updates, An excerpt from Hindustan Times review read, “Overall, Drishyam: The Conclusion has enough drama and nostalgia to keep the followers engaged. But for a franchise that built its reputation on making the impossible seem plausible, this one asks us to take a few too many things at face value. It has the ingredients of a satisfying finale, just not the trick to pull it off. The mystery may finally be over, but the magic of the first Drishyam remains hard to recreate.”

title: ‘Literally took personal responsibility’: Abhishek Bachchan reveals King co-star Shah Rukh Khan’s role in his career and the advice he still follows
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Abhishek Bachchan has carried one piece of advice from Shah Rukh Khan with him for years, long before he made his acting debut. It is simple, but perhaps easier shared than done: if you are doing a movie, you have to love the movie you are doing right now. Looking back at that conversation, Abhishek says the same thought continues to shape the way he approaches his work.

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan ‘literally took personal responsibility’ for Abhishek Bachchan, star reveals advice he still follows. The advice Abhishek Bachchan never forgot In an interview with BBC Asian Network ahead of King, Abhishek went back to his younger days, when Sundays meant cricket at filmmaker Aditya Chopra's house. Uday Chopra, Hrithik Roshan and Sikandar Kher were among the people he would play with. Shah Rukh Khan was also around during that period and, as Abhishek remembers it, became an "elder brother" to the group. The video was liked by Hrithik.

Meanwhile, He has remained close to Shah Rukh and says the superstar has been a constant source of support. Speaking about his involvement in his career, he shared Khan has “literally taken personal responsibility several times now, including in King as well.”

Notably, Abhishek then recalled a conversation he had with Khan before he entered the movie industry. He had asked the star a fairly straightforward question: “Which is your favourite movie?” He told Abhishek, “My favourite movie is the movie I am doing right now. Because if that is not my favourite movie, then why am I doing it? So, what I am doing right now has to be my favourite. What has happened in the past is the past. I don't think about it. Right now it is King."
As per the latest buzz, King is directed by Siddharth Anand and produced by Gauri Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment, with Siddharth and Mamta Anand's Marflix Pictures also backing the movie.

In further updates, The action thriller marks Suhana Khan's theatrical debut. She plays a young protege who is trained by Shah Rukh Khan's veteran assassin. title: Amitabh Bachchan recalls being told ‘no heroine would work with you’ early in his career: ‘I am too tall and my face is too small'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Before Amitabh Bachchan became Bollywood’s iconic Angry Young Man, the star struggled to find a foothold in the industry. His towering height and distinctive appearance, which later became part of his screen persona, were initially seen as drawbacks. Big B has now recalled how producers once told him that his physical appearance could make it difficult for him to find a leading lady willing to work opposite him.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan recalls being told no heroine would work with him. Amitabh Bachchan recalls his early struggle days In a recent episode of Kaun Banega Crorepati 18 , a contestant named Vinamra, whose grandfather was a movie distributor, spoke about Amitabh Bachchan’s signature hairstyle and long sideburns, which became closely associated with his image during the 1970s. The star then recalled his early days in the industry and opened up that there was a specific reason behind the hairstyle.

Meanwhile, The host shared, “Sir, kya hain ki shuruvat mein jab hum filmo mein aaye toh kaam milne keliye toh producer doh cheez pe humme bolte the ki humari height lambi hai toh koi heroine kaam nahi karegi aur dusra ki humara chehra bohut chota hain. Toh kya hain usko bharne keliye humne humare baal badaye aur baal ko kaanpati tak ughaya jisse humara chehra bhar bhara lage (Sir, when we first entered films, producers would tell us two things when we were looking for work: first, that we were too tall and no heroine would want to work with us; and second, that our face was too small. So, to make up for that, we grew our hair and let it grow down to our temples so that our face would look fuller).”

Notably, Amitabh Bachchan began his association with cinema as a narrator in Mrinal Sen’s Bhuvan Shome in 1969 before making his acting debut in Khwaja Ahmad Abbas’ Saat Hindustani. The movie did not perform well commercially, and its recognition did little to immediately change Bachchan’s fortune. He continued to appear in supporting and smaller roles, including alongside Rajesh Khanna in Anand, as well as in films such as Sanjog and Bombay To Goa.

As per the latest buzz, During his early years, several of Big B’s films failed at the ticket-window, and he struggled to establish himself as a leading star. He was even described as a “failed newcomer” during this phase of his career.

In further updates, The turning point came with Zanjeer in 1973. At a time when romantic heroes dominated Hindi cinema, Amitabh’s intense portrayal of Inspector Vijay offered audiences a different kind of protagonist. The success of the movie established him as a major star and eventually collected him the iconic tag of Bollywood’s “Angry Young Man”.

On top of that, Zanjeer was followed by a remarkable run of films, including Deewaar, Sholay, Trishul, Don, Muqaddar Ka Sikandar and Kaala Patthar. These films cemented Bachchan’s position as one of the defining stars of Hindi cinema during the 1970s and early 1980s.

Amitabh Bachchan was widely lauded for his performance as Ashwatthama in Nag Ashwin’s Kalki 2898 AD, which rolled out in 2024. The star’s portrayal was particularly appreciated by both critics and audiences, with his action sequences and screen presence becoming one of the highlights of the movie. Big B will reprise the role in the sequel, which is currently in production. The movie, directed by Nag Ashwin, will also feature Prabhas and Kamal Haasan in key roles.

title: Rahul Gandhi leads INDIA bloc protest, calls CEC Gyanesh Kumar to step down
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Opposition on Tuesday attempted to ratchet up pressure on chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign with an unprecedented protest in central Delhi that lasted nine hours, drawing furious responses from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Adding to this, Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra take part in a protest organised by opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (REUTERS) At least 300 lawmakers from the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) marched from Parliament to the Election Commission of India (ECI), demanding Kumar’s resignation. When police stopped them outside Nirvachan Sadan, more than 250 Opposition members were detained. However, after a brief standoff, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra , along with 20 others, walked into the Akashvani Bhavan campus next door and continued their protest till about 8pm.

Meanwhile, The leaders were finally detained amid high drama around 8pm, when a phalanx of policemen physically dragged away the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and put him inside a bus, but not before Rahul Gandhi attempted to escape through the window of the vehicle.
Notably, The Congress alleged that Gandhi, Venugopal and some others were manhandled and dragged into buses.

As per the latest buzz, They were packed into the vehicles, taken to Kingsway Camp, and subsequently rolled out around 10.15pm. A police aware who did not want to be named shared that Congress workers reached the New Police Lines area and attempted to scale walls of the premises.

In further updates, Gandhi alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi , home minister Amit Shah and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat “hijacked” the country with Kumar’s help by stealing votes.
On top of that, “What has been done to our country is treason. Nobody is going to escape,” he shared.

The BJP hit back. Those who looted the country in power are now talking about ‘theft’...repeated defeats have left Congress frustrated, now it has resorted to threats,” Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan shared.

title: An open gate, a banyan tree, 6 hours of dharna: How Akashvani Bhavan became Cong's battleground against EC
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The historic Akashvani Bhavan campus, home to All India Radio, became the new site for political protests as Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi held a dharna for over six hours as a part of the Opposition’s protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on Tuesday.

Adding to this, Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra at Akashvani Bhavan on Tuesday. According to some leaders, the original plan was to march from the Parliament house to Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission headquarters but as the police stopped the march next to the Akashvani Bhavan, Gandhi, along with other key Congress leaders, switched over to the plan to prolong their demonstrations. Later, they were detained by a large number of Delhi police personnel from the campus.

Meanwhile, When the police started detaining the Opposition leaders, Gandhi and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra slipped through an iron gate—the only one kept open for the Akashvani staff, and sat under a large banyan tree. Congress general secretary KC Venugopal, party MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring and party leaders Manish Chatrath, BV Srinivas and others also joined the protest.

Notably, For the next six hours, till the Delhi police personnel forcibly detained Gandhi and other leaders, the northern Akashvani campus became a stage for the Opposition protests, shifting from the Sansad Marg.

As per the latest buzz, Senior Congress leaders shared that while the Sansad Marg has seen many protests and marches, Gandhi’s decision to shift to Akashvani Bhavan campus, inadvertently turned it into a temporary political platform.
In further updates, To be sure, it is unlikely that the campus can be again used for such political protests. A senior official shared that Gandhi “took advantage of the gate that was left open.”
On top of that, “In future, we have to ensure no such misuse of the Akashvani Bhavan,” he added.
Built in the 1940s, the semi-circular main building enjoys a heritage status. The building houses the news service, drama and FM sections.
