title: 'No party sought meeting till 4 pm': EC on INDIA bloc sit-in against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Tuesday shared no political party had formally sought an appointment with the poll panel before 4 pm, as the INDIA bloc's protest over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls escalated in New Delhi. Track live updates

Adding to this, Opposition MPs led by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the poll panel and the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. (ECI/X, HT) This came hours after Opposition MPs led by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the poll panel and the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The march was stopped by police before the leaders could reach the ECI office, following which several Opposition MPs staged a sit-in.

Meanwhile, In a press note issued later in the day, the ECI shared it was informed by Delhi Police at around 4 pm that a delegation of MPs led by Gandhi wanted to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum.

Notably, “The Election Commission of India had laid down a procedure in 2025 for meetings with political parties. All political parties have been informed about this procedure and follow it. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly authorised representative. The meeting is then held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides,” the statement read.

As per the latest buzz, According to the Commission, the Delhi Police's deputy commissioner subsequently informed it that the proposed meeting involved around 240 MPs and was to take place at the Parliament House Annexe. The ECI shared it considered the request “unusual” and declined it, citing its protocol that such meetings are held at the Commission's premises.

In further updates, “When the Election Commission was considering the proposal for the meeting with the MPs after 4 pm today, the DCP of Delhi Police informed it that the meeting being sought was with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was Parliament House Annexe. The Election Commission considered this request unusual and could not accept it because, as per protocol, such meetings are held only at the premises of the Election Commission of India,” the statement read.

On top of that, The Commission, however, shared it offered to send its most senior serving officer to the Parliament Annexe to receive the memorandum from the MPs. It described the proposal as an unprecedented step, but shared the MPs declined it.

“Any political party can request a meeting with the Election Commission at any time, and the Commission can, depending on the availability of time, decide the date and time of the meeting. This is a normal process,” the statement read.

title: Drishyam 3 box office collection day 5: Ajay Devgn’s crime thriller crosses ₹214 crore despite 18% Tuesday drop, now eyes Drishyam 2’s lifetime record
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 5: Ajay Devgn’s biggest opener now eyes Drishyam 2's lifetime record. Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 5 by 9 PM According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Drishyam 3 has collected ₹ 214.63 crore rupees net in India in its first five days. The movie got off to a strong start on Friday, opening with ₹ 62 crore rupees at the domestic ticket-window. While collections slipped to ₹ 53.50 crore rupees on Saturday, the dip was followed by a healthy Sunday recovery, with the movie bringing in ₹ 61 crore rupees and recording 56% occupancy. The strong weekend gave Drishyam 3 a solid foundation before the usual weekday slowdown kicked in.

Adding to this, Monday saw the unexpected drop, with the movie collecting ₹ 21 crore rupees, around 65.6% lower than its Sunday figure. The decline continued on Tuesday, when Drishyam 3 collected ₹ 17.13 crore rupees at 22% occupancy but approximately 18.4% dip from Monday.

Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram Even with the weekday slowdown, Drishyam 3 has already collected more than double the lifetime collection of the original Drishyam, which ended its theatrical run at ₹ 102.75 crore rupees. More importantly, the third installment is now just around ₹ 30 crore rupees short of Drishyam 2, which collected ₹ 239.67 crore rupees net in India. If it manages to maintain a steady run through the week, Drishyam 3 could soon overtake its predecessor and become the highest-grossing movie in the franchise.

Notably, The movie has given Ajay Devgn a new career-best opening. Drishyam 3 collected ₹ 62 crore rupees net on its first day, beating the ₹ 43.50 crore rupees opening of Singham Again. The Rohit Shetty-directorial ended its theatrical run at ₹ 247.86 crore rupees, while Raid 2 collected ₹ 173.44 crore rupees. Drishyam 3 has already moved into that territory in just five days, with its final total still to come.

title: Javed Akhtar says 99% of people die in the religion they were born into; questions beliefs inherited from parents
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Javed Akhtar has spent much of his career questioning things people often take for granted. That instinct extends well beyond cinema and songwriting. In a conversation with Express Hindi with Saurabh Dwivedi, the veteran writer and lyricist spoke at length about religion, faith and atheism, and why he remains skeptical of beliefs that are accepted simply because they have been inherited.

Adding to this, Javed Akhtar acknowledged that religion can provide solace during difficult periods in life. However, he questioned whether the emotional comfort people draw from faith serves as actual proof that their religious beliefs are true. The writer considered this reliance to be an artificial foundation. (PTI) What Javed Akhtar shared about faith Javed Akhtar acknowledged that religion can provide solace during difficult periods in life. However, he questioned whether the emotional comfort people draw from faith serves as actual proof that their religious beliefs are true. The writer considered this reliance to be an artificial foundation. He explained that individuals often cling to the idea of a higher power merely for the consolation it brings, giving them the comforting but false reassurance that someone is always there to watch over them.

Meanwhile, He illustrated the idea with an example involving Elon Musk . If someone genuinely convinced themselves that Musk was their brother and that a huge amount of money was on its way, the belief could still make them feel secure even if there was no reason to expect it. “Believe it from your heart that next month he is going to send me two, four, six billion dollars, and then keep saying next month, next month, and remain happy. How reassuring would it be if you thought that Elon Musk is my brother? You would be happy, right?” he added.

Notably, He questioned whether faith was ever truly a conscious choice, pointing out that most people simply followed the religion they had grown up with. By noting that 99 percent of people died in the religion they were born into, he questioned how often beliefs were independently formed rather than inherited from childhood. He also stressed the need to separate people from the ideas they put forward. Since people could change their opinions over time, he argued that ideas should be examined on their own merit and questioned rather than accepted simply because they came from someone people trusted.

As per the latest buzz, “Our story is different. We don't trust a person. We trust an idea. That person may say something else tomorrow, it doesn't make any difference to us. We trust the idea, logic and reason," he went onto say, adding "What happens with a person who is religious, or a person of faith, is that he trusts a person. Whatever his parents told him, he probably trusts his parents. Or he may find a saint. There are 10 major religions in the world. And to say that they are all the same is nonsense. They are all different.”

In further updates, Javed Akhtar is one of the most influential voices in Indian cinema and literature, with a career that has stretched across more than five decades. As a poet, lyricist and screenwriter, he has played a part in shaping some of Hindi cinema’s most memorable stories, characters and songs.

title: ‘Is something already being planned’: CJP’s Dipke flags Maharashtra Police notices ahead of protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday alleged that the Maharashtra Police was attempting to stop his party workers from attending its planned protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi next week, claiming that workers were issued notices and questioned about funds for their travel.

Adding to this, Mumbai: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke during a protest by CJP against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, demanding his resignation, at Shivaji Park, in Mumbai (PTI) The alleged clampdown on the workers came after the CJP revealed a fresh agitation at Jantar Mantar from October 10 to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and what the Opposition parties have termed “vote chori”.

Meanwhile, “I have shared multiple times that the Maharashtra Police is the best police force in the country and that the Delhi Police should learn from them. But it is heartbreaking that the Chandrapur police served notices to CJP workers, asking them not to participate in the protest at Jantar Mantar . They also asked CJP workers about the source of funds for travelling to Jantar Mantar,” Dipke shared at Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar on Tuesday.
Notably, Dipke shared copies of two such notices issued by the Chandrapur police to CJP workers from the district.

As per the latest buzz, In one of the notices issued to Mayur Malkhede, the Ballarpur police shared, “You should participate in the New Delhi protest without permission. Do not take along violent protestors for the protest, and do not make violent posts on social media platforms or make provocative speeches… Upon violating the formal notice you will have to face preventive or criminal action.”

In further updates, Dipke also questioned the police’s reference to the possibility of violence in the notices. “In the notice, the police shared that the agitation is going to be violent. How do the police know in advance that the agitation would be violent? Have they planned anything in advance?” he asked.
On top of that, Calling the police action a form of “dictatorship”, Dipke accused chief minister Devendra Fadnavis of potentially “misusing” the police for political ambitions.
“Why is the Maharashtra Police behaving like the Delhi Police? What do they have to do if a person is going to Delhi from Chandrapur?” he asked.

title: Shriya Saran says Drishyam team sent her home before Ajay Devgn when she was a new mother: ‘Very supportive’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shriya Saran of late lauded the makers of Drishyam for being sensitive to her needs as a new mother. The star, in a recent interaction, shared that the Drishyam 3 team would send her home, sometimes even before the movie’s lead star, Ajay Devgn , because she has a young daughter.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 has collected more than ₹300 crore rupees in worldwide collection. 'They were very supportive' In conversation with India Today, she shared, “My daughter was eight months old when I did Drishyam 2. And in Part 3, of course, she’s older. But they were very supportive. After the shoot, they used to send me off earlier, sometimes even before Ajay sir, because they were like, ‘She is a new mother.’ They’re very kind, sweet, and I’m grateful to them.”

Meanwhile, Shriya also shared that her perspective on movie selection changed after becoming a mother, as she is mindful that her daughter will also see her on screen. She shared, “See, I have to be mindful, of course. I want to spend a lot more time with my daughter, and I want to do films that I know one day my daughter will be proud of. I want her to get up and say, ‘You know, Mama, that was a great movie. And I’m glad that you did this movie.’”

Notably, Shriya’s comments come at a time when there is a growing debate about making movie-set environments more compatible for new mothers. Another mother, Deepika Padukone, exited Sandeep Reddy Vanga’s movie Spirit over a fixed working-hour demand, among other conditions, sparking this debate.

As per the latest buzz, Parineeti Chopra, who welcomed her son last year, also spoke about being a working mother. She spoke at her web show, Shaque’s trailer launch, “I would hate to stop working just because I became a mom. It’s a two-way relationship, I’ve to be offered work and I would be sad to lose work because I’ve done such a beautiful thing in producing a baby. The audience is not cancelling mothers, and hence writers, directors and actors are able to make content."

In further updates, She also took examples of other working mothers like Alia Bhatt, Deepika Padukone and her cousin Priyanka Chopra Jonas and shared, “I’m so glad that our generation, including Alia (Bhatt), me, Deepika (Padukone), my own sister (Priyanka Chopra), who is working in the West, and all of us are able to be mothers and we are doing the same quality of work. In fact, I think we are doing better work now,” she added.
On top of that, Meanwhile, Drishyam 3 is enjoying good success at the ticket-window. The movie has collected over ₹ 300 crore rupees in worldwide collections.

title: Tu Hai Meri Kiran Trailer: Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal explore one-sided love, obsession and mystery
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Directed by Karan Rawal, the thriller is scheduled to rollout in cinemas on October 23, 2026.

Adding to this, The trailer introduces Sonakshi and Zaheer in a narrative where a connection appears to gradually take a more complicated turn. While the preview establishes the emotional equation between the two characters, it keeps several details about the larger story under wraps. Elements of mystery and suspense are woven into the narrative, leaving questions around what is real and what may be perceived differently by the characters.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the movie and her character, Sonakshi Sinha shared, “This is a very different space for me, and that’s what made it so exciting. What intrigued me most was the unsettling world the movie creates, where an emotion can slowly become something far more intense and consuming. My character goes through a very unusual journey, and there are so many layers to her that I really enjoyed exploring. The movie keeps you on the edge and makes you question the reality unfolding on screen. I’m looking forward to audiences stepping into this world and experiencing Tu Hai Meri Kiran in theatres.”

Notably, Zaheer Iqbal described the project as a movie that explores the changing nature of one-sided love. He shared, “It is a very special movie for me. What drew me to the story was the way it explores one sided love and how an emotion that begins with intensity can take an unexpected turn. There is a strong sense of mystery and suspense throughout the movie, which keeps you wondering what lies beneath the surface. I really enjoyed exploring the complexities of my character and discovering the different layers to him. Working with Sonakshi made the experience even more special. I’m looking forward to audiences discovering the world of Tu Hai Meri Kiran and experiencing its mystery, suspense and emotions on the big screen.”

As per the latest buzz, Producer Vishal Rana shared, “What drew us to the movie was its exploration of one sided love, obsession and the dangerous consequences that can follow. I was particularly excited by the mystery and the way Karan has built suspense around these characters and their relationship. The movie keeps you questioning what is real, what is imagined and where the story is headed. Sonakshi and Zaheer have brought tremendous intensity to their characters, making the world of the movie even more unpredictable. We’re excited to finally share the trailer and give audiences a glimpse into the intriguing and suspenseful world of Tu Hai Meri Kiran .”

In further updates, Writer-director Karan Rawal added, “With Tu Hai Meri Kiran , I wanted to explore how one sided love can gradually take an unexpected turn, and how far someone can go when they become consumed by their feelings. What drew me to the story was the opportunity to create a thriller where the audience is constantly questioning what is real and what lies beneath the surface. Building that sense of mystery and suspense while keeping the characters at the centre of the story was an exciting creative process. Sonakshi and Zaheer brought a great deal of depth and nuance to their characters, and that was instrumental in shaping the world of the movie. I’m excited for audiences to finally step into this world and discover the story for themselves.”

On top of that, Tu Hai Meri Kiran is scheduled to rollout theatrically on October 23, 2026. The trailer leaves the central mystery and the eventual turn in Sonakshi and Zaheer’s characters’ relationship open, with audiences set to discover the complete story in cinemas.

title: Amitabh Bachchan, Badshah forced to evacuate after Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set fire smoke reached Kaun Banega Crorepati set; Hustle 5 finale disrupted
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

A fire broke out at Movie City in Goregaon East, Mumbai, on Monday afternoon, October 5, disrupting shoots on multiple television sets and forcing actors and crew members to evacuate. The fire started around 4 pm on the outer shade of a temporary setup being used for Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 , behind Prime Focus Studio. The smoke soon reached the adjoining sets of Hustle Season 5 and Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC).

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan, Badshah evacuated as Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set catches fire; Hustle 5 finale disrupted, KBC 18 shoot halted. Nobody was injured. No shooting was scheduled on the Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set when the fire broke out, which meant there were no artists or crew members working there at the time. However, the incident brought nearby shoots to a halt and once again raised questions about safety arrangements at Movie City.

Meanwhile, According to Times of India report, Ashok Dubey, President of the All India Movie Employees Confederation (AIFEC) and General Secretary of the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE), says the situation could have been much more serious had the Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 team been shooting.

Notably, “The shade on the Pati Patni Aur Panga set caught fire, and the smoke spread to the adjacent sets of Hustle 5 and Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC), forcing the crews to evacuate. Amit ji ( Amitabh Bachchan ) also had to step out of the KBC set because of the smoke, bringing the shoots to a halt for nearly an hour and a half. Fortunately, there was no shoot on the Pati Patni Aur Panga set; otherwise, it could have resulted in a major accident,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, For Ashok, Monday's incident is another warning sign rather than a one-off accident. He shared fires have been reported at shooting locations with increasing frequency and that concerns around basic safety checks have not received enough attention.

In further updates, He pointed out that fires on sets have become a routine occurrence rather than an exception. He recalled an incident roughly ten days earlier at Royal Palms, where a fire triggered by a short circuit broke out just as a shoot was set to commence. He stressed that he has consistently advocated for structural audits, fire compliance and safety inspections on sets, yet his appeals have gone unheeded, with no one appearing to prioritise the safety of those working on them. He concluded that no sum of money can ever make up for a life lost.

On top of that, He added that the federation had already taken up the issue with officials, including the labour department, BMC and fire authorities. According to him, the discussions were meant to create a system where sets could be inspected and working conditions checked before productions began.

“We had meetings involving the labour officer, BMC officials and the federation's health and safety team, which was supposed to inspect sets and assess how work was being carried out. I have been writing to the fire department and the Chief Minister for many years. We can't wait for a major tragedy to happen before swinging into action. We wrote to the Chief Fire Officer and the BMC two days ago, and we will be writing again, asking them to look into this concern. We also met Ashish Shelar ji, Cabinet Minister for Information Technology and Cultural Affairs, Government of Maharashtra, a while ago regarding how every set could be inspected and safety protocols followed, which turned out to be quite positive. We are hoping that action will soon be initiated and that the necessary steps will be taken,” he added.

The notice identifies Sugar & Spice Production, represented by Chirag Dhariwal and Param Deep Sandhu, as the production entity associated with the movie.

Adding to this, According to Jain’s notice, his claim arises from a finance agreement and finance term sheet dated June 3, 2019, and November 3, 2020. He has claimed “sole and exclusive negative rights” over the movie, including rights relating to copyright, intellectual property, remake, sequel, prequel, theatrical exhibition, digital platforms, television, satellite, streaming, video-on-demand, dubbing, merchandising, gaming and several other forms of exploitation across territories worldwide.

Meanwhile, Significantly, the notice further claims that these rights were “irrevocably sold, assigned and transferred” to Jain under the aforementioned agreements. It also states that, according to him, none of the copyrights, IPR or other rights in the movie would vest with Sugar & Spice Production, and cautions any person or entity entering into a transfer of the movie’s IP rights that they would be doing so “at their own risk and costs”.
Notably, The notice lists the movie as “ Koka Kola now named as ‘ Chudail ’”, with Sunny Leone and Rahul Dev mentioned as the lead actors.

As per the latest buzz, Jain has also invited any person, copyright society or corporate body having a claim or objection to the grant of rights to communicate the same to him in writing, along with documentary evidence, within 10 days of the public notice.
In further updates, It remains to be seen whether the notice leads to any counter-claim or clarification from the production house or other stakeholders associated with Chudail .

title: 'Make bodycams mandatory for cops': Plea in Delhi HC after alleged harassment during protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed in the Delhi High Court seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras (BWCs) by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel deployed for crowd control and protests. This comes amid allegations of misconduct by security personnel during recent demonstrations held at the Jantar Mantar .

Adding to this, Delhi Police detains a protestor demanding resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi. (ANI) The plea asks the court to direct authorities to frame rules or a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) requiring personnel on crowd-control duty to wear body cameras, ANI reported. It also seeks clear rules on how the recorded footage should be stored, protected and kept for a specified period, and how it can be used as evidence.

Meanwhile, Cameras have been issued to personnel handling crowd management and security around protest sites, as well as those deployed along roads leading to the Election Commission office, PTI reported. Police shared the devices would record interactions with protesters in real time and provide an objective record of events in case complaints are made against officers or demonstrators.

Notably, The decision follows complaints by three women journalists who alleged sexual harassment and manhandling by police while covering a protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. One of the journalists alleged that ACP Vivek Bhagat sexually assaulted her while she was recording police action during the demonstration.

As per the latest buzz, The journalists approached the police after the alleged incidents and underwent medical examinations. Delhi Police shared the three complaints were transferred to the Crime Branch. The allegations have triggered protests outside Parliament Street police station. Journalists, activists and others demand an FIR and action against the cop named in the complaints.

In further updates, On October 5, police detained a group, including journalists and one of the complainants, that gathered outside the station after they spent the night there. They shared the gathering violated restrictions in force in the New Delhi district.

On top of that, The police have also issued guidelines for journalists covering protests, asking them to carry valid identity cards issued by their organisations or PIB/DIP accreditation cards and keep them visibly displayed. They have been advised to ensure their reporting does not obstruct police operations or the movement of security personnel.

The deployment of bodycams comes amid heightened security following demonstrations linked to the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police and paramilitary forces have been deployed in large numbers, with multilayered barricades installed around sensitive locations.

title: Shweta Tripathi says she turned to Anurag Kashyap, Neeraj Ghaywan for lessons in film production
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai, Star-turned-producer Shweta Tripathi says she sought advice from her filmmaker friends Anurag Kashyap and Neeraj Ghaywan as she ventured into movie production, a decision driven by her desire to find good scripts and support talented new storytellers.

Adding to this, Shweta Tripathi says she turned to Anurag Kashyap, Neeraj Ghaywan for lessons in movie production Tripathi is making her feature production debut with "Mujhe Jaan Na Kaho Meri Jaan", where she stars alongside star Tillotama Shome. The movie is directed by Sanjoy Nag.
Meanwhile, Calling Kashyap and Ghaywan her "go-to people", Tripathi shared the duo guided her about the intricacies of movie production.

Notably, "It's important to be surrounded by people who are open, who are ready to share things. Like, I had called up Neeraj, and I had asked him a few things, besides I've discussed it with Kashyap multiple times. So, I've that relationship with him where I keep asking for guidance because it is important," the star told PTI in an interview.

As per the latest buzz, "They told me a lot of small things, whether it's about budget, how to approach a project, how different HODs work, what kind of people you should work with, and how to approach different subjects or stories," she added.

In further updates, The star worked with Ghaywan for his debut feature 2015's "Masaan", which was produced by Kashyap through his erstwhile banner Phantom Films. Kashyap also backed her acclaimed independent films "Zoo", and "Cargo".

On top of that, For Tripathi, known for starring in movies such as "Masaan", "Haraamkhor", "Gone Kesh" and "Cargo", and web-series like "Mirzapur", "Yeh Kaali Kaali Ankhein" and "Kaalkoot", the decision to become a producer did not happen overnight.

"I knew that I wanted to be a bankable star and I wanted to be an star on whom people invest money on. Similarly, when I knew that I wanted to be a producer, I want to be there for people like Shlok Sharma or Aarti Kadav who should be able to get more money to make a movie.

title: Eggoz onboards Boman Irani as brand ambassador
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The campaign, conceptualised by ANC, puts Boman right at the centre of the fun and takes a fresh, playful route to the simple joy of eating an Eggoz egg. It all unfolds in a sleepy office where nothing ever moves fast, until Boman, the classic office boss, strolls in fresh from lunch and sets off a chain reaction of impossibly quick, joyful chaos. Files fly, stamps thump, and stunned faces melt into delight, all thanks to what the campaign calls the "Eggoz effect." The secret, revealed over a spread of golden bhurji, fluffy omelettes and sunny side ups with rich orange yolks, is simple: Eggoz doesn't just fill you up, it fires you up. A cheerful little reminder that food isn't only fuel, it's colour, flavour and everyday joy on a plate.

Adding to this, Speaking on the association, Abhishek Negi, Co-founder and CEO, Eggoz, shared, "Boman Irani brings a warmth and humour that instantly connects with people, which is exactly what Eggoz stands for. We've always believed that a good egg can change the mood of an entire meal, and this campaign captures that spirit with a lot of heart and a lot of fun. Having Boman embody the 'Eggoz effect' felt like the most natural way to tell our story."

Meanwhile, Commenting on the partnership, Boman Irani shared, "What drew me to Eggoz is how they've taken something as everyday as an egg and made it feel special. The movie was a joy to shoot because it doesn't take itself too seriously, and yet it says something true, that the little things on your plate can genuinely brighten your day. I had a wonderful time being part of it."

Notably, Adding to this, Shivan Nair, Head of Marketing, Eggoz, shared, "For us, this campaign was about making the everyday egg impossible to ignore. Boman brings a warmth and humour that cuts through instantly, and that's exactly the kind of connection we wanted with our consumers. The 'Eggoz effect' is really our brand promise in disguise, that good food should lift your whole day, and we can't wait for audiences to see it come alive."

As per the latest buzz, Adding to this, Samarjeet Shimpi, CEO, ANC shared, "The brand needed to own an emotion in the egg space. We defined Eggoz as being delightful and full of energy. Hence, the expression, Sunny Side Up. Boman exemplifies it the best."

In further updates, The campaign reflects Eggoz's larger belief that quality food should be an integral, enjoyable part of everyday life. With freshly dispatched eggs from hens on a special herbal diet, rigorous quality standards and a distinctive rich orange yolk, Eggoz continues to build a brand that pairs nutrition with genuine everyday joy, turning even the most mundane moments sunny side up.

title: Sonu Nigam expands Mumbai property portfolio, buys commercial units in Andheri West for Rs. 16 crores
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:
The singer has acquired three office units at Aston in Sundervan Complex, taking his total commercial investment in the property to Rs. 16 crores approximately.

Adding to this, The primary transaction involves two adjoining office spaces situated on the first floor of the building. The properties have a combined carpet area of 3,885.77 sq. ft and were acquired from Singular Health Private Limited for a total consideration of Rs. 16 crores. The transaction translates to an approximate rate of Rs. 41,175.88 per sq. ft. Stamp duty of Rs. 96 lakhs were paid as part of the registration.
Meanwhile, The two office units also come with dedicated access to four car parking spaces in the basement stack-parking system of the building.

Notably, In a separate transaction registered during the same cycle, Nigam acquired another commercial unit in the same Aston building from the same seller. The ground-floor office measures 258.33 sq. ft and was purchased for Rs. 1 crore rupees. The transaction attracted a stamp duty of Rs. 6 lakhs.

As per the latest buzz, With the latest acquisition, Sonu Nigam’s total holding in the Aston property now covers 4,144.10 sq. ft of carpet area. His combined investment across the three units stands at Rs. 17 crores, translating to an average acquisition rate of approximately Rs. 41,021 per sq. ft.

In further updates, The latest purchase adds to the singer’s real estate activity across Mumbai and Maharashtra over the past two years. In late 2025, Nigam leased a 4,257 sq. ft commercial office at Trade Centre BKC in Santacruz East to Pattni Hospitality, operators of the café-bar chain Downtown 29. The five-year lease is expected to generate more than Rs. 12.61 crores in cumulative rental income over its tenure.

On top of that, Nigam has also undertaken transactions involving land holdings in Karjat. In April 2026, he sold multiple land parcels in Raigad district measuring more than 1.9 hectares for Rs. 1.95 crores. A separate 1.067-hectare land parcel was sold in May 2026 for Rs. 95 lakhs.

Meanwhile, his father Agam Kumar Nigam acquired a 1,197 sq. m. land parcel in Madh Island in February 2026. The property includes a ground-plus-one residential and commercial structure and was purchased for Rs. 10 crores.

title: Protesting tribal students detained at Congress office, taken out of Mumbai
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Tribal students, who marched from Nashik demanding basic facilities in their schools and hostels, were detained at the Congress’s Maharashtra headquarters and taken out of Mumbai on Tuesday, a day after they accused the police of trying to crush their protest.

Adding to this, The Congress provided shelter to the students after police denied them permission to hold their protest at Azad Maidan. The action came as the students insisted on meeting Governor Jishnu Dev Verma after being denied permission to hold a protest at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan. The students vowed to return to Mumbai on October 25 before they were taken out of the city.

Meanwhile, Police guarding Tilak Bhavan, the state Congress headquarters where the students had been staying since Monday, stopped them from exiting as they prepared to leave. Soon the students were put on private buses and driven away.
Notably, “The students are believed to have been taken back to Nashik,” shared a Congress functionary. “We are not sure whether they will be dropped in Nashik or somewhere close to the city.”

As per the latest buzz, The students began their march on September 28 and reached Mumbai late Sunday night. They have been demanding an independent probe into the deaths of students at tribal schools. The students have sought ₹ 1 crore rupees compensation each for the families of three girls who died of snakebite at a school in Gadchiroli.

In further updates, The students demanded an inquiry into alleged irregularities in the distribution of grants and action against officials responsible. They sought the resignation of state tribal development minister Ashok Uike, alleging that he failed to fulfil his responsibilities.

title: Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha producer Prakash Mahobiya alleges ‘negative marketing’; hints at big-budget Ramayana saying, “We never got a chance to reach our audience”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Prakash Mahobiya claims the movie faced online smear campaigns and says the makers are considering a theatrical re-rollout.

Adding to this, Speaking about the movie’s reception, Mahobiya shared, “It was negative marketing throughout. We never got a chance to reach our audience. The ones who watched our movie really enjoyed it. But if they never got to see it, how will they even have an opinion?”

Meanwhile, The producer further claimed that he had been told about efforts involving digital creators to discourage audiences from watching the movie. He shared, “From what we have been told, there are other movies on the same subject coming in, the big-budget movie. As far as we know, a lot of negative marketing opportunities have been given to YouTubers, influencers and other people. They are spreading wrong information and asking people not to watch our movie,” before adding, “I don’t know for sure, but that’s what we are being told.”

Notably, His comments come amid considerable attention around Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana , the soon-to-release two-part adaptation produced by Namit Malhotra. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Raavan and is among the most closely watched soon-to-release Indian movie projects. Mahobiya’s remarks, however, do not establish any connection between Ramayana and the alleged online campaigns against his movie.

As per the latest buzz, Mahobiya also admitted that marketing a movie was a learning experience for him as a first-time producer. He shared, “I have made a movie for the first time, and I am new to this industry. I have no idea how to market a movie after making it. We are not afraid of the loss, but we are disappointed that not many people managed to watch it. And hence, we want to rollout the movie again.”

In further updates, Maintaining that Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha offers a distinct interpretation, he added, “There is a lot of difference between your movie and the other movie that will arrive soon. But we are confident that, given a chance, people would have liked our movie too.”

On top of that, Directed by Abhishek Singh, Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha rolled out in cinemas on September 25, 2026. The movie stars Dev Sharma as Lord Ram, Anjali Arora as Goddess Sita, Sheel Verma as Laxman and Rajniesh Duggall in a pivotal role.
Following its theatrical run, the makers are now exploring the possibility of re-releasing the movie in cinemas to give it another opportunity to reach audiences.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The team of Hanuman Ansh visited the revered Kainchi Dham in Nainital on Monday, a day after the movie's director, Vishal Chaturvedi , had warned devotees of reported overcrowding at the ashram. However, the movie's team appreciated the smooth, well-organised arrangements for devotees, as well as the ongoing development work at the ashram.

Adding to this, Hanuman Ansh team visits Kainchi Dham. Hanuman Ansh team visits Kainchi Dham The movie's lead actors, Shobhinaw Satyaa, Purnima Tiwari, and producer Ragini Sona, lauded the experience as unforgettable and expressed gratitude to Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami for facilitating their visit to Kainchi Dham. They shared the well-organised arrangements enabled them to have a hassle-free darshan of Baba Neem Karoli and seek his blessings.

Meanwhile, In a video message, star Shobhinaw told ANI, “Our entire team got the opportunity to visit Kainchi Dham. We would like to thank CM Pushkar Singh Dhami for inviting us here. We took Baba’s ashirwaad, and it was a heartfelt moment. We also received the opportunity to witness Uttarakhand’s Rangotsav festival 2026.”

Notably, He added, “We got to see so many different colours of Uttarakhand’s culture. I had never seen anything like it before. There were beautiful musical performances, traditional instruments being played, and nagadas (traditional drums) being played. The atmosphere was truly something to witness. It was wonderful to see Uttarakhand’s culture being promoted. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami invited us, honoured us, and even danced with us. It showed how much he loves and respects the culture. He was also among the first to recognise our movie and appreciate it.”

As per the latest buzz, On Sunday, Vishal took to his Instagram handle to share a video and urged devotees to check the situation before heading to Kainchi Dham due to reported overcrowding. He had shared, “Kainchi Dham is overcrowded, and people have shared that this is because of the influence of Hanuman Ansh. If that is the case, and if that is not the case, even then, people should visit there only after knowing the present conditions."

In further updates, He added, “It is my humble request that if there is overcrowding, please consider visiting other places. Don’t become part of a situation where women and children feel suffocated or get stuck in traffic jams."
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dr Vishal Chaturvedi (@filmervishal)

Hanuman Ansh has been written and directed by Vishal . The movie is based on the life and teachings of Neeb Karori Baba, popularly known as Maharaj ji. The movie, which was made on a budget of ₹ 2 crore rupees has crossed ₹ 400 crore rupees at the ticket-window, was rolled out in theatres on August 7, 2026.

title: Students protest RSS leader’s presence at Vande Mataram event in Central University of Kerala
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Kasaragod, Students held protests at the Central University of Kerala on Tuesday against the presence of J Nandakumar, national convener of an RSS-linked organisation, at a Vande Mataram-related event at the institution.

Adding to this, Students protest RSS leader’s presence at Vande Mataram event in Central University of Kerala Besides opposing Nandakumar's presence at the event, activists of various student organisations, including Kerala Students Union and Muslim Students Federation , also contended that many of them were denied entry to the programme despite registering for it.
Meanwhile, Left affiliated student organisations, Students Federation of India and All India Students' Federation , also joined the protest.
Notably, Heavy police presence was seen at the programme venue, preventing the protesting students from entering the hall where the event was being held.

As per the latest buzz, The protesting students, carrying flags of their respective student organisations, shouted slogans against the RSS outside the venue and engaged in push-and-pull with the police in order to gain entry to the programme.

In further updates, Later, a university official claiming to be the Dean of Student Affairs told reporters that he was not aware why registered students were being denied entry and shared he will have to ask the organisers of the programme.

On top of that, The two-day National Seminar, being held on October 6 and 7, on the '150th Anniversary of Vande Mataram' is being organised by the Sahitya Akademi in collaboration with the Akhil Bharatiya Sahitya Parishad and the university as part of the nationwide observance marking 150 years of the national song.
Nandakumar, National Convener of Prajna Pravah, is scheduled to deliver the keynote address at the event and the students told reporters that they are opposed to his presence in the programme.

title: Raju Kher recalls financial crisis after a bad investment, says brother Anupam Kher didn't help him: 'Took him for granted'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Anupam Kher's brother, star-director Raju Kher , of late opened up about facing financial struggles after being cheated in a television project. Raju admitted that he expected his brother, who was already a well-established star by then, to help him during his financial woes. However, he was taken aback when he did not receive the help he had expected.

Adding to this, Raju Kher speaks about brother Anupam Kher. 'Sold flat to invest in a show, channel disappeared' Speaking about the incident and how he sold his house to make a show for a channel that disappeared overnight, Raju told Siddharth Kannan, "There was a time when I was going through a bad phase. I had sold my house because a new channel was coming, so I had bought a flat elsewhere. A new channel was going to launch and many people were making pilots, agreements were already signed. I also made a programme Life Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega. Suddenly, I got to know that the channel has disappeared. I had invested the money that I got from selling the flat in that programme. I thought that I had a first-class life, a 4-BHK house, everything set for the family. And then, the channel disappeared and no one knew what happened.. there was just a lock on their door."

Meanwhile, Raju saw no work coming his way and also faced the pressure of paying rent. During this difficult phase, he expected Anupam Kher to help him. However, Anupam was also going through a difficult phase professionally, as he had stopped taking up projects because he was waiting for substantial roles. This made Raju feel that his brother could have done more to help him.

Notably, He shared, "I also felt the pressure to pay the rent. I had no one else, I could only talk to my brother, and I thought he will help me. But at that time, he had also stopped working. The reason was that he didn't want to do any of those weird films, he wanted substantial roles. So, I felt that my brother did not help me out. 'He could have done so,' that was my thought at that time."
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Raju Kher (@rajukherofficial)

In further updates, However, during the same interaction, Raju admitted that although he had expected Anupam to help him, he later gained a different perspective after reading one of his brother's interviews. Raju recalled reading an interview in which Anupam spoke about his wish to have a child of his own.

On top of that, For the unversed, Anupam is married to star Kirron Kher. Kirron was already a mother to Sikander Kher from her first marriage, and Anupam has often spoken about Sikander as his own child.

Raju shared that hearing Anupam speak about his regret of not having a child of his own made him realise that he had taken his brother 'for granted'. He had assumed that because Anupam was financially successful, he did not have problems of his own. Raju eventually understood that his brother was also dealing with his own struggles.

title: Vidyut Jammwal says Hollywood sets are more disciplined than Bollywood: ‘No actor, whether it is 50 Cent or Jason Momoa, is ever late’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Vidyut Jammwal is all set to make his Hollywood debut with the soon-to-release action movie Street Fighter . Of late, Paramount Pictures India held an event for the movie in Mumbai, where a special featurette featuring the star was unveiled. At the event, Vidyut spoke about the differences between Hollywood and Bollywood movie sets and opened up about his experience working on an international production.

Adding to this, Vidyut Jammwal in a still from Hollywood debut, Street Fighter. Vidyut Jammwal on the difference between Hollywood and Bollywood sets When asked about his experience working on a Hollywood movie and how it differs from a Bollywood movie set, Vidyut shared, "There is a huge difference. I used to hear from my friends who are actors and knew about Hollywood that the budgets there were much higher. But I have seen the discipline here. For the first time, I have seen 300 people on a set following such discipline. There, no star, whether it is 50 Cent, Jason Momoa or Cody Rhodes, is ever late. They simply don’t have a concept of arriving late."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Cody Rhodes (@americannightmarecody)

Notably, The star further lauded Hollywood's strict laws and shared, “There is no such thing as being late. If someone is late by one minute, makers call them to know if they are not doing well. It's a massive difference. Laws are so strict. If you are doing overtime, every technician gets extra money for every minute. Technicians wait to do overtime because they don't think they will be betrayed. The laws are very different. So when you experience something like this with some legends around, you realise this is different. It will take us time to reach that level. We are following the rules and laws but we can get better and do more.”

As per the latest buzz, Vidyut also spoke about his journey to the movie and shared how his long association with martial arts helped him connect with his character. He opened up that he has been training in Kalaripayattu since the age of three and shared that his years of training made him feel that he was meant to play Dhalsim in Street Fighter.

In further updates, Directed by Kitao Sakurai, Street Fighter is based on the popular video game franchise of the same name. The movie stars Noah Centineo as Ken Masters, Andrew Koji as Ryu and Jason Momoa as Blanka, along with Callina Liang, Joe Anoai, David Dastmalchian, Cody Rhodes, Andrew Schulz, Eric Andre, Orville Peck, Olivier Richters, Hirooki Goto, Rayna Vallandingham, Alexander Volkanovski and Curtis ‘50 Cent’ Jackson.

On top of that, The official synopsis of the movie reads, "Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li (Callina Liang) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don't, it's GAME OVER!"
The movie is scheduled to rollout in theatres in India on October 16 in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.

title: Drishyam 3 worldwide box office collection: Ajay Devgn's film crosses ₹300 crore mark despite drop
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ajay Devgn -starrer Drishyam 3 has broken several box-office records since its rollout on Friday. After a record-breaking opening and a money-minting weekend, the movie slowed down a bit on Monday. However, that did not stop it from crossing an important milestone in its worldwide collection.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 has crossed ₹300 crore rupees mark. Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings The Ajay Devgn -starrer collected ₹ 21 crore rupees on Monday in India. This was an almost 65% drop from the movie's Sunday collection of ₹ 61 crore rupees. By the end of Monday, the movie's total India net collection stood at ₹ 197.50 crore rupees, with its India gross reaching ₹ 237 crore rupees. Overseas, the movie collected ₹ 5 crore rupees, pushing its worldwide gross collection to ₹ 303 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, Drishyam 3 started its box-office journey on Friday, earning ₹ 62 crore rupees, becoming the biggest opener of Ajay Devgn's career and the third-highest opening recorded by a Hindi movie after Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan and Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar: The Revenge. The movie also surpassed the opening collections of blockbusters such as Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan, Animal, Dhurandhar and more.

Notably, The movie continued its momentum over the weekend, earning ₹ 53.50 crore rupees on Saturday and ₹ 61 crore rupees on Sunday. Like most films, it saw a fall in collections on Monday, but this did not stop it from crossing the ₹ 300 crore rupees mark worldwide.

As per the latest buzz, Drishyam 3 is being lauded by followers for its writing, with many praising the writers for giving the beloved franchise a fitting ending. Of late, while in conversation with the Free Press Journal, screenwriter Aamil Keeyan Khan spoke about writing over 100 drafts of the movie to get its ending right.

In further updates, He shared, "It was an enormous mountain to climb. You have a beloved franchise, a family that the audiences have lived with for years, and the legacy of two hugely loved films sitting on your shoulders. And most importantly, how do you surprise an audience for the third time? There was the challenge of writing an original screenplay while retaining the DNA of Drishyam. It still had to have humour, family, emotion, drama and thrills without any one ingredient swallowing the others. It was a very, very thin tightrope. Thankfully, none of us looked down."

On top of that, The third part of the franchise stars Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav and Kamlesh Sawant. The movie also features new entrants Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj. It is directed by Abhishek Pathak.

title: MPSC protest: Pune Police start legal action, issue notices to 80
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Pune Police have issued notices to 51 students and 29 coaching class and study-room operators for supporting or participating in the protests demanding greater transparency in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) exams and the resignation of the commission’s chairman, people aware of the matter shared on Tuesday.

Adding to this, Protesters are demanding greater transparency in the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) exams. (PTI) The action came as the protests continued at three sites in Pune despite denial of police permission. Police shared further proceedings, including registration of criminal cases, could follow if the protests continued without permission.
Meanwhile, Thousands of job aspirants have been participating in the protests over issues concerning the commission’s functioning, examination patterns, recruitment, etc.

Notably, A police officer shared organisers were instructed against the protests after permission was denied. “The protests continued, prompting the police to start collecting evidence through video recordings and documenting the situation at the protest sites,” the officer shared.

As per the latest buzz, Police shared the recordings, notices and instructions issued to organisers and the continuation of the protests despite warnings would form the basis for further legal proceedings.

In further updates, Police have also launched an inquiry after a drone was spotted flying over the protest site near SM Joshi Bridge. They were trying to establish who operated the drone and why it was being used.

On top of that, Police shared action could be taken if the drone was found to have been operated without the required permission, including for recording the protest. Security has been increased at all three protest locations to prevent any law-and-order situation, police shared.

The protests in Pune are the latest in a series of such agitations. In July, student protests over examination irregularities forced the then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. Job aspirants and student unions, agitating against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams for nearly a month, revealed a suspension of their sit-in after the Jharkhand government conceded to almost all of their key demands.

title: 17 protesters accused of vandalism during anti-SIR protest in Delhi get bail
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A Delhi court on Monday granted bail to 17 protestors accused of vandalism and defacement of public property during the protest over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, noting that they are young students and did not appear to be habitual offenders.

Adding to this, The Delhi Police registered four cases following clashes between security personnel and members of the NSUI and IYC during protests against the SIR exercise. (HT PHOTO) The 17 protestors were produced before Judicial Magistrate First Class Animesh Tripathi of Patiala House Courts in a late-night hearing.

Meanwhile, The Delhi Police sought 14-day judicial custody, alleging that they were part of an unlawful assembly and had obstructed public space where prohibitory orders were in force. They added that their judicial custody remand was imperative as they could indulge again in violence if rolled out.

Notably, Police alleged that the protestors manhandled officials, including a woman police officer who sustained injuries, while they were being detained to control the situation. They also broke the window glass and rear side glass in which they were kept and accordingly damaged the public property, they submitted.

As per the latest buzz, Opposing the remand plea, defence counsel advocate Saimon Farooqui argued that all the offences invoked carried imprisonment of less than seven years and the accused should therefore not have been arrested. He submitted that no specific roles had been assigned to the accused and that no CCTV footage had been produced to corroborate the allegations.

In further updates, The court shared the allegations were serious, noting that a Medico-Legal Certificate (MLC) showed that a police officer had allegedly sustained injuries. “It should be noted that the allegations against the accused are serious in nature. One police officer has allegedly sustained injuries as per the MLC produced by the Investigating Officer,” the court shared.
On top of that, “While any person has a right to protest peacefully, however, assaulting police officials on duty is a serious concern which cannot be permitted under the garb of peaceful protest.”

The court noted that most of the offences are bailable and carry a maximum punishment of two years. “The accused persons are young and do not appear to be habitual offenders. They have their career lying ahead.”

title: Namit Malhotra's Ramayana team behind Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha's 'negative marketing'? Producer says, 'they're asking people not to watch film'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ahead of Nitesh Tiwari 's Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer Ramayana, another movie based on the mythological epic, Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha , was rolled out in theatres on September 25. However, the movie faced negative reactions over its casting even before its rollout and failed to make an impact at the ticket-window. In an interview with India Today, the movie's producer, Prakash Mahobiya, alleged that negative buzz surrounding the movie was part of a wider campaign and claimed that the team is now planning to re-rollout it.

Adding to this, Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha's producer alleges negative marketing by Ramayana team. Prakash Mahobiya alleges negative PR against Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha Prakash alleged that negative comments about the movie were circulated among YouTubers and influencers, which prevented many people from giving it a chance. He shared, "It was negative marketing throughout. We never got a chance to reach our audience. The ones who watched our movie really enjoyed it. But if they never got to see it, how will they even have an opinion?"

Meanwhile, He added, "From what we have been told, there are other movies on the same subject coming in, the big-budget movie. As far as we know, a lot of negative marketing opportunities have been given to YouTubers, influencers and other people. They are spreading wrong information and asking people not to watch our movie."
Notably, When Prakash was asked if he was accusing Nitesh Tiwari and Namit Malhotra's team of being behind the alleged campaign, he shared he was not sure, but that this was what they had been told.

As per the latest buzz, Helmed by Abhishek Singh, the movie features Anjali Arora, Dev Sharma and Rajneish Duggal in lead roles. Before its rollout, the movie faced backlash over Anjali's casting as Sita and criticism of its VFX. After its rollout, viewers also pointed out several issues, including a poster which showed one of the members of the Vanar Sena wearing spectacles. The criticism continued after the movie's rollout, and it collected only ₹ 46 lakh worldwide, according to Sacnilk.

In further updates, Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari and backed by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the two-part epic is mounted on a reported budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, along with Ravi Dubey, Sunny Deol, Rakul Preet Singh and others in key roles. The movie will be rolled out in two parts, with the first part scheduled to rollout on Diwali 2026 and the second on Diwali 2027.

In its first weekend, Drishyam 3 has outpaced the collections of films such as War and Tiger 3, beating the lifetime of Awarapan 2. It remains to be seen how the movie fares through the week.

title: Anant Joshi admits backlash over replacing Vaibhav Raj Gupta as Gullak’s Annu Bhaiya affected him: ‘Made me question my choice’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

This year, followers saw two of their beloved characters being replaced. Mirzapur made the transition from the web series to the big screen with Mirzapur: The Movie, with Jitendra Kumar stepping into the role of Bablu Pandit, originally played by Vikrant Massey . Similarly, the fifth season of the popular web show Gullak saw Anant V Joshi replace Vaibhav Raj Gupta as the beloved character Annu Bhaiya.

Adding to this, Anant V Joshi spoke about replacing Vaibhav Raj Gupta in Gullak. 'There was a little bit of nervousness' Playing a well-established character can be tricky, as it can invite scrutiny from the character's ardent followers. Anant, in a recent interaction, admitted that the backlash he faced when the Gullak Season 5 trailer was rolled out affected him.

Meanwhile, In conversation with NDTV, he shared, "More than pressure, it was nervousness. There was a bit of pressure because there were doubts. After all, Vaibhav did it so well. The show is so loved. It has such a massive fan base, which I only realised after Season 5 came out. But I was very excited to bring my own lived experiences to the character. So, yeah, I was excited to play the character. But there was a little bit of nervousness about how the audience was going to respond."
Notably, Sharing how the audience's reaction changed after the season was rolled out, Anant shared the initial backlash made him question his decision to take on the role.

As per the latest buzz, He shared, "When the trailer came out, there was backlash. It really affected me. It made me question my choice. Did I do it right? Because people were absolutely missing their favourite character. But when the show came out and the way the reactions completely flipped, that was an even higher high. Because when you are not expecting it at all, you are already prepared that maybe that was not probably a good choice. You have stepped onto a really big show. But out of expectation, when that kind of love comes through, I think that was the biggest or the most rewarding feeling."

In further updates, Created by Shreyansh Pandey and produced by The Widely shared Fever, Gullak revolves around the Mishra family and their everyday lives. The series follows parents Santosh (Jameel Khan) and Shanti Mishra (Geetanjali Kulkarni) and their sons Anand, fondly known as Annu, and Aman (Harsh Mayar). The show is known for its slice-of-life storytelling, family dynamics and humour rooted in everyday middle-class experiences.
On top of that, Gullak Season 5 premiered on SonyLIV on June 5, 2026.

title: Dia Mirza Rekhi: Just speaking up about things is not enough, it should follow through with action
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Twenty-five years after making her debut, Dia Mirza Rekhi finds herself in a place where stories with a soul matter more than ever. Having moved seamlessly between mainstream cinema, production and socially conscious content, she now asks herself a simple question before taking on a project: "Why is this story being told, and what impact is it going to have?" For Dia, who shot exclusively for HT City Showstoppers, purpose comes first. “Those answers matter to me more than ever. And then, of course, it extends itself to: Why does the character matter, and what can this character contribute?”

Adding to this, The star wears a vibrant red saree from Roseroom by Isha Jajodia styled with a delicate pendant necklace from CLARA. The star wears a pure handloom saree featuring real zari from Aliyana By Meena Bazaar, paired with a statement neckpiece from Jain Parash Jewellers. The success of her latest show, Operation Safed Sagar, a military war drama, has only reaffirmed that instinct. She is delighted by the response, particularly because of the integrity with which the story was made. "There was something so unhurried about the way this story was approached," she says, pointing to the research, writing, shooting and execution. For an star who chooses parts for their depth rather than their screen time, the philosophy remains simple: “It's not about length, but really about depth.”

Meanwhile, That sense of purpose extends well beyond cinema. Dia has spent years advocating for environmental action, but believes the conversation now needs to focus on the very direct link between the planet and our own lives. "We are dealing with a triple planetary crisis of climate change, pollution and biodiversity loss." Still, optimism comes naturally to her. "I'm an optimist. I would like to believe we care enough about our own survival to do better - and, hopefully, a lot more of it."

Notably, For Dia, speaking up only matters when it is followed by action. "Just speaking up is not enough." Her activism has always come from a place of love, she says, which has also helped her weather the criticism that comes with being vocal. "I have always responded from a place of love, so the hate has never bothered me."

As per the latest buzz, Dia's advocacy for women and children is closely tied to her wider commitment to social justice. As a UN SDG Advocate and UNEP Goodwill Ambassador, she has used her platform to speak about women's participation in decision-making, climate leadership and the importance of representation. Her association with Save the Children has also seen her advocate for the rights and wellbeing of vulnerable children. For Dia, these causes are interconnected, rooted in a larger belief in building a more equitable and compassionate world.

In further updates, Perhaps that philosophy explains her approach to fashion, too. Twenty-five years in the public eye have given her a front-row view of Bollywood's changing aesthetics, but trends have never been the destination. "For me. fashion has never been about what is in trend. It's always been about seeking stories." She finds them in handwoven textiles, handcraft, artisanship and community. Her fascination began with her mother's wardrobe, where every piece carried “a powerful, beautiful story of our legacy, of our history, of many centuries of inheritance.”

On top of that, Her most treasured possession is her great-grandmother's saree, which she estimates to be at least 300 years old. She has worn it before and plans to wear it again soon. It feels like the perfect Dia Mirza Rekhi metaphor: rooted in history, engaged with the present and looking ahead.

title: Pooja Meri Jaan review: Mrunal Thakur starrer asks difficult questions about consent, but offers convenient answers
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Consent on screen has come a long way. From “tu haan kar ya na kar, tu hai meri Kiran” to having two films in the same week, Prem Keetanu and Pooja Meri Jaan , where the woman’s decision is final and binding... Bollywood seems to be finally getting the memo.

Adding to this, Pooja Meri Jaan review: Mrunal Thakur plays the lead role. Pooja Meri Jaan story Pooja Meri Jaan must have sounded intriguing on paper. The story revolves around Pooja ( Mrunal Thakur ), an star who plays Juliet in a theatre production of Romeo and Juliet. Her on-stage Romeo, Aniket (Vikram Singh Chauhan), proposes to her after a performance. Too shocked to respond, she rejects him after the show, and, in a fit of rage, tells him he can “go and die” for all she cares. He ends up taking his own life, leaving Pooja accused of abetting his suicide. Did her rejection and those angry words really push him to take such a drastic step? That question forms the crux.

Meanwhile, One hears that the movie’s rollout was stuck for nearly four years before this Navjot Gulati directorial finally saw the light of day. Yet, given how relevant its themes remain today, the delay has done little to date the subject. The movie starts on a promising note, venturing into the tricky, often misunderstood territory of how consent can be fluid and, most importantly, how it must be respected at every stage. A woman may choose to be in a relationship with someone one day and change her mind the next, and that decision deserves to be accepted without question. The movie also touches upon the complicated issue of leading someone on, among several other facets of relationships and rejection.
Notably, The problem is that, as complex as this entire discussion is, the movie itself never quite arrives at a satisfying understanding of it.

As per the latest buzz, Niren Bhatt’s screenplay does have a promising arc. What may appear to the outside world as an innocuous crush can, from the woman’s perspective, quickly take on an unsettling, even sinister, dimension. The screenplay also brings the alpha male mentality into the conversation, examining the sense of entitlement that can turn attraction into obsession. But the movie ultimately takes the most convenient route out of this morally murky territory. In its eagerness to establish Pooja’s innocence, it ties up the ambiguity far too neatly.

In further updates, Performance-wise, Mrunal Thakur plays her part well as Pooja. Huma Qureshi as Sana Mahfooz, who plays Pooja's lawyer, delivers. Vishal Singh Chauhan, as Aniket, comes off as slightly irritating, and that's a win because that's the character's demand.

On top of that, Overall, Pooja Meri Jaan deserves credit for attempting to engage with a conversation that Hindi cinema has, till now, approached rather simplistically. It understands that consent is not a one-time contract, and attraction does not create entitlement. More importantly, rejection, however hurtful, cannot be treated as an offence. There are moments when the movie gets close to the grey areas of modern relationships, where intentions can be misread. Unfortunately, it lacks the courage to stay in that grey zone for long. Instead, it eventually opts for a convenient resolution, diluting some of the complexity it so carefully built up.

In a beat driven by loud PR machinery and carefully scripted answers, Rishabh prefers cutting through the noise to focus on how stories get made and why trends shift. title: Shefali Shah on writing about her first divorce with Harsh Chhaya in memoir: ‘Nothing to really hide’
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Bollywood star Shefali Shah rarely speaks about her personal life, but the star of late opened up about it in The Audacity of Being, her memoir-in-essays. During a recent interaction, she spoke about writing about her first marriage and divorce from star Harsh Chhaya , and her experience of watching a marriage fall apart.

Adding to this, Shefali Shah opens up on split with star Harsh Chhaya. 'Nobody’s prepared for a divorce' In conversation with The Indian Express, Shefali shared, “I’m not naming anyone in the book. I’m not even getting into what happened or didn’t happen. I’m just talking about what happens on a general scale when people get married and nobody’s prepared for a divorce.”

Meanwhile, Shefali spoke about how people often enter marriage with “the idea of a happily-ever-after”, but when things do not go as planned, and the marriage does not work out, they have to deal with the reality of the relationship ending.

Notably, Asked about her decision to speak about her first marriage and divorce, and the candour with which she has written about her life, she shared, “There was nothing to really hide about. I think I’ve written about it very respectfully. I’m just talking about any marriage falling off the brink. There’s an entire thing about when you realise your marriage is falling apart. So it’s, I think, about the failure of a relationship.”

As per the latest buzz, Shefali was married to star Harsh before the two parted ways. The couple got married in 1997 and divorced in 2001. She has largely kept details of the relationship private and has rarely spoken publicly about their marriage or divorce.

In further updates, After her divorce, Shefali married filmmaker and producer Vipul Amrutlal Shah in 2000. The couple have two sons, Aryaman and Maurya. Shefali and Vipul have also worked together professionally, with Vipul producing some of the projects featuring the star.

On top of that, Shefali Shah has established herself as one of the most acclaimed actors in Hindi cinema. title: Shekhar Suman defends Sanjay Dutt after backlash over ‘no peace in India’ remark: ‘He has huge respect for our country’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Sanjay Dutt 's recent comments about not feeling the same sense of “peace” in India have sparked a social media debate. The star has since clarified that the remarks were part of a scripted, satirical conversation and were not intended to offend anyone. Shekhar Suman , whose show the star appeared on, has also defended him, saying the star's words were misunderstood and taken out of context.

Adding to this, Shekhar Suman defends Sanjay Dutt over ‘no peace’ comment, says star ‘has utmost regard’ for India. Shekhar Suman comes out in Sanjay Dutt's defence The row started after Sanjay Dutt appeared on Shekhar Suman's show Shekhar Tonite in a special episode for Gandhi Jayanti. Shekhar has now backed Sanjay, arguing that the star's comments were neither malicious nor anti-national. In conversation with NDTV, he shared the star has always had deep respect for India and its people. "Sanjay Dutt has huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen, and what he shared was completely innocuous and in a very positive way. He should not be penalised and maligned for what he never shared or meant. I know him for years; he is a good man who loves his country and has utmost regard for it," Suman told the publication.

Meanwhile, Suman also pointed to the nature of his programme, describing Shekhar Tonite as a satirical show that is “pro-people” and “totally unbiased and democratic.” According to him, the segment was intended as light-hearted commentary rather than an attempt to offend or target anyone.
Notably, While discussing India and its people, the star spoke about the need for peace and shared he felt that something had changed.

As per the latest buzz, “The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I can't feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people, and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shiv ji that those days come back soon,” he shared on the show.

In further updates, With the comments attracting backlash, Sanjay took to X to explain the context behind what he had shared. He stressed that he never intended to hurt or disrespect anyone and shared the exchange was scripted and meant to be light-hearted. “I would like to clarify that it was never my intention to hurt, offend, or disrespect the sentiments of any individual, community, or institution,” he wrote.

On top of that, The star also connected the segment to the humour and satire associated with his Munna Bhai films. He shared the conversation was meant to carry the same message of warmth and togetherness that was central to the idea of Gandhigiri.

"My remarks were made in the context of a scripted conversation intended to be light-hearted and humorous. The spirit behind them was similar to the humour and satire seen in films like Munna Bhai , particularly the concept of ‘Gandhigiri,’ which was intended to convey a message of love, warmth, togetherness, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted outside of that intended context," he shared.
