title: Amitabh Bachchan reveals he struggles to find time to sleep amid KBC shoot: ‘Must run to bed’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Amitabh Bachchan of late left his followers worried after revealing that he had slipped on the Kaun Banega Crorepati set and injured his knee. Now, the star has taken to his blog to speak about struggling to find time to sleep on time, something he believes would help his tired body repair and recover.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan speaks about difficulty in sleeping. Amitabh Bachchan on facing sleepless nights Amitabh wrote on his blog, "They shared the night sleep is the best repair mechanism of the human body .. and I struggle to find the time to follow that... But tonight is a try... now to retire early and be up for a early wake for work .. it is a different feel .. a state of many thoughts and ideas .. all filled with drive and a sense of conquering all that was once considered as a goal .. that gives immense power to run to its destination, in time .. and I must run to the bed."

Meanwhile, In a recent episode of Kaun Banega Crorepati, Amitabh opened up that he had slipped and injured his knee. The star entered the show running towards his seat but quickly chose to sit down. He explained, “Usually, I do my monologue standing at the centre, but today, I have a knee injury. Yesterday, during the shoot, I slipped and fell and injured my knee.”

Notably, The star pointed towards his left knee while talking about the injury. After seeing the audience's worried expressions, Amitabh quickly reassured them that the injury was not severe. He shared he would stand up to host the contestants but had chosen to sit during the opening monologue because he had a “little bit of difficulty standing up”.

As per the latest buzz, However, a few days after speaking about his knee injury, Amitabh was seen out and about in Mumbai. He attended a book launch event with his wife and veteran star Jaya Bachchan. Legendary writer Gulzar was also spotted at the event, sharing a laugh with the Bachchans.

In further updates, Amitabh will reprise his role as Ashwatthama in Nag Ashwin’s Kalki 2898 AD Part 2. The movie also stars Prabhas and Kamal Haasan in lead roles. As per the latest buzz, Amitabh is also associated with Aankhen 2, though little has been revealed about the movie.

On top of that, The star also has Section 84 in the pipeline. The courtroom drama is directed by Ribhu Dasgupta and also stars Diana Penty, Nimrat Kaur and Abhishek Banerjee in pivotal roles. The movie is currently in post-production.

Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows. A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today. At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through movie reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, star interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing. Now, as Assistant Editor at Hindustan Times Entertainment, Vibha continues to chronicle the world of movies and pop culture. Her work spans breaking entertainment news, exclusive interviews, star features, and stories that capture the conversations shaping Indian cinema. Read More

title: Big B recommended my name, Jaya ji was original choice: Shefali Shah on 'Waqt'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

New Delhi, Shefali Shah says her husband Vipul Shah had advised her against taking the role of a mother in his 2005 directorial "Waqt" when she was barely in her 30s but she ended up doing the part after other casting choices fell through and Amitabh Bachchan recommended her name.

Adding to this, Big B recommended my name, Jaya ji was original choice: Shefali Shah on 'Waqt' In the movie, she played Akshay Kumar's mother though she was younger than him in real life. Her casting raised eyebrows at the time and ended up affecting the kind of roles that came her way.
Meanwhile, Shah has now looked back at this chapter in her debut book, "The Audacity of Being: A Sort-of Memoir".

Notably, According to the 53-year-old star, Vipul originally wanted veteran star Jaya Bachchan for the role. Hema Malini was also considered, but the idea was eventually dropped as it felt too similar to the Amitabh Bachchan-Hema Malini starrer "Baghban", which was rolled out in 2003.

As per the latest buzz, "The mother, Sumi, was the anchor of the story the silent strength between the father and the son. Vipul had originally wanted Jaya ji, but that did not work out. Hema Malini ji was another great choice, but it felt too much like a repeat of 'Baghban', a movie that Amit ji and Hema ji had done only a while ago," Shah wrote.
In further updates, "Waqt: The race against time", which also starred Priyanka Chopra, was based on "Aavjo Vhala, Fari Malishu" , a play written and directed by Aatish Kapadia.
On top of that, Shah shared she fell in love with the character of Sumi after watching the play and eventually asked Vipul if she could play the role.
"He flat out shared no and insisted it would not work, warning me that it would label me as a 'mother' on screen forever," she wrote.

title: ‘Well over a hundred drafts’: Drishyam 3 screenwriter reveals how the franchise’s ending was cracked
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ajay Devgn -starrer Drishyam : The Conclusion has given the star the biggest opening of his career. The movie isn't just ruling the ticket-window but has also received rave reviews from critics and audiences. Malayalam followers, too, are lauding the movie's writing, with some even calling it better than the original Mohanlal-starrer Malayalam movie. Now, the movie's screenwriter Aamil Keeyan Khan has spoken about the writing process and opened up that it took him over 100 drafts to get the ending of Drishyam 3 right.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 stars Ajay Devgn, Tabu, Shriya Saran, and Jaideep Ahlawat. (HT_PRINT) ‘There was the challenge of writing an original screenplay’ In conversation with The Free Press Journal, Aamil spoke about the big task of writing a new story for Drishyam 3 without borrowing from the original movie, while keeping the essence of the popular franchise alive.

Meanwhile, He shared, "It was an enormous mountain to climb. You have a beloved franchise, a family that the audiences have lived with for years, and the legacy of two hugely loved films sitting on your shoulders. And most importantly, how do you surprise an audience for the third time? There was the challenge of writing an original screenplay while retaining the DNA of Drishyam. It still had to have humour, family, emotion, drama and thrills without any one ingredient swallowing the others. It was a very, very thin tightrope. Thankfully, none of us looked down."
Notably, The screenwriter shared that the task of doing justice to Drishyam 3 wasn't easy and opened up that he went through more than 100 drafts to get the franchise's ending right.

As per the latest buzz, He shared, "I have folders inside folders, drafts with dates, numbers, dates after numbers, and files called things like “FINAL”, “FINAL 2”, “FINAL FINAL” and presumably “FINAL PLEASE GOD”. I have genuinely lost count, but well over a hundred drafts in different forms. Easily."

In further updates, Drishyam: The Conclusion marks a major departure for the Hindi franchise as it has an original story and ending. The first two Hindi films were direct remakes of Mohanlal's Malayalam Drishyam films, while the third instalment takes the story of Vijay Salgaonkar and his family in a new direction.

On top of that, Directed by Abhishek Pathak, the movie brings back Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Shriya Saran, Tabu, Ishita Dutta and Mrunal Jadhav. Jaideep Ahlawat, Rajat Kapoor and Prakash Raj are also part of the cast.

title: Unannounced protest on Gurugram’s Sohna Road triggers hours-long traffic jam
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

An unannounced student protest on Gurugram’s Sohna Road triggered a traffic jam along a nearly three-kilometre stretch on Monday afternoon, with an ambulance remaining stuck for over 40 minutes. Paramedics and motorists watched helplessly as tightly packed cars, trucks, and motorcycles filled every inch, making it impossible for the ambulance to move.

Adding to this, Bumper-to-bumper traffic lasted for over two to three hours. Desperate two-wheeler riders tried squeezing through narrow footpath edges, only to block lanes. The jam choked key arterial roads, from the busy Rajiv Chowk underpass and junction past Tau Devi Lal Sports Complex up to Civil Lines and the District and Sessions Court.

Meanwhile, An HT spot check found bumper-to-bumper traffic for over two to three hours. “We had not moved an inch in nearly 40 minutes,” shared a commuter in his car en route to Old Gurugram. “Inside the underpass, the trapped exhaust fumes and blaring horns were suffocating. The worst part was seeing an ambulance siren wailing right behind us with nowhere to go.”

Notably, Gurugram traffic police officers shared some students staged the unannounced sit-in outside the State Council of Educational Research and Training office over some admission issues. “The traffic police were prompt in diverting traffic to ease the congestion. Our teams were deployed on the ground continuously to monitor the situation,” shared Gurugram traffic police spokesperson Vikas Verma.
As per the latest buzz, Traffic police personnel took nearly three hours to regulate and implement diversions to gradually ease the bottleneck and restore normal vehicular flow.

In further updates, Sampurna Panigrahi is a Correspondent at the Gurugram Bureau of Hindustan Times, where she covers crime, health, civic issues, traffic, and pollution. With over three years of experience in the field, Sampurna's journalism is driven by passion. She joined the Gurugram team in March 2026 and has since reported extensively on the city's sanitation challenges, crumbling infrastructure, public health systems and rapid urban transformation. Sampurna has a knack for numbers; she loves chasing data-driven stories and uncovering trends. Her reporting is rooted in rigorous groundwork, supported by data and official records. She enjoys digging through datasets, identifying trends and translating complex civic and policy issues into stories that are accessible and meaningful for readers. She likes to travel to different parts of the city and is a team player. Before joining Hindustan Times, Sampurna worked at ThePrint for over two years, where she reported on economy, finance, industry, and governance policies. The experience continues to shape her analytical approach to reporting. For Sampurna, journalism is about listening before writing. Every face, every voice has a story waiting to be heard, and she believes patience and empathy are often a reporter's most valuable tools. title: Rakul Preet Singh BREAKS silence on Income Tax searches, DENIES involvement in illegal foreign remittances: "Have been paying my due taxes since the age of 20"
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Addressing the reports, Rakul shared that she wanted to clarify her position and objected to what she described as unverified and sensationalised coverage. “It’s heartbreaking to see that there’s a growing trend amongst the self styled online reporters & some mainstream media journalists to sensationalise the news without verifying facts,” she shared.

Adding to this, Rakul went on to specifically deny that she was involved in the alleged financial irregularities. “The search was not pertaining to me,” she shared, adding that she comes from an Armed Forces background and entered the movie industry without a godfather. The star also shared that she has been paying her taxes since the age of 20 and described herself as a responsible, law-abiding citizen. “I am not involved in any kind of illegal foreign remittance in personal capacity or on behalf of any Production house,” Rakul shared.

Meanwhile, Rakul also addressed speculation surrounding alleged undisclosed assets. She shared that she does not hold any benami property for anyone in India or abroad. “I would also add here that I do not hold any Benami property on behalf of anyone anywhere in the country or abroad,” she shared. The star further shared that nobody had ever gifted her any property and that she does not accept expensive gifts as a matter of principle.

Notably, Rakul concluded her statement by calling on publications and individuals who, according to her, had published inaccurate reports to retract them and clarify the facts. “I urge all those who published these false, malicious and speculative reports to retract them and clarify the facts,” she shared.

As per the latest buzz, Acknowledging the commercial pressures faced by media organisations, Rakul shared that such pressures should not come at the expense of accuracy or an individual's reputation. “I understand that everyone running a media business however big has their own commercial pressures. But it cannot come at the cost of facts. And certainly not at the cost of someone’s reputation and livelihood,” she added.

In further updates, On September 28, the Mumbai Income Tax Department conducted searches at around 12 locations as per reports linked to Rakul, her father-in-law and producer Vashu Bhagnani, and Panorama Studios, associated with producer Kumar Mangat Pathak. The searches were as per reports part of an investigation into suspected irregularities involving movie financing and overseas transactions.

On top of that, Reports had shared that officials were examining documents, bank records and financial transactions as part of the probe. The focus was as per reports on substantial funds allegedly remitted overseas under the shared heads of shooting expenses, production costs and overseas distribution. However, no specific amount, formal finding or charge has been publicly revealed by the authorities. A search by an investigative agency does not by itself establish wrongdoing, and the investigation remains ongoing.

title: Ajay Devgn leaves superstars Tom Cruise, Brad Pitt in the dust as Drishyam 3 outearns Digger and Heart of the Beast globally
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

There have been very few times when Indian films have had global releases at the ticket-window and come out victorious. RRR was famously the number one movie in the world upon its rollout, as was Dhurandhar The Revenge. Others, like Jawan and Kalki 2898 AD, also challenged big releases. But never has an Indian movie outearned a Tom Cruise -starrer in a direct clash, up until now. Ajay Devgn ’s Drishyam The Conclusion has created a sensation at the international ticket-window, ending up as the number 2 movie in the world on its opening weekend.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings: Ajay Devgn's movie is off to a great start. Drishyam 3 beats Tom Cruise, Brad Pitt films Drishyam The Conclusion had a magnificent start at the Indian ticket-window, minting ₹ 62 crore rupees net on a manic opening day. After sustaining that momentum through the weekend, it reached ₹ 176.50 crore rupees net ( ₹ 211.80 crore rupees or $22 million gross) in three days. In the US and Canada, it did not have a bumper start, but still did well. According to Comscore and Ticket-window Mojo, the movie collected $2.7 million in North America from just over 500 theatres. The movie has been a success outside the US as well. In other international territories (including Europe and the Gulf), it has collected over $3.4 million. As of Sunday, Drishyam The Conclusion has collected $28.4 million ( ₹ 273 crore rupees) worldwide.

Meanwhile, This makes the Ajay Devgn-starrer the second biggest movie in the world this weekend. The only movie ahead of it is Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson’s erotic thriller, Verity, which collected a staggering $62.6 million worldwide, including $32 million in the US and Canada alone.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abhimanyu Mathur (@madcrazyhatter_)

As per the latest buzz, But, Drishyam 3 managed to beat Tom Cruise’s Digger, which also rolled out in theatres this weekend. Digger, Tom’s return to director-backed films after a spate of actioners, was met with negative reviews and opened at just $20 million worldwide, well below what Drishyam 3 managed in the same period. The Hindi movie beat another star-led Hollywood venture this weekend. Brad Pitt’s Heart of the Beast came in third over the weekend, adding $28 million to its total in its second week. The horror movie Resident Evil rounded up the top 5 with a weekend global haul of around $24.5 million.

In further updates, The third part of the franchise brings back Ajay Devgn’s Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also reprises his role from Drishyam 2 in a cameo. The new entrants in the cast are Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj. Written and directed by Abhishek Pathak, the movie rolled out in theatres on October 2, a date quite significant for the franchise.

On top of that, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Richa Chadha says Hanuman Ansh’s ₹400 cr success doesn't mean 2026 is a landmark year for content-driven cinema: ‘Religious stuff works well’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Richa Chadha has a different take on whether 2026 has been a landmark year for content-driven cinema. While Hanuman Ansh has emerged as one of the biggest surprise successes of the year, she believes it may be too early to conclude that the Indian movie industry is witnessing a wider shift in audience preferences. She also decoded the movie’s success and shared what she believes could help Indian cinema become more driven by strong content and scripts.

Adding to this, Richa Chadha talks about Hanuman Ansh. Richa Chadha decodes the success of Hanuman Ansh Richa disagreed with the idea that 2026 has been a landmark year for content and further decoded the success of Hanuman Ansh. She shared, "If it is in the context to Hanuman Ansh, that’s a separate thing. What else has worked this year? Obsession is Hollywood, so we cannot compare our films to theirs. Mythological stuff does relatively well. Be it religious or mythological, it is safe for everyone to see. Yeh toh log dekhte hi hain. It is early to say ki kuch accha ho raha hai (They are bound to watch this. It is too early to say that something good is happening).”

Meanwhile, She further suggested what could help the Indian movie industry become more content-driven and shared, "I feel better scripts and money for writers could lead us to the phase where content-driven cinema takes the lead."

Notably, Vishal Chaturvedi’s Hanuman Ansh, based on the life and teachings of spiritual guru Neem Karoli Baba, has emerged as one of the biggest surprise successes of 2026. The devotional drama, which opened to a relatively quiet response, gradually gained momentum through strong word of mouth and continued to attract audiences weeks after its rollout. Made on a budget of around ₹ 2 crore rupees, the movie crossed ₹ 300 crore rupees in India and ₹ 400 crore rupees worldwide within eight weeks of its theatrical run.

As per the latest buzz, Even with major releases such as The Paradise, The Vvaan - Force of the Forest and Drishyam 3 arriving in theatres, Hanuman Ansh has continued to record steady collections. As of October 5, the movie has crossed ₹ 423 crore rupees worldwide, according to Sacnilk.

In further updates, Following the movie's success, the makers revealed a sequel. The movie's producer, Anupriya Nagar, opened up that the sequel's budget will not be increased to ₹ 20 crore rupees despite the success of the first part, as doing so could lead to unnecessary use of VFX. The movie's success has also led SonyLIV to announce a series on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, although the cast and rollout date are yet to be revealed.

On top of that, Musafiri is the latest project from Richa Chadha and Ali Fazal’s home banner, Pushing Buttons Studios, bringing together travel, personal experiences and the couple’s interest in exploring the city they call home. Hosted, written and produced by Richa, the eight-episode series is available on Phull Stop, the new YouTube channel launched by the star couple.

The idea for Musafiri took shape during Richa’s journey into motherhood. The star has previously shared that becoming a mother made her look at her surroundings differently and sparked a curiosity to discover more about the city where she had built her home, career and family.

title: Drishyam 3 writer Aamil Keeyan Khan reveals how makers protected the film’s biggest twist from the crew
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Drishyam: The Conclusion had one particularly difficult job: surprise an audience that has spent years trying to stay ahead of Ajay Devgn 's Vijay Salgaonkar. Every clue, every suspicious detail and every possible loophole is bound to be examined more closely when it comes to the Drishyam franchise. For writer Aamil Keeyan Khan, that meant the third movie could not simply repeat what had worked before. It had to find a new way to keep viewers guessing.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3: Aamil Keeyan Khan reveals 100+ drafts, Ajay Devgn’s ‘17 tabs’ and why the climax was kept need-to-know. As Drishyam 3 continues its strong run in theatres, Aamil has opened up about what went into creating the final chapter. He also recalled working with Ajay Devgn and why the star's ability to switch between conversations and characters left him stunned.

Meanwhile, One of the biggest questions around Drishyam 3 was how much of its story would come from the Malayalam version starring Mohanlal. Since that movie already exists, there was bound to be curiosity about whether the Hindi version would follow the same path or take a different route.

Notably, Aamil opened up that the Hindi team had actually started working on its own story before they read Jeethu Joseph's draft for the Malayalam movie. The writing began after Drishyam 2, when neither version was ready and the team was still figuring out where the story could go. He believed the two films cannot be looked at simply as the same story being told in two languages. The tone, performances and even the way audiences connect with the characters can change considerably.

As per the latest buzz, If there is one thing the makers of a Drishyam movie cannot afford, it is a leak. The climax and major twists had to remain protected, and director Abhishek Pathak apparently took that responsibility very seriously.

In further updates, In an interview with Free Press Journal, he revealed Abhishek ran the production with the same caution that Vijay Salgaonkar would have used while covering his tracks. "Abhishek basically ran the production like Vijay Salgaonkar would," he shared. “The climax wasn't given to a large part of the crew. People got information on a need-to-know basis. Sometimes a department only knew what it needed to execute a scene, not necessarily why it was executing it. A lot of actors and crew from the movie, and my own friends and relatives, tried to bribe me for the ending. But like Gaitonde, I remained honest and loyal to the producers”.
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abhimanyu Mathur (@madcrazyhatter_)

His time with Ajay Devgn also gave him a glimpse into the star's remarkably quick mind. He recalled a moment while shooting Drishyam 2, when they were in the middle of discussing another movie and Devgn was suddenly called away to shoot a scene.

title: R. Madhavan set to host Game Changers featuring startup founders and global investors; details inside!
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Game Changers will bring together startup founders from different parts of the world, giving them an opportunity to pitch their businesses before an international panel of investors. The investor panel will feature representatives from Dubai, London, Russia and the United States.

Adding to this, Production on the show is scheduled to begin shortly. The format will focus on entrepreneurship, business decisions and the personal journeys behind companies as founders attempt to secure investment and scale their ventures.

Meanwhile, Vipul D Shah, Founder and Chairman of Optimystix, shared the company sees the project as more than a standalone television show. “Game Changers is being developed as a future-facing global entertainment franchise for Optimystix. It is more than a new show. It is an owned IP with the potential to travel across markets, attract marquee brand partnerships and create multiple monetisation streams over time,” he shared.

Notably, He added, “We are combining our proven expertise in creating mass-audience entertainment with a format that speaks directly to the global energy around entrepreneurship, innovation and investment.”

As per the latest buzz, According to Rajesh Bahl, Co-Founder and Group CEO of Optimystix, the format will also explore the people and decisions behind the businesses being presented. “The format goes beyond a conventional pitch show. It spotlights the ambition, resilience, strategy and personal conviction behind promising businesses while giving audiences an inside view of what it takes to build, fund and scale a company in today’s competitive global economy,” he shared.

In further updates, Dubai has been chosen as the production base for the first edition. The city’s position as an international business hub is expected to provide the show with access to founders, investors and businesses from different markets. The UAE edition could also pave the way for regional versions and adaptations of the format in the future.

On top of that, With R. Madhavan as host, the show will combine the business-focused format with a mainstream entertainment element. His role is expected to involve engaging with the participating founders and taking audiences through their journeys as they pitch their ventures to the investor panel.

For Optimystix, Game Changers marks a move towards developing and owning original formats alongside its existing work across television, films, OTT and digital content. The company has produced more than 160 television shows over the past two decades, including Comedy Circus, Crime Patrol, Baalveer, Rising Star and Laughter Chefs. Its movie credits include OMG 2 , Khel Khel Mein and The Diplomat .

title: EXCLUSIVE: Shreyaa Chaudhry of Bandish Bandits fame to star opposite Ayushmann Khurrana in YRF and Posham Pa Pictures’ Mupapa
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Known for her natural performances and ability to bring depth and emotion to her characters, Shreyaa has built a strong connection with audiences through a diverse body of work. Her performances across both seasons of Bandish Bandits were appreciated for their natural and relatable portrayal, while The Mehta Boys further showcased her versatility and ability to take on layered characters. With Mupapa, Shreyaa takes another significant step forward in her career.

Adding to this, Directed by Kaala Paani fame Sameer Saxena, Mupapa is produced by Akshaye Widhani (CEO, Yash Raj Films) and Posham Pa Pictures, the banner Sameer co-founded with Biswapati Sarkar, Saurabh Khanna and Amit Golani. The movie marks the first theatrical collaboration between the studio and the production house. title: 'Please comment on Smit Machchhar's bravery also': Piyush Mishra slams Naseeruddin Shah after his meeting with CJP's Abhijeet Dipke
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Piyush Mishra of late shared a video on social media, accusing veteran star Naseeruddin Shah of selective activism. Naseeruddin Shah of late met Abhijeet Dipke during The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest held at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, where protesters demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Adding to this, Piyush Mishra targets Naseeruddin Shah in latest video. In the video, Piyush questioned Naseeruddin over his silence on the previous Jharkhand student protest and the incident at Lovely Professional University (LPU), but supporting CJP's protest. Moreover, he also questioned Naseeruddin Shah’s silence on Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar’s bravery after the nation lauded him for saving the lives of 174 passengers mid-flight despite being stabbed by his co-pilot.

Meanwhile, The video that Piyush shared on social media has since been doing the rounds online. In it, he shared, "Naseer Sahib, I offer my regards. I am Piyush Mishra, an old acquaintance of yours. It was great to see you meet Abhijeet Dipke. Sir, an accident was averted of late. This happened on a Fly Dubai Flight 1073, a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. In this, Mr Smith Machchhar showed bravery and saved the lives of 180 people. Please comment on this as well, congratulate the captain, he will feel nice."

Notably, He added, "Secondly, sir, please send a message to Lovely Professional University (LPU) students. They study there too and a very dangerous incident has happened there. Girls were dragged down by the police by their hair. There was a fight. You made a comment -- that the students have taught you more that what National School of Drama or FTII taught you -- I didn't understand this statement of yours. I don't know since when did students became acting teachers. Please disclose the same. However, LPU also faced an equally dangerous incident. So, please offer your thoughts to those students as well and send a message to them."

As per the latest buzz, Piyush Mishra also spoke about the time he participated in a Jharkhand student protest and asked Naseeruddin Shah for help, but claimed that the star stayed silent on the matter. Piyush indirectly took a dig at Shah for being vocal about The CJP protest in Delhi over the NEET paper leak, while, according to him, remaining silent when students in Jharkhand protested over alleged irregularities in government exams.

In further updates, Speaking about the same, Piyush made a reference to CJP protesters receiving online food deliveries from around the country as people showed their support for them, while the Jharkhand protest did not see the similar kind of support. He shared, "Third, Sir, I asked you for help for Jharkhand, and you sent me a poem by a Pakistani poet. Sorry sir, they didn't want poems by poets there. They wanted flour, lentils, bread, jaggery and more. They didn't want pizza or burgers."

On top of that, The row between Naseeruddin Shah and Piyush Mishra is not new. Earlier, during the NEET protests in Delhi, Naseeruddin Shah questioned the silence of Bollywood celebrities. In conversation with The Wire, Naseeruddin Shah had shared, "Celebrities will speak when their conscience tells them to do so. There's a saying that a dog with a bone in its mouth cannot bark. As soon as the bone falls from its mouth or its teeth break, then it will bark."

Meanwhile, Piyush Mishra, who attended the Jharkhand protest, expressed his displeasure over a statement made by Naseeruddin Shah. During the protest, he told the media, "Naseeruddin Shah sir, you shared something about celebrities remaining silent on the Cockroach Janata Party protest, saying that dogs with bones in their mouths won't speak. My apologies, but with all due respect, I want to ask you, who are those dogs with bones in their mouths right now?"a. Thank you, sir. Your son, Piyush Mishra. Long live the revolution, sir. Thank you."

title: Janhvi Kapoor condemns morphed AI video from Devara Part 1 song ‘Chuttumalle’: “Consent, choice and respect for a woman's body should be basic”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The star calls out the misuse of AI and says women’s consent, choice and boundaries cannot be open to interpretation.

Adding to this, In a detailed note, Janhvi highlighted how the objectification of women through manipulated digital content has become an increasingly serious concern. She wrote, “The criminal misuse of technology to objectify women and circulate fictionalised content without consent is deeply violating, bordering on sexual assault. Almost every woman in my industry has faced some version of this, and women everywhere are increasingly being subjected to it,” her note read and continued, “Consent, choice and respect for a woman's body should be among the most basic notions of humanity. Yet somehow, they continue to be treated as complicated. They are not.”

Meanwhile, Janhvi further explained that consent cannot be assumed or taken for granted under any circumstances. Drawing an analogy, she wrote, “It is surprising that it still seems too nuanced for some people to understand that even if a woman says yes five days in a row and no on the sixth, that no must be respected. If she happens to wear a miniskirt, it does not give anyone permission to put a camera up her skirt, capture violating angles or visually exploit her body. What a woman is comfortable with, where she draws the line and what she chooses to do with her body are decisions that belong exclusively to her. This is basic.”

Notably, The star also placed the incident within the larger conversation around women’s safety, saying that the threat of violation has now extended into the digital space. “This goes far beyond the ai videos I have dealt with over the last few days, or anything I have personally experienced throughout my career. It is about the larger reality of being a woman, the gaze, the judgement, the constant negotiation for safety, and the feeling that our boundaries somehow remain open to interpretation. That threat has now expanded into the digital sphere, when we have not even adequately addressed the very real, physical fear that continues to disrupt the lives of women every day,” she shared.

As per the latest buzz, Janhvi also stressed that the responsibility cannot solely be placed on women to protect themselves - “The answer cannot simply be to "protect your daughter." we also need to undo the conditioning that makes people believe they are entitled to violate somebody else's boundaries in the first place. And part of that change will come from exemplary men with the moral compass and the spine to say clearly what is right and what is wrong.”

In further updates, The star thanked her Devara co-star NTR Jr., along with Chiranjeevi, Vijay Deverakonda and Khushbu Sundar, for speaking up against the incident and supporting her. She expressed, “I am deeply touched by NTR sir for taking such a strong stand and condemning this violation. Thank you, sir. When someone whom millions look up to speaks up about something that may not directly concern him, it makes a difference to every woman who has experienced some degree of this behaviour.” “Thank you also to Chiranjeevi sir, Vijay and Khushbu ma'am for amplifying that sentiment and calling for action against this mentality and these immoral practices,” she added.

On top of that, She concluded by urging people to reconsider the attitude towards women’s boundaries and choice, “I hope everything unfolding around us right now forces those who participate in any form of harassment to introspect. Is it really too much for a woman to ask to simply be treated and seen as a human being? Her body. Her image. Her boundaries. Her choice.”

title: Drishyam 3 worldwide box office collection: Ajay Devgn film mints ₹272 crore, beats Raid 2, Bhooth Bangla lifetime hauls in opening weekend itself
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings day 3: After a record-breaking start on Friday, Ajay Devgn ’s Drishyam: The Conclusion jas continued its rampage over the remaining weekend. The movie soared past several milestones in its first three days, stopping just short of the ₹ 300-crore rupees mark. The movie is already among the highest-grossing Indian films of 2026, and it still hasn’t even seen its first Monday in theatres yet. If it gets a solid first week, Drishyam 3 will climb higher on that list very quickly.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings day 3: Ajay Devgn in a still from the movie. Drishyam 3 ticket-window update The advance bookings for Drishyam The Conclusion were proof of how well it was slated to perform. The movie minted ₹ 50 crore rupees in gross earnings from India even before rollout. This converted into a strong opening day, helping the movie amass ₹ 93 crore rupees worldwide on Friday. The momentum continued beyond that, on to Saturday and Sunday as well.

Meanwhile, The Abhishek Pathak directorial collected ₹ 53.50 crore rupees net on Saturday in addition to the ₹ 62 crore rupees it collected on Friday. On Sunday, it reported net earnings of ₹ 61 crore rupees. This takes the Drishyam The Conclusion’s domestic earnings to ₹ 176.50 crore rupees net ( ₹ 211.80 crore rupees gross) after three days. The movie has set the record for the seventh biggest opening weekend for a Hindi movie, almost rivalling Sultan and beating War and Tiger 3.

Notably, Overseas, Drishyam 3 did not have the same kind of craze and fervour, but it still performed better than most of Ajay Devgn's films. According to trade sources, Drishyam The Conclusion has remained steady overseas in its first three days. So far, it has collected just over $6 million in international territories. This takes its worldwide gross to ₹ 273 crore rupees in its opening weekend.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abhimanyu Mathur (@madcrazyhatter_)

In further updates, Drishyam 3’s mind-blowing start has put many pan-India films in the shade. It has surpassed the lifetime collections of many recent big-budget films, including Ajay Devgn’s own movie, Raid 2 ( ₹ 243 crore rupees), Aamir Khan’s Sitaare Zameen Par ( ₹ 266 crore rupees), and Akshay Kumar’s Bhooth Bangla ( ₹ 247 crore rupees). Drishyam 3 is now on course to become Ajay Devgn’s highest-grossing movie of all time. For that, it will have to surpass Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 347 crore rupees) and Tanhaji ( ₹ 367 crore rupees).

On top of that, The third part of the franchise brings back Ajay Devgn’s Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also reprises his role from Drishyam 2 in a cameo. The new entrants in the cast are Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj. Written and directed by Abhishek Pathak, the movie rolled out in theatres on October 2, a date quite significant for the franchise.

title: Played young Shah Rukh Khan in Baazigar, became a TV superhero, then quit acting to build media tech company: Where is actor Sumeet Pathak now?
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Many may not immediately recognise the name Sumeet Pathak, but they are likely to remember his face. As a child star, he played the younger version of Shah Rukh Khan ’s Ajay Malhotra in the 1993 thriller Baazigar. The role was brief, but his performance stood out enough to earn him a Filmfare Award for Best Child Star and open more doors in the industry. He continued acting through the 1990s, later became a popular television superhero in Hero Bhakti Hi Shakti Hai, and then gradually moved away from acting. Today, Sumeet is working in a very different part of the entertainment business as a media tech entrepreneur.

Adding to this, Remember the child star who played young Shah Rukh Khan in Baazigar? Here’s where Sumeet Pathak is now. From Baazigar to more films Sumeet made his acting debut with Ek Ladka Ek Ladki in 1992. A year later, Baazigar changed the course of his career. As the young Ajay Malhotra, he played the childhood version of Shah Rukh Khan’s character and made an impression on audiences despite having limited screen time.

Meanwhile, The success of the movie was followed by more work. He appeared in Ikke Pe Ikka in 1994 and went on to feature in Rajkumar and Maahir in 1996. At the same time, he was also working on his training. He graduated from the National School of Drama in Delhi and received training in classical dance.

Notably, Like many child actors, Sumeet eventually had to make the difficult move into adult roles. He returned to films in 2002 with Tumko Na Bhool Paayenge, where he played Salman Khan ’s brother. In 2004, he appeared in Taarzan: The Wonder Car with Vatsal Sheth.

As per the latest buzz, His most memorable adult role, however, came on television. From 2005 to 2007, he played Joy Sehgal in Hungama TV’s Hero Bhakti Hi Shakti Hai. The show became particularly popular with younger viewers, with Joy gaining superpowers from Goddess Durga and using them to take on villains.

In further updates, He was also active as a voice artist. He worked on popular animated shows including Oswald, Power Rangers, Richie Rich and Beyblade. He also lent his voice to the Hindi versions of several South Indian films.

On top of that, View this post on Instagram A completely different career Sumeet eventually chose to step away from acting and move into a different part of the entertainment business. He started Gulmohar Media with his wife and business partner Shweta Pathak, and what began with language localisation has since grown into a much larger post-production operation. The company now has studios across six Indian cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai.

Technology has also become a key part of the way the company works. Gulmohar Media uses cloud-based editing and production, making it possible for teams to work remotely instead of depending entirely on traditional studio setups. The company has also expanded its accessibility work, offering sign language services along with audio description.

title: Raj Thackeray to join Pune MPSC protest, day after MP is heckled for defecting
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray is scheduled to join protests in Pune, demanding greater transparency in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) exams and the resignation of the commission’s chairman, Vivek Bhimnawar, at 4pm on Monday, even as the protesters heckled parliamentarian Omraje Nimbalkar for defecting from Shiv Sena (UBT).

Adding to this, Parliamentarian Omraje Nimbalkar at the protest site. Nimbalkar visited the protest site late on Sunday, the fifth day of the protest. A section of the protesters raised slogans questioning his decision to join the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena in June. Some called him a “traitor”. Nimbalkar defended his decision and insisted that he had not distanced himself from his constituents.

Meanwhile, “I have not gone anywhere. I am right here. I am an elected representative,” he shared. He added that he remained connected with people in his constituency and stood by them during floods, droughts and other crises.
Notably, Nimbalkar shared the lack of power made it difficult for him and his colleagues to carry out work for constituents. He backed the students’ concerns over the MPSC examination system.

As per the latest buzz, Nimbalkar added that an examination is directly linked to a student’s future. He shared irregularities such as question-paper leaks could force the cancellation of examinations, causing severe hardship to aspirants who had prepared for them.
In further updates, Nimbalkar shared the MPSC secretary had been transferred. He added he would meet chief minister Devendra Fadnavis with a delegation of students to press for their demands.

On top of that, Slogan-shouting protesters repeatedly interrupted Nimbalkar’s speech. “I have come here to support you. Have I made a mistake?” asked Nimbalkar amid sloganeering. Agitator Vivekanand Patil appealed to the students to allow him to complete his address. The protesters eventually applauded Nimbalkar after his speech ended.

The agitation continued at three sites. Opposition leaders have visited the Rohit Pawar-led protest at Pune’s SM Joshi Bridge. Ruling Bharatiya Janata Party leaders have visited the group protesting on KBS Road. A third group is holding a separate agitation.

title: Mika Singh asks Diljit Dosanjh why he promoted film with Pakistani actor Hania Aamir but not Border 2: ‘Not even 1%’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mika Singh has lauded Diljit Dosanjh for taking Punjabi music to a global audience, but he also has one question for the singer-star: why does he not promote his Bollywood films more? In a recent conversation with Times Now, Mika shared he was proud of Diljit’s success but was confused by what he sees as a lack of promotion for some of his Hindi films, including Border 2 .

Adding to this, Mika Singh asks Diljit Dosanjh why he stayed quiet on Border 2 but promoted his movie with Hania Aamir. Mika questions Diljit’s Border 2 promotion Mika was asked if he felt jealous of Diljit’s success. He shared there was no reason for him to feel that way and instead spoke about how proud he was to see another Punjabi singer make it big. Mika dismissed any suggestion of jealousy, saying he was proud of Diljit and his achievements. He credited Diljit with carrying forward the legacy of Daler Mehndi as a turbaned Punjabi singer who has made a strong mark in the music industry.

Meanwhile, Mika then brought up Border 2, which starred Diljit alongside Sunny Deol, Varun Dhawan and Ahan Shetty. Directed by Anurag Singh, the movie is a sequel to the 1997 war drama Border and rolled out in January 2026.

Notably, According to Mika, Diljit could have spoken more about the movie and his experience of working with Sunny Deol. “I could be wrong, but I feel that when Border 2 came out, Diljit paaji did not promote it even one per cent. He didn't even thank Sunny paaji one percent. I have never seen Diljit say, ‘It is a big thing that my movie with Sunny Deol is coming.’ He never spoke about Border 2. When the movie came out, and even afterwards, I didn't see him post about it. And Main Vaapas Aaunga was also rolled out, but he didn't put up any post. He made only one post about his movie in which there was a Pakistani artist,” Mika added.

As per the latest buzz, He went on to question why Diljit would choose not to promote Bollywood projects despite being part of them. “I don't understand this. Why don't you promote Bollywood when you work in Bollywood? Then you say, 'I don't need Bollywood,' but you work in Bollywood. I am saying these things to him as a brother. Border 2 is one of the biggest films for our country. It is a movie about Hindustan. Why don't you post about it? You can check his Instagram and see if there is even one video where he has promoted Border 2,” he added.

In further updates, Diljit did share promotional material for Border 2. He unveiled his first look in December 2025 and featured in the movie’s promotional campaign. He also shared some behind-the-scenes videos from the movie and songs.

On top of that, Mika also spoke about Diljit’s Sardaar Ji 3 , which starred Hania Aamir alongside Diljit and Neeru Bajwa. “The only one he posted was about his movie with the Pakistani heroine ( Hania Aamir ). Neeru Bajwa is also in that movie, but there was no mention of Neeru Bajwa. I feel you should promote everything,” he shared.

Sardaar Ji 3 became controversial in 2025 because Hania was part of the cast. Her involvement came under scrutiny amid tensions between India and Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack. The movie did not rollout theatrically in India and instead opened overseas on June 27, 2025.

title: Rakul Preet Singh breaks silence on Income Tax searches at her place, calls reports ‘false, malicious’: The search was not pertaining to me
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Rakul Preet Singh has issued a statement regarding reports that the Income Tax Department conducted searches at her addresses over financial irregularities. The star has called the reports ‘malicious and false’, saying she has no Benami property, as claimed in some reports.

Adding to this, Rakul Preet Singh has addressed the IT searches at locations linked to her. Rakul Preet Singh addresses reports of IT searches In a long note Rakul shared on Instagram, the star addressed some of the news reports about the IT searches at her premises and wrote, “It’s heartbreaking to see that there’s a growing trend amongst the self-styled online reporters & some mainstream media journalists to sensationalise the news without verifying facts. Let’s therefore set the record straight once and for all. The search was not pertaining to me.”

Meanwhile, The star added that she has been paying her income tax for years and has no illegal remittance. “Let it be known that I am from the Armed Forces background & had no Godfather in the Industry. I have come up through sheer hard work & as a responsible law-abiding citizen have been paying my due taxes since the age of 20 years. I am not involved in any kind of illegal foreign remittance in personal capacity or on behalf of any Production house. I would also add here that I do not hold any Benami property on behalf of anyone anywhere in the country or abroad. Neither ANYONE has EVER gifted me any property at any time nor do I accept such expensive gifts as a principle,” wrote Rakul.

Notably, Addressing the reports that claimed that Rakul’s premises had been ‘raided’ due to suspicion of illegal foreign remittances for movie production, she added, “I urge all those who published these false, malicious and speculative reports to retract them and clarify the facts. I understand that everyone running a media business, however big, has their own commercial pressures. But it cannot come at the cost of facts. And certainly not at the cost of someone's reputation and livelihood.”

title: Delhi Police avoid name tags at Jantar Mantar protests to prevent social media targeting
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Police deployed at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar for protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls did not wear name tags as a “deliberate measure” to prevent them from being targeted and identified on social media, officials aware of the matter shared. The measure was adopted because personnel were targeted on social media following the July 20 violence during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) march, they added.

Adding to this, Members of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) and other student organisations take part in a protest march towards Jantar Mantar amid heavy security deployment on Sunday, October 4, 2026. (Sanchit Khanna/HT photo) The CJP called the march after weeks of protests and a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. Thousands of demonstrators attempted to march to Parliament demanding the resignation of the then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over examination paper leaks. Police used tear gas and baton-charged to disperse the crowd as protesters attempted to breach multiple layers of barricades. Videos circulating on social media appeared to show several protesters being beaten. The Delhi Police maintained that force became necessary after demonstrators turned violent.

Meanwhile, On day one of the protests against Kumar on Friday, many protesters photographed and filmed police personnel questioning why they were not wearing name tags. In videos circulated on social media, some police personnel shared their tags had fallen off amid the commotion. Others shared they had forgotten to attach them. Some shared they had deliberately removed the tags to prevent them from coming off. Many refused to offer any explanation.
Notably, Officials aware of the matter shared this deliberate measure was part of lessons learnt from the July 20 protests when police personnel were targeted and identified on social media.

As per the latest buzz, Top officers directly involved in crowd management told their seniors in review meetings of crowd handling during the July CJP protests that they and their families were identified and targeted on social media for doing their jobs. “Many officers shared their families were called out by friends or in social circles. Some officers even reported that their families had been deliberately targeted by colleagues at work and through memes on social media,” shared a police officer aware of the deliberations at the review meetings.

In further updates, The officers involved in crowd management were subsequently assured that no action would be taken against anyone for removing name tags if they were performing their duty within the law. “While most IPS [Indian Police Service] officers, who are easily identified by the public, chose to retain their tags at Jantar Mantar this time, many junior personnel were allowed to be on the ground without wearing their tags,” the officer shared. He added that many influencers were posing as media personnel and deliberately targeting police officers.

On top of that, Security forces have had a no-name-tags strategy in Left Wing Extremism-affected areas, the northeast and Jammu and Kashmir. In photographs of anti-insurgency operations, the faces of special forces personnel are blurred.

The removal of tags in Delhi drew criticism as police were accused of excesses while quelling the protests in July. Experts shared there are no written rules mandating whether personnel must wear or remove their name tags. It has long been an operational practice in conflict zones to prevent them from being identified and targeted.

title: Delhi protests LIVE: CJP claims govt planning to arrest Dipke, spokespersons before Oct 10 stir against CEC
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

In this image posted on Oct 2, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke waves to supporters during a protest by CJP against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar Protest news LIVE: Security officials and protesters clashed for at least three hours in central Delhi on Sunday, the third consecutive day of protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. More than 120 people were briefly detained as police reiterated that no permission had been granted for the demonstrations. While protesters alleged they had been manhandled, police shared they used minimum force. ...Read More

Adding to this, The protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar began on October 2, however, the detentions by security forces have triggered calls for extension of the agitation, with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announcing a mega demonstration on October 10. Abhijeet Dipke's CJP led protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar from Mumbai's Shivaji Park on October 2. The protest was also escalated by the accusation of three women journalists against police officers of sexually harassing them during the protest against the Election Commission (EC) at Jantar Mantar on Saturday. Their complaints were forwarded to the crime branch for a detailed probe, the police shared on Sunday. In a post on X, the Delhi Police shared: “On October 3, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. The New Delhi district has received their complaints and the same are transferred to crime branch for fair and impartial enquiry.” Anti-Gyanesh Kumar protest | Key points -Delhi Police deployed around 5,000 personnel, including Rapid Action Force (RAF) and other paramilitary personnel, ahead of protest marches from India Gate to Jantar Mantar on Sunday. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) have been in force in the area since July. -A Citizens' March, led by the All India Students' Association (AISA), began at 4pm, followed by a march by the Indian Youth Congress, led by national president Uday Bhanu Chib, along the same route at 5pm. -Around the same time, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and, separately, a group of independent journalists also staged protest marches to India Gate against the CEC. -While the marches began peacefully, tensions escalated as protesters approached Jantar Mantar. Police stopped them at several points, including Ashoka Road at the roundabout near Andhra Bhawan, and later near the Le Méridien and Shangri-La hotels. -Police detained dozens of people, including AISA national president Neha Bora. Bora was picked up in a car, which deputy commissioner of police (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma shared was a "government vehicle with two female staff in the back".

Meanwhile, CJP news LIVE: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a cryptic X post on Monday saying the local DCP of his hometown has “suddenly gone on leave” and a “new DCP” has come.

Notably, “The local DCP of my hometown has suddenly gone on leave, and a new DCP has been brought in to take charge,” he shared on X amid claims by CJP leadership of being informed by sources that the government is planning to arrest them before October 10.

As per the latest buzz, Delhi protests LIVE: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke shared on Monday that the chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar is “more valuable to this regime than the citizens of this country.”

In further updates, “Gyanu is more valuable to this regime than the citizens of this country. Because to stay in power, they don't need you or your vote. They just need Gyanu. And that is exactly why Gyanu must go!" Dipke shared on X.

On top of that, His statement came in response to CJP spokespersons' claim that the government is planning to arrest the three - Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - before the October 10 protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t. We are prepared to face whatever comes our way and, if necessary, spend months or years in jail, but we will not back off from our fight to save democracy,” Dipke shared on X.

title: BJP threatens agitation over Form 7 cases across K’taka
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The BJP on Sunday threatened a statewide agitation if police take legal action against its workers over bulk filing of Form 7 applications during Karnataka’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, escalating the political fight over alleged attempts to delete voters.

Adding to this, Former chief minister and senior BJP leader B S Yediyurappa issued the warning (PTI) Former chief minister and senior BJP leader B S Yediyurappa issued the warning after a party delegation led by him met Director General and Inspector General of Police M A Saleem and sought protection for workers facing police cases. The delegation included state BJP president B Y Vijayendra, Leader of Opposition R Ashoka, Council Opposition leader Chalavadi Narayanaswamy, MPs, MLAs and MLCs.
Meanwhile, He alleged that the police were acting at the behest of Chief Minister DK Shivakumar and shared officers should act according to law rather than work to please the government.

Notably, The BJP’s intervention came as police registered another case linked to the Form 7 row in Bengaluru. The Vyalikaval police have registered an FIR following a complaint by Congress leader Anoop Iyengar over 778 applications seeking deletion of voters in the Malleswaram Assembly constituency.

As per the latest buzz, G S Vasanthalakshmi, identified in the FIR as a BJP member, has been named accused No. 1. Another person, described as being associated with an RSS wing, has been listed as an unidentified accused. The complaint alleges that the applications sought deletion of voters who had in fact cast their votes, by describing them as having shifted residence or as otherwise ineligible. The 778 applications were spread across eight polling parts.

In further updates, Ashoka defended the submission of Form 7 applications and shared the validity of individual applications should be decided by election authorities. “Submitting Form 7 is not a crime. It is the Election Commission, not the police station, that has to determine the truth and validity of a voter,” he shared.

On top of that, The BJP’s warning follows a direction from Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar to Electoral Registration Officers in all 224 Assembly constituencies to act against applicants who knowingly make false statements or declarations in Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8.

In a circular issued on October 1, Anbukkumar directed EROs to take action under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, after an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

title: Sanjay Dutt clarifies after backlash over his 'can't feel peace in India' remark, says it was taken out of context: ‘Never my intention to hurt’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sanjay Dutt appeared on the star Shekhar Suman -hosted talk show, Shekhar Tonite, on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. The star shared his opinion about the current state of the country, saying that he doesn't feel "peace" in the nation anymore. His comment courted backlash on social media.

Adding to this, Sanjay Dutt has clarified his remark that was made on Shekhar Suman's show. (File Photo/ PTI) What Sanjay Dutt shared On Sunday evening, the star took to his X account to pen a statement and clarified his comments that were made on the show. It read, "I would like to clarify that it was never my intention to hurt, offend, or disrespect the sentiments of any individual, community, or institution.

Meanwhile, My remarks were made in the context of a scripted conversation intended to be light-hearted and humorous. The spirit behind them was similar to the humour and satire seen in films like Munna Bhai, particularly the concept of 'Gandhigiri,' which was intended to convey a message of love, warmth, togetherness, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted outside of that intended context."

Notably, Sanjay had made the comments with his trademark humour, taking a cue from his character from Munna Bhai MBBS. He spoke about the state of the country and explained why he no longer feels the same sense of peace in India as he once did. He shared, “The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I can’t feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people, and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shivji that those days come back soon.”

As per the latest buzz, Sanjay Dutt holds a 10-year UAE Golden Visa, and his family -- wife Maanayata Dutt and twins Shahraan and Iqra -- lives in Dubai. He commutes between Mumbai and Dubai for work. In another segment of the show, Sanjay was asked to imagine himself as the Prime Minister for five minutes and say something to the people of the country. title: Hanuman Ansh director makes humble request as Kainchi Dham sees massive influx of devotees: ‘Waha ki paristithi pata karke hi jana chahiye’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Hanuman Ansh has become a nationwide sensation. The impact of the biopic drama on the life and legacy of Neem Karoli Baba is such that now it has directly impacted the livelihood of people. Videos on social media over the last few days have claimed that thousands of devotees have arrived at Kainchi Dham to pay a visit after watching the movie. Kainchi Dham is a famous spiritual ashram and Hanuman temple in Uttarakhand, known worldwide for its association with the mystic saint Neem Karoli Baba.

Adding to this, Hanuman Ansh has led to a large influx of tourists at Kainchi Dham. What Hanuman Ansh director shared On Sunday evening, Hanuman Ansh director Dr Vishal Chaturvedi took note of the overcrowding at Kainchi Dham after the rollout of his movie. He made a video on Instagram to share a request with people. He shared, “Kainchi Dham mein bohot bheed hui hai iss waqt aur bohot saare logon ka ye kehna hai ki waha Hanuman Ansh movie dekhne ke baad log waha pohonch gaye hai. Yadi aisa hai toh bhi aur yadi aisa nahi hai toh bhi humein sabhi ko waha ki paristithi pata karke hi waha pe jaana chahiye (Kainchi Dham is overcrowded and people have shared that this is because of the influence of Hanuman Ansh. If that is the case, and if that is not the case, even then, people should visit there only after knowing the present condition).”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dr Vishal Chaturvedi (@filmervishal)

Notably, He went on to add that there are many other shrines to visit too, which can be considered by the devotees. Giving example of Neem Karoli village and Vrindavan, Vishal shared that these places are also important if one is unable to get to Kainchi Dham. “Aap sabhi se anurodh hai ki aise samay main yadi kainchi dham mein bohot bheed hai aur ghanto ki line lagi hai toh ap in sthaano pe bhi ja sakte hai… Mera aapse anurodh hai ki aisi sthiti na ho paaye aap ke ghar mein bachche, mahilayein jo hai woh waha pe suffocate ho rahi hai, woh jam mein phasi hui hai (It is a humble request that during this time if there is overcrowding there then visit other places. Don't be part of a situation where the women and the children feel suffocated and get stuck in traffic jam),” he added.

As per the latest buzz, The rush began ahead of the long weekend, with a government holiday on October 2, followed by Saturday and Sunday, giving travellers three consecutive days off. Mussoorie witnessed a major influx of tourists on Friday, leading to long queues of vehicles along the Mussoorie-Dehradun Road.

In further updates, Thousands of vehicles arrived from Delhi-NCR, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, HT reported earlier. Nainital's Kainchi Dham, the shrine of Baba Neem Karoli, also witnessed a large influx of tourists. The rush was driven by the long weekend and the recent rollout of the movie Hanuman Ansh, visuals shared on social media showed.

title: When Bhagyashree revealed how she made sure that her shaadi ki mehendi did not fade for one year after marriage: ‘Toothpick se khud hi laga deti’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Bhagyashree and Himalay Dassani have been married for more than thirty years. In a chat with Hauterrfly from earlier this year in January, Bhagyashree opened up about her marriage and how she had one wish- to keep her mehendi intact. The star then went on to share how she made sure that her shaadi ki mehendi did not fade away, keeping it on her palms even after one year of marriage!

Adding to this, Bhagyashree opened up about her marriage and the desire to keep her mehendi. (Photo:Rajesh Kumar/HT) What Bhagyashree shared During the chat, Bhagyashree shared, “Regarding the wedding, I wasn't as attached to the wedding outfit as I was to having mehendi on my hands. That was the only thing that I told my mother-in-law, ‘Buy the wedding saree as you wish, but I just want mehendi on my hands…’ In fact, for a whole year, I didn't let the mehendi fade.”

Meanwhile, “Woh kam ho jaati toh vaapas main bulaake lagwa leti. Jab mehendi waali nahi thi tab mehendi ki katori leke baith jaati aur toothpick se khud hi mehendi laga deti (If it started to come off, the person would be called. When they were not available, I would sit with the bowl and apply it using a toothpick)!” she added with a smile.

Notably, Maine Pyaar Kiya star had also opened up that her husband never really proposed to her. In a surprise move last year, Himalay went down on his knees and popped the question. The star took to her social media and shared about the romantic proposal. She wrote, "Secret let out...No matter what everyone feels about Himalayji being a romantic husband.. he wasn't so earlier and I kept telling him that he never really had proposed to me. So here I was, midst of a photoshoot & to my surprise he just interrupted us with this song. (Diljit would have cried to hear this version tho). But yay ! Hubby decided to finally to go on his knees. Sharing some candid pics that my photographer @prashantsamtani clicked." She used the song Kabhi Usey Noor Noor Kehta Hoon with the pictures.

As per the latest buzz, Star Bhagyashree married Himalay Dassani right after her debut movie Maine Pyar Kiya became a massive hit in 1989. The couple have two children, a son and a daughter. Their son Abhimanyu Dassani made his Bollywood debut in 2019 with Mard Ko Dard Nahi Hota and won the Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut for his performance. Their daughter, Avantika Dassani, debuted with the web series Mithya in 2022. The psychological series also starred Huma Qureshi, Parambrata Chatterjee, Rajit Kapur and Samir Soni in pivotal roles.

title: This Bollywood icon cancelled her grand wedding to billionaire, uninvited 2,000 guests, only to marry him at home
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Despite being one of the biggest actors of the 1990s, Juhi Chawla has largely kept her personal life away from the limelight. While followers have always been curious about her marriage to billionaire industrialist and Mehta Group chairman Jay Mehta , the star has rarely spoken about her relationship or married life. However, on a few occasions, Juhi has opened up about her wedding and shared some interesting anecdotes about her life with Jay.

Adding to this, Juhi Chawla and Jay Mehta tied the knot in 1995. When Juhi Chawla doubted her marriage would end her career As per reports, Juhi and Jay were introduced by filmmaker Rakesh Roshan, and they eventually fell in love and tied the knot. In 2024, at an event hosted by the Gujarat Chamber of Commerce & Industry, Juhi had opened up about her wedding and opened up that she was initially supposed to have a grand ceremony with around 2,000 guests. However, having lost her mother a year earlier, the star admitted that she was going through emotional turmoil and wanted to cancel the big-fat wedding.

Meanwhile, During the interaction, Juhi also admitted that she was worried that getting married would mark the end of her career. Amid all these emotions, the idea of a big wedding became overwhelming for her. She shared, “I was shooting for some of the really big films of my career, and I was supposed to get married. My mother had just passed a year ago. When the marriage date was coming close, I was thinking my mother is gone, whom I loved the most, and now my career will also go away. I didn’t know how to be happy about it. So, I broke down one day, and I told my mother-in-law.”
Notably, As per a report in the Times Of India, The Mehta Group business empire that he chairs is valued at over ₹ 17,500 crore rupees ($2.1 billion).

As per the latest buzz, While it may have been difficult for many families to accept, Jay Mehta’s mother and Juhi’s mother-in-law prioritised her emotions over the elaborate wedding plans. Juhi shared that despite invitations having been sent out to around 2,000 guests, the wedding was called off in its original form and the couple instead got married at home in a quiet ceremony attended only by family and close friends.

In further updates, Sharing the same, she shared, “My mother-in-law shared, ‘It’s okay.’ Can you imagine your mother-in-law doing it for you? Invitations had gone out to maybe 2000 people. She shared, 'Abhi nahi horahi hai (It's not happening now)'. She convinced the family to not have the big wedding, and I got married, but it was at home with just the family and closest friends. So with just 80-90-100 people, the wedding was done. Imagine your mother-in-law cancelling those invitations which had gone out all over the world.”
On top of that, The couple got married in 1995. They became parents to two children, daughter Jhanvi and son Arjun.
Jay Mehta is a romantic at heart and Juhi once spoke about his grand romantic gestures during their courtship that proved the same.

title: When Aishwarya Rai reacted to her and Abhishek Bachchan being compared to Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie: ‘Turn this around’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood A-list couple Aishwarya Rai and Abhishek Bachchan have been married for almost two decades and remain one of the most iconic couples in the Hindi movie industry. Of late, a clip from Aishwarya’s old BBC interview from 2010, just three years after her marriage to Abhishek, has been doing the rounds on social media. In the interview, the couple was referred to as the ‘Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie of India’. However, it was Aishwarya’s witty response that has her followers in awe.

Adding to this, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and Abhishek Bachchan have been married for 19 years. When Aishwarya reacted to being called Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie of India During the interaction, Aishwarya and Abhishek were called the ‘Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie of India’. Aishwarya, in her trademark charm and confidence, turned the comparison around and shared, “What if we turn this around and call them Aishwarya and Abhishek of America.”

Meanwhile, During the same interview, Aishwarya also spoke about living with her in-laws, Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan, after her marriage to Abhishek. Explaining to the English journalist why living with family is considered a normal part of Indian culture, she shared, "Before marriage, I was asked whether I live with my parents and people for some reason would be so intrigued and fascinated by this whole idea, which to us as Indians is normal. We live with our families. We are very family-oriented culture. I have lived with my parents right up to the point I got married. And as Indians mostly when a girl does get married, she goes and stays with her husband, who also stays with his family, largely. I mean, I’m not saying that in the urban culture, people are not living independently of their parents, but, largely, as a culture, this is the set up."

Notably, Aishwarya and Abhishek’s love story began with friendship. The two first worked together in Dhai Akshar Prem Ke in 2000 and later reunited for Kuch Naa Kaho. Their friendship grew over the years before they eventually started dating.

As per the latest buzz, The two grew closer while working together on Umrao Jaan in 2006, and their relationship as per reports blossomed further during the making of Mani Ratnam’s Guru. After the movie’s premiere in New York, Abhishek proposed to Aishwarya on the balcony of his hotel.

In further updates, Aishwarya shared yes, and the couple got married on April 20, 2007, in a private ceremony at the Bachchan family home in Mumbai. They welcomed their daughter, Aaradhya, in November 2011.

On top of that, Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows. A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today. At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through movie reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, star interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing. Now, as Assistant Editor at Hindustan Times Entertainment, Vibha continues to chronicle the world of movies and pop culture. Her work spans breaking entertainment news, exclusive interviews, star features, and stories that capture the conversations shaping Indian cinema. Read More
